Newest entries on top. Append only. Never edit or delete past entries. If a previous entry was wrong, write a new correction entry that references it.

By: Claude Code

Changed: five commits (06b714f Part A, 3a10cae engine/intake C-F, f32482e migration + SCHEMA.md + manifest, 6843b43 settings UI + housekeeping, plus this entry). Migration `2026-08-12_prompt73_instant_touch_drips.sql` APPLIED LIVE to zdfpzmmrgotynrwkeakd via MCP and verified by re-query. Deploy confirmed live (whats-new.json marker). npm test green: 902 checks including the two reshaped/new suites (appt-notes 16 checks, instant-touch 74 checks).

**The migration, verified live.** Lead campaign e646981a renumbered to exactly 9 steps at day offsets 0,1,2,4,7,11,16,22,30, max_touches 9. **Active enrollments at renumber time: 0, so nothing was bumped** (the DO block re-checked inside the transaction and would have shifted next_step_index for any nonzero count; it also refuses to double-shift on a re-run). pec_drip_steps gained fixed_template / fixed_subject / auto_send (all existing steps null/false, byte-identical behavior) and ai_guidance went NULLABLE (SCHEMA.md had it NOT NULL and live agreed; the day-0 step needed null). Surprise finding: `_migration-manifest.json` had not been regenerated since 2026-08-03; this build's regen picked up review_drip through prompt 72 as well (154 files, 316 artifacts).

**The day-0 template as shipped (pec_drip_steps step 0, fixed_template; subject "Thanks for reaching out to Prescott Epoxy Company"):**

> Hi {first_name}, thanks for reaching out to Prescott Epoxy Company. We got your request and someone from our team will call you shortly.{{#booking_link}} If it is easier, you can pick a time for your free on site estimate right here: {booking_link}{{/booking_link}}

HOW the conditional works: the {{#booking_link}} block survives only when routemize_booking_url is non-empty, so an empty setting drops the whole sentence and can never ship a dangling "right here:". {first_name} falls back to "there". The email footer (dripEmailHtml) already carries the company line and opt-out; the SMS leg appends the STOP line like every drip SMS. Editable via SQL on the step row today; wording changes need no deploy.

**How the instant touch works (sendInstantTouch, _pec-drip.cjs).** Fires INLINE in pec-lead-intake immediately after enrollLead, same request, never on the runner (the runner's new auto_send branch is only the crash safety net, and the fixture test proves it sends with zero model calls when it does fire). Preconditions in order, each with a logged reason: drip_instant_touch_enabled, drip_sending_enabled, kill switch, enrolled-on-a-live-lead-campaign with step 0 auto_send+fixed_template, lead not archived / not opted out, no prior step-0 ledger row (Zapier-retry guard). It bypasses ONLY the approval gate and quiet hours; consent still rules the SMS leg (a skipped row with reason no_sms_consent is the expected shape while the web form sends no consent). ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION from the prompt's sketch: the prompt said send-then-advance; I built CLAIM-FIRST (the conditional next_step_index 0->1 PATCH is the atomic claim, then send). WHY: step 0 has day_offset 0, so the enrollment is due the moment it exists and a 15-minute runner tick can race the inline call; claim-first makes a double-text impossible, which is the tradeoff the whole engine already made (never-double-text beats never-lose-a-touch). auto_send is PER-STEP (landmine 2) and the runner's pending-hold branch still outranks it (landmine 3). Steps 1-8 keep the approval gate exactly as before; the non-leak regression is tested explicitly (step 0 auto-sends, then step 1 lands pending in the same fixture).

**Booking link ({booking_link}).** One settings key routemize_booking_url, editable in Settings > Drips. Day-0: template conditional. AI steps 1-8: the URL rides the render prompt with an include-exactly rule, renderCopyReal REJECTS any rendered routemize.com URL that is not character-identical to the configured one (or any routemize URL when none is configured), scrubCopyKeepUrl lets exactly the configured URL through the link-stripping scrubber, and a capped SMS that would truncate the URL is rejected too. Lead campaign only; estimate/invoice/review keep their code-appended tails.

Nothing to approve, nothing to run today; the script is there for the day the mix changes.

## [2026-08-06 MST] Cowork: prompt 73 scoped (reminder-note routing, lead drip coverage, day-0 instant touch). The UUID bug Dylan reported was already fixed; the real finding is that 6 of 15 leads never enrolled and four gates block "immediately".

By: Cowork

Changed: one new file, `claude-code-prompt-73-instant-touch-drips.md`, plus this entry. No code, no schema, no data, no migration, nothing deployed. Read-only queries against prod (zdfpzmmrgotynrwkeakd) via the Supabase MCP.

Why: Dylan brought two things. (1) "email is showing these codes as of 8/3, remove the codes", with a pasted appointment reminder carrying two raw UUIDs. (2) "drip campaigns for all leads, to follow up immediately after lead comes through if its an online lead." Mid-scoping he added a third: the ability to put the Routemize booking link in drip messages, including the instant touch.

**Request 1 is already closed and the prompt says so in its section 0.** Prompt 65 Part A shipped the intake-side UUID strip on 2026-08-03 and Dylan approved the Part A3 backfill the same day. Re-queried all 8 appointments carrying customer notes on 2026-08-06: ZERO UUIDs remain. The message Dylan pasted went out 2026-08-02, before the fix. He is checking whether anything code-bearing arrived after 8/3; if it did, the prompt routes Claude Code to the Routemize UPDATE branch and the other senders before doing anything else.

**What survived that fix, and is the actual Part A.** Stripping the UUID made the reminder less alarming, not correct. `_pec-appt.cjs:143` appends `customer_notes` to every customer-facing appointment message on both channels, and Routemize fills that field with a dump of the customer's own intake answers, INCLUDING the service-picker value. Brent Boyer's reminder ended with a dangling "Grind and Seal"; Lynette Williams' note ends in the bare word "Other", so her reminder read, in full, "Other." Dylan's call: keep the free-text project description, drop the picker answer, send the picker to internal notes for the rep.

**The mechanism that makes Part A precise instead of heuristic.** The raw envelopes in `pec_webhook_ingest_log` (endpoint `appt-intake`) show `customerAnswers[]` carries a stable `questionId` identical to the UUID-valued `question` field, and there are exactly two questions in play: `605f816a-b861-c865-3e12-3a2177755a80` is the free-text description and `1077d4b4-4c1d-1f34-52a1-3a2177807ce1` is the service picker. **Order is not stable** (Rob Rudman's envelope has the picker first, Brent Boyer's has it second), so position-based routing would have been wrong roughly half the time. The prompt specifies a settings-driven `routemize_answer_routing` map of questionId to customer/internal/drop, defaulting an unmapped question to `customer` so new questions never silently lose content the customer typed. Rule 12: a new Routemize question is a settings edit.

**Request 2, the finding that reframed it: 6 of 15 leads have never been enrolled in anything.** `enrollLead` is called from exactly three places (pec-lead-intake.cjs:191 and index.html:26986 / :27657). `pec-appt-intake.cjs` never enrolls, which features.json documents as deliberate. Every unenrolled lead except three arrived from Routemize already holding a booked estimate. Dylan's decision: those stay out, because a "still interested?" taper aimed at someone with Tuesday 2pm on the calendar reads as broken; the re-engagement trigger is appointment CANCELED or no-showed. Three leads (Jay McCoy, Larry Bowles, Cowork Smoke Test) came in outside Routemize and still never enrolled, which the prompt makes Claude Code investigate rather than assume, since it determines whether "all leads enroll" is actually true going forward.

**The four gates between a new lead and an instant text, all of them things Dylan had already turned on.** `drip_approval_required` = true (every step is a draft awaiting a human click). `sms_consent` false on 14 of 15 leads while step 0 is channel `both` (the SMS leg is unsendable for essentially every real lead). Quiet hours 08:00-20:00 Mon-Sat (a Sunday evening lead waits until Monday morning). Runner ticks every 15 minutes, so nothing fires inline at intake.

**The contradiction, and Dylan's reversal, which is the decision the whole build turns on.** Asked about the approval gate, Dylan first answered "keep approval on everywhere". That is incompatible with the thing he asked for: with the gate on, the day-0 message is a draft in a queue and "immediately" means "whenever someone opens the queue", and the quiet-hours answer he gave in the same batch has no effect at all. Naming the conflict flipped him: **the day-0 touch auto-sends, steps 1 through 8 keep the gate exactly as today.** The risk is bounded because day 0 is a FIXED template with no AI, read once by Dylan before it can ever go out. The prompt makes `auto_send` a per-step column, never a global setting, and landmine 2 says why.

**Dylan's other locked decisions:** "online lead" means webhook-created rather than a per-source flag (coherent, because the Routemize webhook path is excluded by the appointment rule anyway, leaving the web-form intake); new day-0 step with the existing 8 shifting to days 1-30 and max_touches 8 to 9; the instant touch ignores quiet hours because it is a reply to a message the person just sent; a Slack ping to a NEW leads channel (`SLACK_LEADS_WEBHOOK`, falling back to `SLACK_OFFICE_WEBHOOK`) plus an in-app notification; one `routemize_booking_url` settings key with a `{booking_link}` token carried by the day-0 touch AND all eight nurture steps; and auto-enroll of still-open non-appointment backlog leads, which Cowork accepted only with an exclusion filter, since a naive read of that instruction currently catches two test rows and a smoke test.

**Three constraints written into the prompt so the build does not trip on them.** (1) The step renumber is the highest-risk change here: `pec_drip_enrollments.next_step_index` points at the old numbering, and it is safe today ONLY because all 6 lead enrollments are currently `stopped` and zero are active. The prompt requires re-verifying that count inside the migration transaction and bumping any active rows in the same transaction. (2) `_pec-drip.cjs` section 4.5 has a `pending_held` branch that fires regardless of the gate setting, by design, so flipping the gate off can never auto-send an item a human was mid-review on; the new `auto_send` branch must not defeat it. (3) An AI step that hallucinates a `routemize.com` URL sends a customer to a 404 with PEC's name on it, so the prompt adds a validation rejecting any lead-campaign message containing a routemize.com URL that is not character-identical to the configured one.

**Called out as NOT fixable from this repo:** `sms_consent` is false almost everywhere because the web form does not capture or pass it. The code side is small (accept the truthy spellings Zapier actually sends, store the disclosure text, surface a 30-day consent-rate readout in Settings). The real fix is a consent checkbox with TCPA-style disclosure on the website plus a Zap field mapping, which is a Dylan handoff, not a build task.

## [2026-08-05 MST] Prompt 72 shipped: optional line items on any line, opt-out selection, declined-line record and one-click add-back

By: Claude Code

Changed: one migration (2026-08-11_prompt72_optional_lines.sql, applied via MCP, verified by information_schema re-query), seven code commits pushed and deployed (22a244d, 9bcf468, f1934d7, d09d6a7, 81e478a, 336cd85, plus this docs commit). npm test: **828 checks, 0 failed, exit 0** (783 baseline from prompt 70 + 45 new in production/optional-lines.test.js). Every locked decision implemented as written; deviations called out below.

**The shape.** `estimate_areas.is_optional`/`preselected` are the rep's source of truth (the estimator reloads areas by position, exactly the constraint Cowork wrote into the prompt) and mirror onto `estimate_line_items` at save, so every downstream reader kept its existing columns. Shared rules live in new `production/optional-lines.cjs` (the scope.cjs pattern): the three totals (required-only / all-in / opening), the send gate, the accept guard, the declined-area filter with its keep-unmatched guardrail, the crew declined note, and the selected-lines scope doc; the estimator bundles it, pec-public-estimate.cjs requires it, and the 45 fixture checks drive it plus the REAL accept handler through the estimate15b in-memory PostgREST harness.

**Stored money (decision 7), stated precisely because it moved.** While an estimate is OPEN, `estimates.price` is the REQUIRED-ONLY floor and every stored money bucket (gp_dollars/gp_pct/gp_per_hour/labor_budget/commission_dollars/budgeted_hours) is computed over that same required set so each number qualifies the number it sits next to; `price_all_options` is the ceiling. On an estimate with nothing optional the sets are identical and every stored value lands exactly where it always has (tested). Accept still overwrites price with the signed total and leaves price_all_options as the record of what was offered. The estimator's HEADLINE is the customer's OPENING total (required + pre-selected), which is also what the send email now quotes (estimateOpeningTotal, computed live from the rows) so the email and the page can never disagree. Pipeline, estimate list, and the detail header render "up to $Y" only while open and only when the two differ.

**The kit-merge tradeoff (decision 5), which is a MATERIAL change and not a price change.** On accept the job is built from the SELECTED areas only: job_areas, pec_prod_areas (the recipe side that drives the material plan, ordering, and the costing rollup), jobs.sqft, jobs.scope, and pec_prod_jobs.notes. Prices are honored exactly as signed. The named test proves the point the prompt demanded nobody optimize away: two 200-sqft bays share ONE basecoat kit when offered together, and after a decline the remaining bay's plan still buys the FULL kit alone, all on the sold bay's cost basis. The rep-side defense is the required-only GP readout plus the amber warning (verified live at 37.9% vs the 40% floor, exact spec wording), warn not block.

**E3 verified before deciding, as instructed:** the only readers of estimates.gp_* after acceptance are the estimate LIST's GP% column and the detail page's "Pricing logic" panel, both displays of the as-quoted economics; post-accept GP reporting reads the job and the costing rollup (prompt 66's canonical formula). So the stored gp columns are left as signed, no browser-layer recompute, no calculator.cjs was created.

**Live verification (prescottepoxy.netlify.app, signed in, DB re-queries; baseline counts captured first per the BusyBusy-entry template).** Built EST-102070: required Garage (Standard Flake 800) + pre-selected optional Patio (Quartz 400) + unselected optional Stem Walls add-on ($500). Estimator showed headline $6,850 (opening), All-in $7,350, Required only $3,995 · GP 51.4%, and the amber warning fired correctly when a test discount pushed required-only to 37.9%. Public page: Garage rendered with NO control, Patio ticked under Your project with an Optional tag, Stem Walls unticked under Options to add; unticking the Patio dropped the total $6,850 -> $3,995, exactly its price. Signed with the Patio unticked: price patched to 3,995 (the ticked-lines sum to the cent), price_all_options untouched at 7,350, the Patio row is the declined record, the signature jsonb lists the (empty) ticked ids. Job side re-queried: job_areas and pec_prod_areas contain the Garage and NOT the Patio, jobs.sqft = 800, and pec_prod_jobs.notes carries the selected scope plus "Declined by customer: Patio: Quartz, $2,855; Stem Walls, $500". Estimate detail rendered both declined lines struck through with Declined tags, read-only, excluded from the $3,995 total. The job's Declined options card listed both lines with quoted dates; Add to job opened the change-order modal prefilled Patio / Quartz / 400 / $2,855 with "Quoted 2026-08-05 at $2,855" and saving landed a normal job_areas change-order row at the quoted price (job price 3,995 -> 6,850, CO signature minted). The customer card shows both "Declined on EST-102070" lines. Zero residue: every row deleted and re-queried; all fourteen tracked table counts match the pre-test baseline exactly (estimates 13, estimate_areas 14, estimate_line_items 20, jobs 96, job_areas 145, pec_prod_jobs 95, pec_prod_areas 64, customers 94, timeline_stages 476, installments 3, views 6, busybusy 27, notifications 50, CO signatures 10).

**BusyBusy handling for the test accept:** `busybusy_autocreate_enabled` was flipped to 'false' for the one test acceptance and restored to 'true' immediately after (re-queried both ways), so NO BusyBusy project was created at all, zero cloud residue, and nothing needed archiving; the loop itself was already proven live end-to-end by Cowork's 2026-08-04 E2E2 run. This seemed strictly better than creating and archiving a real project, given this session's Zapier surface could not drive the busybusy connector on 2026-08-04.

**Deviations and judgment calls, called out:** (1) The send-email number parity was verified structurally, not by sending: the deployed send flow quotes estimateOpeningTotal computed from the same rows the page renders (grep-verified in the deployed bundle) and the arithmetic was proven against the live estimate; no real email went to the fake test address. (2) A declined CUSTOM line's Add to job prefills SIMPLE mode (title + amount + detail), not AREA mode, because area mode requires a system and sqft a custom line never had; area declines prefill AREA mode per decision 12. (3) jobs.scope follows the same selected-only composition as pec_prod_jobs.notes when something was declined (decision 10 says the JOB side strips; the spec named notes explicitly, jobs.scope feeds the same crew surfaces). (4) One existing check updated, not weakened: estimate15b's preview-parity normalization learned the renamed read-only option-card copy ("These items were offered and not selected."), both vintages normalize to the same token. (5) The whole-estimate custom line (build 24) stays hardcoded required: it is the estimate's ONLY line and decision 1 forbids sending an all-optional estimate.

## [2026-08-05 09:40] Cowork: prompt 72 scoped (optional line items on any line). The flag already exists; only the estimator's hardcoded false was stopping it.

By: Cowork

Changed: No code, no schema. Wrote claude-code-prompt-72-optional-line-items.md after 12 scoping questions with Dylan and a read of the estimator, the public estimate function, and SCHEMA.md.

Why: Dylan's ask was "need to be able to make all line items optional when building an estimate."

**The finding that shrank the build.** Optional lines are not missing, they are half-wired. `estimate_line_items.is_optional` and `.selected_by_customer` have existed since 2026-07-13, `includedTotal` / `freezeLineItems` / `applySelection` in pec-public-estimate.cjs already do the whole selection-and-freeze dance, and the public page already renders tickable cards that re-total live. The only thing blocking area and custom lines is three literal `isOptional: false` values in EstimatorScreen.tsx (:1759 whole-estimate custom, :1782 custom line, :1821 area line); the add-on loop right below them reads a real flag. So Part B is mostly replacing hardcodes with a checkbox, and the interesting work is downstream.

**The real trap, and Dylan's call on it.** Since prompt 69 the per-line solve merges ONE kit-merged material plan across all areas (two bays each needing 0.44 of a basecoat kit buy one kit between them). A customer dropping a line keeps that shared-kit discount in the remaining lines' prices while the job now has to buy the full kit alone, so GP silently lands under what the estimate showed. Dylan's decision: **do not touch pricing, fix the material estimate.** The customer's total stays the plain sum of ticked lines and the rep's prices are honored exactly; at accept, the job is built from the SELECTED areas only, so pec_prod_areas (the recipe side that drives the material plan and the costing rollup) is computed on what was actually sold. The rep-facing defense is a required-only GP readout plus an amber warning when that number falls under the line-pricing floor, warn not block. Worth flagging for the next reader: "re-cost at accept" here means the material plan, NOT the price.

**Dylan's other locked decisions:** any line can be optional, but an estimate cannot be SENT with zero required lines (that rep-side gate is what makes the customer floor automatic, since required lines are not tickable); rep decides per line, default required; optional AREA and CUSTOM lines start TICKED (opt-out) while add-ons keep today's unticked opt-in behavior; two stored numbers, `estimates.price` = required only for forecasting and a new `price_all_options` = the ceiling, pipeline reads "$8,200 (up to $12,400)"; selected lines only flow to the job with declined lines kept on the estimate as the record; `estimates.scope_of_work` is never rewritten after signature, the JOB side strips declined scope; declined lines are logged with no automation; and a declined line gets a one-click "Add to job" that opens the existing change-order modal in AREA mode at the originally quoted price.

**Two constraints written into the prompt so the build does not trip on them.** (1) The estimator reloads areas by position and never selects area ids (estimateLoad.ts:130), so the rep's optional flag has to live on `estimate_areas.is_optional` and be mirrored onto the line item, not inferred by joining line items back to areas. (2) `production/calculator.js` is ESM and no .cjs function requires it today, so the accept path must NOT grow a third copy of the calculator to re-cost; the prompt instructs Claude Code to first check whether anything actually reads `estimates.gp_*` after acceptance, and to do any recompute in the browser layer if so.

The email body is a sandboxed 480px iframe, which consumes the wheel event where the pointer naturally sits, so the bottom Close never scrolls into view; separately, openModal's backdrop-click guard disables click-outside whenever the modal contains an iframe (by design, for the estimator), and Escape is off because the modal is not opened with `dismissible: true`. Three independent reasons it feels stuck. Prompt 71 Part E adds a sticky `.pec-modal-xhead` close header to openModal and to all seven hand-rolled #prodModalRoot sites, keeps Escape scoped to dismissible modals (a global Escape would silently wipe a half-typed change order, which prompt 63 Part D already litigated), and passes `dismissible: true` for the read-only email log modal.

## [2026-08-04 MST] Prompt 70 shipped: comps hard-filtered on system type, one AI call returning a recommendation per line with server-computed confidence, custom lines read from typed scope

By: Claude Code

Changed: one data-only migration (2026-08-10_prompt70_pricing_intelligence.sql, applied via MCP, verified by re-query: estimate_ai_enabled 'true' + comps_min_sample '3', settings 76 to 78), four code commits pushed and deployed (6659954, 146fc24, daf832c, plus this docs commit). npm test: **783 checks, 0 failed, exit 0** (726 baseline from prompt 69 + 39 new in production/ai-lines.test.cjs + 18 new per-line server sections in estimate15b.test.js).

**Provenance note, stated plainly: no prompt-70 spec file was ever written.** Cowork's 2026-08-04 entry queued it; Dylan said "run prompt 70". The build follows the SCOPE THE PROMPT-69 SPEC LOCKED in its "Explicitly out of scope" section, verbatim: (1) system type becomes a hard filter in buildComps; (2) the AI moves from one job-level recommendation to one call returning a recommendation per line plus a short job-level roll-up; (3) each line gets a range, a why, and a server-computed confidence flag (comps-backed / thin sample / no comps), never model-claimed; (4) custom lines reason from the typed scope with an explicit no-comparables statement. Both prompt-69 seams were used as reserved: pricing_snapshot keeps its estimate-level shape with ai.lines[].line_key as the per-line keying, and the per-line inputs stayed cheaply hashable.

**The comps hard filter (the actual fix for "AI prices off square footage").** buildComps' widen ladder is now exact -> same-system any-size -> STOP. The old ladder dropped the system filter under 3 same-system jobs, so most estimates blended $/sqft across systems; zero same-system jobs now honestly returns ZERO comps with a label naming the system, because a quartz price built from polyaspartic comps is worse than no comp at all. The old similar_size/any rules are unreachable but stay renderable for pre-70 stored snapshots. The one prior buildComps caller outside the estimator is the estimate detail page, which renders the STORED snapshot and needed nothing.

**The per-line AI.** New production/ai-lines.cjs (CJS, the scope.cjs pattern: required by pec-estimate-ai.cjs, bundled by Vite, driven by fixture tests): per-line prompt building, response validation (a model that omits a line is a hard 500 naming the line, never a partial render), the inputs key (calc lines key on system+sqft+mvb; custom lines on typed price + a scope hash, joined in order), and finalizeLinesRecommendation, which stamps the confidence flag per line FROM THE COMPS SAMPLE (overwriting anything the model claimed, proven by a test where the model claims comps_backed on a custom line), prepends the no-comparables statement to a custom line's why when the model forgot it, and derives the roll-up range as the SUM of the line ranges so the totals can never drift from the lines. The estimator sends each calc line ITS OWN hard-filtered comps (its system, its sqft); custom lines send comps null by definition. The row cache is unchanged in mechanism: matching pricing_snapshot.inputs_key still serves the stored read with zero model calls (tested server-side AND proven live: reopening the test estimate made 0 requests to pec-estimate-ai). One consequence: pre-70 estimates carry old-format keys, so their FIRST reopen re-reads once, then caches under the new key.

**Settings (rule 12), Settings > Estimates > Pricing intelligence:** estimate_ai_enabled (server-gated AND client-gated; off returns a clean disabled response and the panel says "Turned off in Settings", never an error; tested to make zero model calls) and comps_min_sample (the ONE knob shared by the comps ladder and the confidence boundary, so the panel and the flag cannot disagree about what "thin" means; buildComps gained a minSample param). Legacy single-recommendation request bodies still work (deploy-skew safety, tested), and the dashboard's estimate detail renders BOTH snapshot vintages (per-line chips added under the existing range block).

**Live verification (prescottepoxy.netlify.app, signed in, DB re-queries).** Built EST-102060 (Garage 800 sqft Standard Flake + Patio 400 sqft Quartz + custom Stair install $1,500/$220/6h). ONE model call returned the roll-up ($8,350 to $9,300) plus three per-line reads that landed exactly on the three confidence tiers: Garage COMPS-BACKED against 14 same-system flake comps (its own set, not the estimate-level 8), Patio THIN SAMPLE against exactly 2 quartz jobs with the model naming the any-size widening and the size mismatch, and Stair install NO COMPS reasoning from the typed scope ("this is a custom line, so by definition no comparable jobs exist"). Saved; pricing_snapshot re-queried: inputs_key in the new per-line format (custom line keyed by price + scope hash), ai.lines = 3 with Garage=comps_backed | Patio=thin_sample | Stair install=no_comps, roll-up 8350/9300 = the line sums. Reopen: full panel served from the snapshot with 0 network calls to pec-estimate-ai. Estimate detail page: roll-up, all three chips, and the same-system comps label all render. Zero residue: the test estimate + areas + line items deleted and re-queried to 0; estimate_areas 9 and estimate_line_items 14 match the post-69 baseline exactly. (The concurrently-appearing "ZZ BusyBusy E2E2" rows are Cowork's own queued retest running in parallel, not this session's.)

**One polish committed after the live read:** the roll-up paragraph referred to lines as "L0/L1/L2" (the internal keys); the system prompt now instructs label-only references in rollup_why. Landed with the docs commit; the next fresh read picks it up.

Files touched: production/comps.js, production/ai-lines.cjs (new), production/ai-lines.test.cjs (new), production/estimate15b.test.js, netlify/functions/pec-estimate-ai.cjs, apps/estimator/src (ai.ts, comps.ts wiring untouched, catalog.ts, EstimatorScreen.tsx, types/calculator.d.ts), index.html (Pricing intelligence card + snapAi.lines render), package.json, supabase/migrations/2026-08-10_prompt70_pricing_intelligence.sql (new), SCHEMA.md, features.json (new entry + two amended), help/whats-new.json (1 entry, no em dashes), PROJECT-LOG.md (this entry).

## [2026-08-04 MST] Prompt 69 shipped: per-line pricing, custom lines inside a normal estimate, per-line GP, per-line notes and scope

By: Claude Code

Changed: one migration (2026-08-09_prompt69_per_line_pricing.sql, applied via MCP, verified by information_schema re-query), six code commits pushed and deployed (9298629, 83afd9b, 63809c2, 96a8ecb, 9de6c14, 03e5857), plus this docs commit. npm test: **726 checks, 0 failed, exit 0** (646 baseline from prompt 68 + 80 new in production/per-line-pricing.test.js). CALC_VERSION bumped to 2026-08-04.1 in BOTH copies (production/calculator.js and the index.html mirror).

**The estimate model changed shape.** An estimate_areas row is now the ONE line unit: a calculator area carries its own solved price (`calc_price`) and an optional rep-typed per-line price (`price_override`); a CUSTOM line is an area row with `is_custom=true`, a typed label/scope/material cost/crew hours, and its typed price in `price_override`. Eight nullable/defaulted columns, five `line_pricing_*` settings keys (floor seeded from the live estimator floor, 40). Forward-only, no backfill: pre-69 rows have them all null/false and render unchanged.

**Part B, the solve, and the trap it was built around.** `computePerLinePricing` keeps ONE estimate-wide kit-merged material plan (the ordering truth), attributes M back to areas by each area's PRE-merge raw fractional-kit cost via allocateProportionally (parts sum to M exactly), then solves each area with the same closed form as before but at its OWN system's labor% and target GP%. HOW IT AVOIDS THE DOUBLE-BUY: two 200-sqft bays each needing 0.44 kits of the same basecoat still buy ONE merged kit; the test proves the per-line total ($8,218) lands under the naive solve-each-area-alone sum ($10,062). WHY a mixed estimate's total moves: each system now hits its own target GP instead of a blended average silently letting a high-margin system subsidize a low-margin one. The single-area identity invariant (same price to the cent as computeEstimatePricing) is proven over six fixture variations, and the dashboard's change-order pricer (single-area computeEstimatePricing) is untouched by construction.

**The old-vs-new report over every existing estimate (required before committing the behavior change):**

| Estimate | Areas | Old total | New total | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EST-102038 (Dylan Nordby, draft) | 1 | $5,995 | $5,995 | $0 |
| EST-102033 (Chris Lopez, draft) | 1 | $0 (stored calc_price 0; price 4950 was a rep override) | $0 | $0 |

Those are the only two live estimates with area rows; both single-area, so the identity invariant makes every delta $0 and EST-102038's new number equals its stored calc_price exactly. No multi-area estimate exists yet, and no sent/accepted estimate has area rows, so nothing stored moved anywhere.

**Part C, the estimator.** Every area row shows its solved price, an editable Line price box (writes price_override), and its own GP$/GP% that goes red under `line_pricing_gp_floor_pct`. "+ Add custom line" sits next to "+ Add area": label, scope textarea with its own Polish-with-AI + undo (same pec-estimate-custom-polish endpoint), typed price/material cost/crew hours, optional sqft, and internal notes. The job-level sell/discount operates on the SUM and allocates across the lines by current price (allocateProportionally, so the parts sum to the typed total to the cent). The reason rule tightened WITH the relief valve: a written reason is demanded whenever the final total lands under the CALCULATED total by more than the greater of 2% / $100 (both settings keys), no matter whether the rep got there by line edits, the job discount, or both; the warning states the shortfall and the allowed leeway in dollars. The below-floor save confirmation NAMES the offending lines with their GP% (proven live: "Below the 40% line floor: Garage (9.6%), Patio (24.6%)"). The whole-estimate Custom mode (build 24) is untouched.

**Part B fixed add-ons note (required by the prompt):** the estimator has never passed `fixedAddons` (add-ons are their own line items), so F stays 0 per area; the parameter is still supported and allocates by the same raw-cost weights (tested).

**estimate_line_items.unit_cost now carries the line's REAL cost** (materials + labor + commission + sundries at its final price, i.e. price minus its GP$), instead of materials-only-for-area-lines / 0-for-custom. Verified safe first: zero readers exist anywhere (grep of index.html + all netlify functions; the only prior touch was a write in the add-optional-item modal).

**Parts E-F, scope and accept.** pec-estimate-scope: a custom line's typed scope is used VERBATIM (explicit skip; the writer never rewrites it), and each area's internal notes ride that line's generation context as `internal_notes` with a hard system-prompt rule: substitution facts only, never quoted into customer text, never new scope, never overriding the verbatim-template rule. On accept, every job_areas row now carries its line's final `price` and scope `description`; a custom line becomes a real job_areas row (name = custom_label, no system, typed sqft or null) so the crew sees it, and jobs.line_items carries all three lines for the work order's page 2. pec_prod_areas deliberately SKIPS custom lines (found live, see below).

**One real bug found and fixed during live verification:** the first accept of the mixed test estimate 500'd because `pec_prod_areas.sqft` and `.system_type_id` are NOT NULL and the custom line has neither. Fix (03e5857): custom lines are filtered out of the pec_prod_areas insert; that table is the RECIPE side driving the material plan, which a custom line contributes nothing to by locked decision 6, while the crew-facing scope and price live on job_areas per decision 7. The idempotent heal path then completed the same acceptance cleanly, which is the accept path's crash-recovery design doing its job.

**Live verification (prescottepoxy.netlify.app, signed in, database re-queries for every write).** Built EST-102055 for "ZZ Prompt69 Test": Garage 800 sqft Standard Flake + Patio 400 sqft Quartz + custom "Stair install" ($1,500 typed, $220 material, 6 crew hours), notes on two lines. Engine solved Garage $3,995 + Patio $2,855 (each at its own target: Patio GP exactly 50.0% at calc) = $6,850 + $1,500 custom = $8,350 base. Applied a $7,995 job sell price (reason recorded): line items landed at **3825.15 + 2733.62 + 1436.23 = 7995.00 to the cent** (allocation exactness proven with numbers). Reopen rehydrated every field including notes, custom cost/hours, and the typed scope. Scope generation wrote each calculator line its own template document (Garage 1,999 chars, Patio 1,313 chars from ITS quartz template) and left the custom line's 157-char typed text untouched; the note text never leaked into customer text, and where a note conflicted with an explicit intake fact (coat-past-garage), the intake's answer won, which is the designed precedence. Public page rendered all three lines with their scopes and prices; the presentation view and the PDF are that same page (iframe / window.print). Accept created 1 job, 1 prod job, 1 customer, 7 stages, **3 job_areas rows each carrying its line's price and scope (custom included)**, 2 pec_prod_areas (custom skipped), and the deposit installment. Estimate detail (dashboard) rendered the mixed line items with no regressions. Legacy regression: EST-102030 (whole-custom, SENT) re-saved byte-identical (price 1950, one Custom-scope line, scope untouched; the CUSTOM_LINE_LABEL edit filter still works); EST-102038 re-saved with price/calc/GP identical to the cent (5995 / 5995 / 3117.15 / 52.0%), with only the intended new provenance (calc_version stamp, real unit_cost, area calc_price).

**Zero residue, re-queried:** every ZZ Prompt69 row deleted and confirmed 0 (estimates, areas, line items, jobs, job_areas, prod jobs, prod areas, customer, 7 stages, installment, views, notification, busybusy link row). Table totals after: estimates 11, estimate_areas 9, estimate_line_items 14, jobs 95, job_areas 143, pec_prod_jobs 94, pec_prod_areas 63, customers 91, timeline_stages 469, installments 2, views 3 (each exactly the pre-test count).

The local row is deleted; whether the Zap run actually created BusyBusy project 102055 (or was held by the account's task ceiling Cowork flagged) could not be confirmed from this session, because the Zapier MCP surface here rotated mid-session (list action deprecated) and the busybusy code-action fallback could not drive the connector's find/archive actions. ## [2026-08-04 MST] Cowork: prompt 69 spec written (per-line pricing, custom lines inside a normal estimate, per-line GP, per-line notes and scope)

By: Cowork

Changed: one new file, `claude-code-prompt-69-per-line-pricing-custom-lines.md`, plus this entry. No code, no schema, no data, no migration, nothing deployed. This is a spec handoff to Claude Code, not a build.

**What Dylan asked for**, in his words: AI pricing suggestions based on the specific system and not just square footage; the ability to add a custom system onto an estimate that already has Pricing Estimator areas (his example: a quartz estimate that also needs a custom system on it); the ability to price each line item individually with each line carrying its own scope of work generated from its system type and notes; and AI price suggestions per line item rather than per job total.

**The diagnosis that shaped the split.** "AI prices off square footage, not the system" is not an AI-prompt problem. `buildComps` (production/comps.js:126-160) runs a widen ladder: exact, then same system at any size, then **any system** at similar size, then any completed job. With roughly 35 completed jobs in the 12-month window, most estimates fall past the same-system rung, so the median $/sqft the model reasons over is frequently blended across systems. The model is reporting its comps faithfully; the comps are the problem. Rewriting the system prompt without fixing the ladder would only make it more confidently wrong. That put the comps fix and the AI rebuild together in a second prompt rather than bolted onto this one.

**The build was split into two prompts (Dylan's choice among three options).** Prompt 69, written today, is the data model and pricing half. Prompt 70, not yet written, is the comps hard filter and the per-line AI. Rationale: per-line pricing lands and gets used on a few real estimates before the AI is rebuilt on top of it, and prompt 70's per-line recommendations need per-line prices to exist first.

**Twelve multiple-choice questions were asked before writing anything**, per the project instruction, plus a follow-up round of three once the GP math surfaced a hole. Decisions Dylan locked, all recorded in the prompt so Claude Code does not relitigate them:

1. A custom line is a custom `estimate_areas` row (new nullable columns), not a bare line item and not a new `pec_prod_system_types` record. It reuses the existing area to line-item pipeline, the scope writer, and the public page.
2. Each line solves its own price; the job total is the sum. The proportional back-allocation of a single job price goes away for the calc price.
3. The sell/discount override stays job-level and allocates across lines. `estimates.price_override_reason` stays the audit trail.
4. GP is shown per line AND combined.
5. A custom line takes a typed material cost and typed labor hours, not one blended cost and not price-only. Without a cost it would show 100% GP and drag the combined number up; typed hours also keep gp_per_hour and crew day planning honest.
6. A custom line pulls no catalog products in this build. Typed cost only, nothing into the material plan, so the kit-rounding path is untouched.
7. On accept, a custom line becomes a real `job_areas` row carrying its scope and price, so the crew sees it on the work order.
8. Per-line internal notes are a new field on each area and custom line, feeding that line's scope generation.
9. Scope generation stays ONE action with its never-overwrite rule. No per-line buttons, no auto-regeneration.
10. Forward-only migration, no backfill. Existing estimates keep their stored line amounts.

**The trap the prompt spends the most words on.** The obvious per-line implementation, "call `computeEstimatePricing` once per area and sum", is wrong, and the existing code already knows it: `soloByArea` (EstimatorScreen.tsx:1440) is used only as allocation weights, never as money. Materials kit-round ACROSS areas via `mergeAcrossAreas` (calculator.js:849), so two areas each needing 0.6 of a kit consume one kit, not two; solving each area alone buys two and inflates the total. The prompt specifies keeping one estimate-wide material plan, attributing its cost `M` back to areas by pre-merge raw cost via `allocateProportionally` so the parts sum to `M` exactly, then solving each area at its OWN system's labor% and target GP%. It also requires a hard test invariant: a single-area estimate must price to the identical cent as today.

**A behavior change Claude Code is required to quantify before shipping.** Today a mixed estimate uses a sqft-weighted average target GP, so no individual system hits its own target; a high-margin system silently subsidizes a low-margin one. Per-line solving corrects that, which is the point, but multi-area totals will move. The prompt requires an old-vs-new total report over every existing estimate, in the log entry, before the behavior change is committed, with sent and accepted rows left frozen. That requirement is a direct callback to prompt 56, where a derived-beats-stored rule moved GP on 34 finalized jobs by $4,785 before anyone counted.

**One decision refined after Dylan reviewed the draft.** The prompt originally required a written reason whenever the final total landed under the calculated total by any route, closing the loophole where a rep edits three lines down instead of using the discount box. Dylan agreed but took the relief valve: the reason is now only demanded when the shortfall exceeds the greater of `line_pricing_reason_threshold_pct` (default 2%) or `line_pricing_reason_threshold_dollars` (default $100), measured on the whole estimate rather than per line, so several small trims that add up still ask. Both are settings keys, not rep-editable.

Files touched: `claude-code-prompt-69-per-line-pricing-custom-lines.md` (new), PROJECT-LOG.md (this entry).
Next steps: Dylan runs prompt 69 in Claude Code. After it ships and a few real mixed estimates have been quoted, Cowork writes prompt 70 (comps hard filter on system type, one AI call returning a recommendation per line plus a job roll-up, server-computed confidence flags, custom lines reasoning from typed scope with an explicit no-comparables statement). Prompt 69 deliberately leaves two seams for it: `estimates.pricing_snapshot` stays jsonb and un-restructured so prompt 70 can key it by line, and per-line inputs stay cheaply hashable so the `inputs_key` cache discipline survives.

## [2026-08-03 MST] Prompt 67 shipped: Appointments calendar chips in the Google Calendar shape (month tinted pills, week/day solid blocks, real name resolution)

By: Claude Code

Changed: one code commit, pushed and deployed (ec0bd1a), plus this docs commit. No migration, no schema change, no data change, SCHEMA.md untouched. npm test green before the code commit: **618 checks, 0 failed, exit 0** (identical to the prompt-66 baseline; no test touched). All 7 real inline script blocks parse clean (node --check; block 1 is the importmap JSON, expected non-JS). Everything below was verified in the BROWSER against the LIVE deploy (prescottepoxy.netlify.app), signed in as Dylan, with live-database re-queries.

**Part A, name resolution, with one forced deviation from the prompt.** The prompt specified `leads(...)` as a PostgREST embed. That is IMPOSSIBLE: `pec_appointments.lead_id` deliberately has NO foreign key (SCHEMA.md: an appointment survives its lead's soft-delete), and PostgREST embeds require one; re-verified live via pg_constraint (only customer_id and sales_member_id carry FKs). Attempting the embed would 400 the whole range query and blank the calendar. Shipped instead: `customers(name)` rides the range query as a real embed (FK exists), and lead names come from ONE batched `leads .in(ids)` read for the whole visible range, merged as `row._lead`. Never per-event; one extra round trip only when lead-linked rows exist. Degradation is layered: an embed error retries the range read plain (a relation problem can never blank the calendar), a failed leads read just falls through to the title, and `apptDisplayName` is wrapped so it can never throw inside FullCalendar's events callback. Precedence as specified: customer name -> lead business_name -> full_name -> first+last -> title's name half -> type label. The prompt-65 inline title split (`"Jane Doe, Estimate"` -> `"Jane Doe"`) was extracted into `apptTitleNameHalf` and BOTH call sites use it; no second implementation exists.

**Parts B-C, the two treatments.** `apptChipContent` (wired via `eventContent`) returns plain divs/spans carrying `--pec-member`/`--pec-type` CSS custom properties; the event objects no longer set backgroundColor/borderColor, so the stylesheet owns the visuals and an inline style can never fight it. Month: tinted pill = type dot (8px) + short time (`9am`, `9:30am`, no `:00`; new `apptChipTime`, distinct from the form-field `apptFmtTime`) + ellipsised name, background `color-mix(member 14%, var(--rd-card))`, ink text, member-color left bar. Week/day: solid block stacking semibold name + time, type label, city/short address; background `color-mix(member 78%, #0b1220)`. Line collapse is keyed off DURATION set as classes in `apptEventFromRow` (under 60 min drops the place line, under 30 min collapses to one line), never a resize observer. All-day keeps the solid treatment and shows no time in every view. Part D: 6px radii, hover lift (shadow + 1px rise), today's day number in accent; toolbar and legend untouched, and the legend still reads true (round dot = member = chip background, square dot = type = chip dot).

**Dark mode, honest scope.** The prompt required dark-mode screenshots and contrast numbers. **The CRM has no dark mode**: `pecCurrentTheme()` (index.html ~7202) hardcodes `'light'` with a comment naming itself the single derivation point if a dark theme ever ships, and no `prefers-color-scheme` rule exists in the file. ## [2026-08-02 MST] Cowork: scoped prompt 63 (estimator product slots, inline-estimator gap, preview-modal exit, job-page picks) and prompt 64 (presentation view)
By: Cowork

Changed: two new prompt files only. No code, no schema, no data.

- `claude-code-prompt-63-estimator-slots-iframe-gap-preview-exit.md` (new)
- `claude-code-prompt-64-presentation-view.md` (new)

Dylan brought four items: (1) hide Basecoat/flake/topcoat from the estimate, (2) "estimate detail scrolls forever", (3) the customer preview modal cannot be exited, (4) a SumoQuote-style on-site presentation view. 28 multiple-choice questions were asked before writing anything. Dylan chose to split the work: prompt 63 is the three fixes plus the job-page picks, prompt 64 is the presentation on its own.

**Two root causes diagnosed from the code, not guessed:**

1. **The "scrolls forever" complaint is not a layout-taste problem.** Dylan clarified it is a large blank gap between the estimator's Notes-for-the-crew box and the Customer view card on draft estimates. Cause: `apps/estimator/src/styles.css:48` sets `html, body, #root { height: 100% }` unconditionally, and the embed height reporter (`EstimatorScreen.tsx` ~1178) measures `#root.scrollHeight`. In an iframe that means the reported height can never be LESS than the frame's current height, so the frame (mounted at `min(1100px, 85vh)`, `index.html:7171`) ratchets: it grows with content but never shrinks. `body.embed .screen { min-height: 0 }` at styles.css:54 was the attempted fix and it misses `#root`. Fix specified: `body.embed #root { height: auto }` plus a forced re-post, with a browser-verified SHRINK test as the acceptance criterion.

2. **The preview modal is a genuine dead end, by construction.** `estPreview` (`index.html` ~27515) passes iframe-only HTML to `openModal`, so there is no ✕ and no header. `openModal` (7982-7999) deliberately disables backdrop-click-to-close when the content matches `form, input, textarea, select, iframe` — `iframe` is in that guard to protect the ESTIMATOR modal's inputs, and the preview inherits protection it does not need. No Escape listener covers `.pec-modal-bg`. Only exit today is a page reload. Fix specified as an opt-in `dismissible` flag so no existing data-entry modal loses its stray-click protection, with three negative regression tests (change order, payment, compose must still refuse Escape and backdrop).

**Finding that made Part A safe:** `defaultSlotValues` (`EstimatorScreen.tsx` ~156-174) prefills every product slot from `default_product_id`, and `planForArea` resolves `pick || default_product_id`. Hiding the product dropdowns therefore cannot change `calc_price` or `materials_cost`. Prompt 63 requires proving it on three existing estimates rather than assuming it. One real behavior change is called out: `flakeColorFromPicks` will stop writing `estimates.flake_color` (swatch slots are deliberately unprefilled), so the manual `#estFlakeColor` field on the estimate detail page becomes the only writer. Dylan chose to keep that field for exactly this reason.

**Irony worth recording:** prompt 62 Part H is what made this card always visible. It deleted the `More detail` accordion because "a collapsed section kept getting skipped in the driveway". That was right for the work-order questions and wrong for the product dropdowns. Prompt 63 keeps the work-order questions always visible and hides only the product-kind slots, with a `Specify products` link as the escape hatch for commercial specs.

**Locked decisions, prompt 63:** hide EVERY product-kind slot (via the existing `kindOf(s)` helper) not just the three named ones, so a future product material_type hides automatically; keep choice/text slots and the system picker; keep the Work order block; `Specify products` link, session-only, defaults collapsed; job-page product picks are display-and-ordering ONLY and must never touch `computeCostingRow`, `materials_cost` or GP (the prompt-56 lesson is cited at the write site); preview gets ✕ + Escape + backdrop, the offline estimator fallback gets ✕ only.

**Locked decisions, prompt 64:** dashboard-side present mode, ONLINE ONLY; the estimate slide embeds the existing `?preview=` render from `pec-public-estimate.cjs` and never reimplements price or line items (Dylan said "never a new estimate itself" three times); the same Settings-managed section content ALSO renders read-only on the public estimate page so the literature reaches the spouse who was not home; four section types (why-us + warranty, process, gallery + reviews, financing); all active sections in Settings sort order, rep skips live, no per-estimate toggles; photos manually curated in Settings, reviews pulled from the prompt-60 reviews table; customer can sign on the rep's device, reusing the existing accept path with the approach to be reported before it is built.

**Conflict flagged rather than silently resolved:** Dylan answered the good/better/best tiering question three times across rounds and answered "no tiers" twice and "yes, and it's the point" once. Prompt 64 is written as NO tiers (one price plus a better visual treatment of the existing optional line items) and states the conflict explicitly so Dylan can overrule it. Real tiers would touch the calculator, the accept path, costing and metrics, and belong in their own prompt.

**Risk named to Dylan and accepted by him:** a dashboard-only present mode is a second surface, and online-only means a dead signal in a driveway kills the pitch. He kept the choice after being told. The drift risk is mitigated by the embed-the-real-renderer rule, which is the reason that rule is the governing constraint of prompt 64.

## [2026-08-02 MST] Cowork: multi-tenancy readiness assessment (no code changed)
By: Cowork

Changed: nothing. Read-only survey answering Dylan's question "how hard would it be to set this up for another company."

Findings, measured not guessed:
- No tenant model exists. 84 tables in SCHEMA.md, zero company_id / tenant_id / org_id columns. A `company` column exists on exactly three tables (admin_users default 'both', customers default 'prescott-epoxy', pec_webhook_ingest_log) and is the PEC/FTP brand flag, not a tenant key.
- RLS is staff-wide, not tenant-scoped. supabase/policies.sql has 17 policies, mostly blanket `authenticated` / is_staff_or_admin. Nothing would separate two companies inside one database.
- Single stack. One Supabase project, one Netlify site, 30 distinct process.env vars in netlify/functions plus 3 VITE_ vars, all single-valued. All 63 functions use the service role key, which bypasses RLS entirely, so each is a potential cross-tenant leak in any shared-instance design.
- Brand config partly exists already: pec_brand_identity (18 columns: logo, colors, business name, address, license, invoice copy) and the settings table (66 keys). That is the seed of a white-label layer.
- Hardcoded brand strings in index.html: PEC 102, FTP 43, "Prescott Epoxy" 34, "Finishing Touch" 11, plus the three Google Sheet IDs.
- Trade-specific depth: index.html mentions flake 312x, basecoat 208x, topcoat 121x, quartz 46x, moisture 25x, MOHS 22x. Catalog carries 182 products, 24 recipe slots, 11 system types, 21 colors, 25 lead sources. production/calculator.js is 938 lines of epoxy spread-rate math. A non-epoxy trade cannot reuse this half.
- Scale for reference: index.html 39,741 lines, 148 migrations, 953 commits since 2026-04-15.

Two paths were costed for Dylan in chat: (A) clone-per-company, separate Supabase + Netlify + third-party accounts, roughly 40 to 80 hours for the first one if the target is another epoxy contractor, plus a permanent two-fork maintenance tax; (B) true multi-tenant, company_id on ~84 tables, full RLS rewrite, per-tenant secrets, webhook routing, 3 to 6 months.

Highest-value de-risking step identified, not yet done: verify that supabase/migrations replays cleanly into an empty database and produces today's schema. Many migrations were applied live via MCP rather than by replay, so a fresh-database build is currently unproven. Every clone plan is blocked on that being true.

Why: Dylan asked a scoping question before committing to anything.

3. **Estimate start**: new `estimates.customer_id`. Three paths: existing customer, from existing lead, new customer. An estimate does not need a lead.
4. **Pipeline**: new **Drafts** column (derived from `estimates.status = 'draft'`, NOT a new stage, no CHECK change) between Estimate Scheduled and Estimate Sent. The board renders **two card shapes**: lead cards as today, plus estimate cards for estimates with no lead. Estimate cards move by estimate status, not by drag. Lost added to the Metrics pipeline widget.
5. **Lost**: keep the six reasons, no Settings surface. New `leads.lost_notes`, optional and always available. AI pre-fills the reason and notes from a recent call at Mark-lost time (suggestion only), plus a nightly backfill for already-lost leads that never overwrites a human value.
6. **Estimator**: the `More detail` accordion is deleted and its fields render always-visible. `special_notes` is retired in favor of one large "Notes for the crew" box at the bottom bound to `crew_notes`. MOHS and moisture get a loud red banner and are **never blocked** (Dylan wrote "required for every quote" but chose warning-only and confirmed on a second pass).
7. **Search**: `#rdSearch` becomes one global bar on every page across jobs, estimates, leads, customers, grouped results, 5 per group. The existing in-list search boxes are kept; Dylan said he did not know the difference between the two, and they filter a visible table rather than jump to a record.

## Landmines recorded in the prompt

- **Prompt 61 is unverified** and prompt 62 rebuilds the same estimate-start path. Dylan was offered a verify-first sequencing and chose to run one prompt straight through; the prompt tells Claude Code to stop and report if 61's behavior contradicts its log entry.
- **`estimates.lead_id` can now be null.** Part E requires an audit of every reader (leadValueMapFrom, kanban value, Metrics, Ops Queue, drips, accept path, pec-webhook-proposal-accepted, estimator load/save) before building.
- **Two card shapes touch every board behavior**: column sort, score sort, value rollup, source badge, filters, appointment sort, empty state, drag. It will look fine on 6 leads and break at 60.
- **`pec_call_log` has `customer_id`, not `lead_id`** (474 rows). Lost-reason matching has to go through `phone_norm`; the prompt requires reporting the actual match rate so a decorative feature gets caught.
- `full_name` must never be null for a Business lead. supabase-js still returns an empty response for a nonexistent column without throwing.

Why: Dylan's pasted list of eight items, expanded by his own answers into the lead/customer/estimate rework.

**Part A, inline estimator.** The estimate detail page now hosts the estimator iframe inline: a draft opens with it up, Edit swaps it in on any other status, Close returns to the read-only summary in place, and the right column (customer view, pricing, activity) stays visible throughout. The app posts its content height (`pec-estimator-height`, ResizeObserver throttled to one message per animation frame) and the page grows with the form. **The height fallback exists but was not needed in reasoning about normal flow; it fires only if no message lands within 1500ms (min(1100px, 85vh), 520px floor), and whether it ever fires in practice needs Dylan's walkthrough to confirm.**

**Landmine 1, the audit.** 15 `renderEstimateDetail(` references exist (1 definition, 14 call sites: list-row click, the openEstimateId shortcut, send flows x2, status changes, archive/restore, flake save, line-item toggle/remove/add, scope answers/generate/edit-cancel/edit-save). Rather than guarding each caller, the guard lives ONCE at the top of `renderEstimateDetail`: when the inline estimator for that estimate is alive, the skeleton (chrome / inline host / body) is kept and only chrome+body rebuild around the untouched iframe. Every existing call site therefore refreshes data without reloading the PWA, and a save from inside the estimator stays put with the header/totals visibly refreshed (Part A items 7/8).

**Visual continuity (Part A item 9), stated honestly.** The estimator's styles.css now mirrors the dashboard's `--rd-*` tokens verbatim (PEC orange accent, same surfaces/ink/lines/font), embed mode drops the dark brand bar and app title in favor of a slim status row, the frame background is transparent so the page supplies the surface, and theme is parent-driven (`pec-theme` postMessage, dark token set ready). **I could not verify by screenshot in this session** (the change needs the Netlify deploy plus a signed-in session); Dylan's handoff walkthrough is the visual acceptance. Note also the dashboard's CRM skin is light-only today, so the both-themes screenshot is not reachable until a dark CRM ships; the channel and dark tokens are in place for that day. **Part B, draft-on-create.** New estimate / Start estimate inserts the draft row first (duplicate guard BEFORE the insert, via the shared `leadOpenEstimates`; a declined duplicate leaves no orphan), prefills job info onto the row from the lead in BOTH column shapes (split + composed legacy, mirroring the estimator's save exactly), and lands on the detail page with the estimator open. Offline (or a network-shaped insert failure) falls back to today's modal + outbox with a visible note; that is the one remaining modal launch. The estimator seeds the create-path Main area when a loaded draft has zero areas (`initialAreas` in estimate-draft.cjs; the stale placeholder in estimateLoad.ts was removed so default slot values seed properly).

**Draft counting, the one behavior change to disclose (Part B item 7):** `leadValueMapFrom` now SKIPS rows with a null price. Before, the newest-live-estimate rule meant a fresh priceless draft would zero out a lead's kanban/Metrics value even when an older, real estimate existed; with drafts now created before pricing, that would have fired constantly. No Ops Queue check and no Metrics counter reads draft estimates; Metrics conversion-by-source reads lead stage columns, not estimate rows.

**Part C, native job info editing.** `#estJobInfo` renders provenance ("from lead X (still matching)" vs "edited on this estimate · differs from lead" with one-click Push to lead) and states the authority rule in one line: the estimate carries its own snapshot; the lead and customer are only updated when someone says yes. Edit swaps in a form in place; save writes split + legacy columns and then, when shared fields differ from the linked lead/customer, asks each time with PRE-CHECKED boxes. Salesperson mirrors the estimator's admin lock and fails closed; a change read-modify-writes the whole `intake` on a fresh read. Propagation writes a `lead_events` `lead_updated` row and `leadEventHtml` renders it.

**Part D, lead source unification.** Inventory printed in chat before any write. Live state was: leads.source held tokens (meta x3, google x2, manual, other, Other, webform, word_of_mouth; 10 rows), customers.lead_source already held managed names (36 rows) or null (55). Applied mapping: meta -> Facebook (alias), google -> Google, webform -> Website (alias), other/Other -> Other, and four NEW managed rows for counterpart-less tokens: Manual entry [manual], Word of Mouth [word_of_mouth], Google LSA [google_lsa], plus Angi [angi], Phone Call [openphone], DripJobs [dripjobs] for the intake vocabulary (19 -> 25 rows). **Rewrite counts: 9 lead rows changed, 0 unmapped leftovers, 0 customer rows changed, 55 customer nulls untouched.** Routemize's `'routemize'` fallback token is deliberately unmapped (resolver warns and passes it through; its real leadSourceText values map by name). `resolveLeadSourceName` (new `_pec-lead-source.cjs`) maps exact name > ci name > alias; `pec-lead-intake` maps BEFORE the source+source_ref dedupe (landmine 9), `pec-appt-intake` maps at both its sites without touching fill-only-when-null, and the only other `source` writer found (pec-webhook-proposal-accepted) writes `jobs.source`, a different concept, untouched. Client: `leadSourceKey` normalizes every badge lookup (canonical names keep colors), the New-lead picker and board filter run off the managed list plus data leftovers, and the Settings lead-source editor gained the Aliases field (this build's rule-12 surface).

**Part E, manual source editing.** Click the source badge on a lead (or the source line on a customer), pick, save: `changeLeadSource` updates both records in sync and writes a `source_changed` lead_events row with the actor; the timeline renders "Source changed from X to Y". No permission gate, no kanban editor, no bulk edit (all declined by Dylan). A customer with no lead updates without a timeline entry, by design (code comment, not a new table). The customer form's required source select shares the same option builder.

**Test update to disclose:** `estimate15b.test.js`'s duplicate-guard section asserted the guard query lived inline in `openEstimatorModal` and that the lead button routed to the modal. The invariant is unchanged (one guard query, every create-for-a-lead path covered, raw frame never opened with a fresh lead); its home moved per this build's architecture, so the assertions now check `leadOpenEstimates` + both callers, including that draft-on-create guards BEFORE the insert.

## [2026-07-31 MST] Cowork: wrote prompt 61 (estimator inline on the estimate detail page, native job info editing, lead source unification and manual editing), 16 decisions locked
By: Cowork

Changed: one new file, claude-code-prompt-61-estimator-inline-lead-source.md. No code, no schema, no prod change. Sixteen multiple-choice questions were asked before writing (project rule); the answers are the LOCKED lines in the prompt.

WHAT DYLAN ASKED FOR, verbatim: "estimator pre fills job info. Instead of a pop up modal, can you make it all on the estimate detail page? The flow is confusing right now" and "Ability to update lead source manually."

THE FORK THAT SHAPED THE BUILD: "make it all on the estimate detail page" spans a 10x range, from moving the iframe out of the modal to porting 2,373 lines of React into index.html. Dylan chose **inline hosting, not a rewrite**: the estimator PWA stays exactly as it is architecturally (own service worker, offline outbox, /estimator/ standalone) and gets rendered inline in the estimate detail page instead of over it. He also named the three things that actually bother him: two UIs for one estimate, editing one field costing a full estimator reopen, and the modal trapping him over the dashboard. Inlining alone only fixes the third, which is why Parts B and C exist.

THE FINDING WORTH REMEMBERING, and landmine 1 in the prompt: **a whole-page re-render while the estimator is mounted destroys the iframe, reloads the PWA, and silently discards the rep's unsaved work.** renderEstimateDetail(est.id) is called from roughly a dozen handlers in index.html (line-item toggles, scope edits, status changes, archive/restore). Today that is free because the estimator lives in a modal that is never inside the re-rendered region. The moment the frame lives inside the page, every one of those calls is a data-loss path. The prompt makes auditing them the first landmine and criterion 2 tests it. This is the single most likely way to ship something worse than the modal.

THE SECOND FINDING: **Dylan wants New estimate to create a draft row immediately**, which is what lets creation land on the detail page too. estimates is permissive enough for it (every column nullable or defaulted; an insert of lead_id + created_by is legal), and job info gets prefilled ONTO THE ROW rather than only into form state, which is the "pre fills job info" half of his sentence. Two consequences he accepted knowingly: abandoned empty drafts accumulate (he declined auto-archive, hiding, and a Draft filter, and will archive by hand), and estimate_number is a sequence default so abandoned drafts burn numbers and customer-facing numbering will show gaps. Also written in: the estimator currently seeds a single Main area only on the CREATE path, so a freshly created empty draft opened via ?estimate_id= renders with no area row at all. That fix belongs in the estimator, not in a fake database row.

THE THIRD FINDING, on lead source: **it is two columns with two vocabularies.** leads.source holds code tokens (manual, meta, google_lsa, webform, angi, openphone, dripjobs), is set once in the New lead modal, and has no edit UI anywhere. customers.lead_source holds pec_lead_sources names (19 managed rows with a Settings CRUD already built). Dylan ruled one vocabulary: unify on pec_lead_sources, migrate the stored data, and map incoming feed tokens at intake, with a new aliases column so a future feed is a data change not a code change. He also wants both fields kept in sync and every change logged on the lead timeline (lead_events), and he declined an original_source column, a role gate, bulk edit, and kanban-card editing.

THE BUG THAT MIGRATION WOULD HAVE CAUSED, caught while writing: pec-lead-intake.cjs dedupes with /leads?source=eq.<source>&source_ref=eq.<ref>. Rewrite the stored values to canonical names while the endpoint still queries with the raw token and idempotency breaks, so every Zapier retry creates a duplicate lead. The prompt makes "map before dedupe" landmine 9 and acceptance criterion 10. Same class of thing: LEAD_SOURCE_COLORS / LEAD_SOURCE_LABELS are keyed by token, so post-migration every source badge silently goes gray unless the lookup key is normalized.

His first answer put the source editor on the customer page only. That was put back to him with the observation that most leads have no customer record until they book, and that Metrics conversion-by-source reads leads.source, so customer-only editing leaves the number that matters uncorrectable. He added the lead detail page.

WHAT COWORK COULD NOT DO: the Supabase MCP returned 502 three times, so the live pec_lead_sources rows and the live distinct source values were never read. Rather than guess a mapping, Part D step 1 is an inventory step: Claude Code queries prod, prints the counts, and proposes the token-to-name mapping in chat for Dylan to approve BEFORE the migration is applied. Nothing in the prompt hardcodes a mapping.

Correction to my own reading of state: this session started by reading the last 3 log entries, at which point the top entry was the prompt-60 revision and prompt 60 was unrun. Prompt 60 shipped (commits 9802b39 through dba990a) while these questions were being asked, so the sequencing answer ("one prompt 61, both features, run after 60") is already satisfied and 61 is simply next.

Why: Dylan brought two feature requests; project rule requires 10+ scoping questions and a written prompt before Claude Code touches code.

## [2026-07-31 MST] Prompt 60 shipped: Google review ask drip, Zapier review intake, crew leader attribution, review bonus ledger
By: Claude Code

Changed: the full prompt-60 build, across seven commits (9802b39, 04708d8, c6d7278, 1228c6a, 6ed7792, 819a42f, 36ad3f0 plus this bookkeeping commit). Migration `2026-08-04_review_drip.sql` APPLIED LIVE to zdfpzmmrgotynrwkeakd via MCP and verified with pg_get_constraintdef / information_schema (kind CHECK now admits 'review'; reviews.job_id and customer_id NOT NULL DROPPED; both new tables, the one-open-ask partial unique index, uq on pec_review_bonuses.review_id, seven review_* settings all confirmed live). SCHEMA.md regenerated. npm test green, 563 checks including the two new suites.

WHAT SHIPPED, by part:

- **A, schema**: `pec_review_requests` (one row per ask; token for /r/; crew_lead/crew_id SNAPSHOTS; job_completed_date preserves the real completion date for backfills), `reviews` widened for the Google feed (external_id idempotency key, match_status unmatched/auto/confirmed/rejected), `pec_review_bonuses` (unique review_id so one review can never pay twice), campaign 'Review request' seeded kind 'review', 4 steps day 1/3/7/14 sms/sms/email/sms, **mode 'live'** per decision 15.
- **B, close-out popup**: all FOUR completion paths that stamp completed_date open the same openReviewAskModal after the write commits (markJobComplete, the status-change modal / pipeline drag, the job detail Mark job complete, and the production completeActiveJob via the window bridge, since the production dashboard is a separate module scope). The fifth completed_date writer, the Bonus Report set-completion-date data fix, is DELIBERATELY not wired (it stamps weeks-old dates for bonus locking; the backfill covers those jobs) and says so in a comment. Both popup branches write a request row; Skip records skipped_at/_by so a choice is never confused with forgetting. Job detail gets the review-status chip and a Request review button.
- **C, tracking link**: /r/* netlify redirect to pec-review-redirect.cjs, which resolves the destination FIRST (with a hardcoded fallback to the live g.page URL), then does all bookkeeping best-effort (first_clicked_at first-write-wins, click_count increment, asked->clicked only forward), then 302s no matter what. A garbage token still lands on Google.
- **D, drip kind**: KIND_CHECKS.review (stop reasons reviewed / touchup_opened incl. child callback rows / job_closed / request-carried bad_review; replies and STOP ride the universal core untouched), review render prompt + explicit-null crew_lead in the fact record, kindTail appends the /r/ link by code, reviewCopyViolation mechanically drops any rendered leg offering something of value for a review, review_drip_enabled as a hold-in-place master switch, and THE GUARD: enrollReviewDrip (server) and enrollReviewDripClient (browser mirror) both refuse to enroll while the campaign is live, drip_approval_required is not 'true', and no send was ever approved. That guard is the entire dry-run substitute; do not special-case around it.
- **E, intake**: pec-review-intake.cjs (REVIEW_INTAKE_SECRET header, candidate-list field reading for both the raw GBP resource shape and flattened variants, starRating words like FIVE parsed, deterministic synthetic id when Google sends none). Idempotent on external_id: re-fires update and never re-alert. Auto-match scores name similarity (contradicting last initial scores ZERO), crew-leader mention in the text, and click evidence; only an untied score >= 2 matches, and the ceiling is match_status='auto'. The intake cannot write 'confirmed'; the test suite asserts it.
- **F, surfaces**: renderReviews rebuilt (badges keep Auto-matched amber and visually distinct from Confirmed green; Confirm / Reassign / Reject per row; the 'Asked, no review yet' tab is a filter with days-since-ask + phone/email and raises nothing anywhere, per decision 14). Metrics Reviews section: ask funnel with rates (windowed), per-crew-leader scoreboard labeled 'HUMAN-CONFIRMED reviews of N+ stars only', star breakdown including unmatched. Settings > Reviews with all seven keys. Bad-review bells route through notifTarget to the Reviews view.
- **G, bonus ledger**: Confirm on a qualifying rating inserts pec_review_bonuses at the settings amount (crew_member_id only on an unambiguous name match, else null with the name shown). Bonus Report gains the Review bonuses card: Approve -> Mark paid (payroll date) -> or Void with a reason (the reversal path). Grepped and verified ZERO coupling: nothing review-related reads or writes pec_prod_job_bonuses, bonus_cost, or computeCostingRow, so a review landing after costing finalizes cannot move GP (the prompt-56 lesson, decision 13).
- **H, backfill**: scripts/backfill-review-asks.cjs, re-runnable and idempotent, with --dry-run printing the exact list to skim. Anchors to ENROLLMENT time by construction (enrollSubject computes next_send_at from now), so a 25-day-old completion yields exactly one due step; the test proves it. The gate guard runs ONCE up front so a refused run writes nothing (a request row without an enrollment would poison the idempotency check).
- **I, bad reviews**: a rating at or below review_alert_max_stars raises one pec_notifications bell (stars + customer name if matched, reviewer name if not, clickable to Reviews) and stops any live review enrollment with stop_reason 'bad_review'. Unmatched bad reviews still alert. Insert-only, never on a re-fire.

Design choice worth recording: the popup opens AFTER the completion write commits rather than before, so completing a job is never hostage to the review UX; dismissing the modal without choosing records nothing and stays recoverable via the Request review button (a dismissal is closer to "forgot" than to "chose not to ask", and only Skip should record a choice).

Verified live while building: drip_approval_required is ALREADY 'true' and drip_sending_enabled is 'true' on prod, and google_review_link_epoxy holds https://g.page/r/prescottepoxy/review. So the gate is on before this deploys, which was the one precondition with teeth.

Why: Dylan wants NiceJob-style review asks inside TopCoat with per-crew-leader attribution and a bonus, per the 25 locked decisions in claude-code-prompt-60-review-drip.md.
