## [2026-07-21 MST] Notes split + phone-on-details + combined Email/Text send (prompt 38, all three features)
By: Claude Code
Changed: Shipped prompt 38 in five commits, one per feature/sub-part so each reverts alone: the Cowork scoping docs commit (7123fb1), the appointment notes split (b10ceec), phone tap-to-call/text on details (5eeb05c), the invoice combined Send control (120c976), and the NEW estimate text channel + its combined control (eb8471a), plus this docs commit.

FEATURE 1 (notes split): `pec_appointments.notes` STAYS the internal Company notes (no data migration; existing notes were written as internal detail and already fed the Google description); the new `customer_notes` column (migration `2026-07-21_appointment_customer_notes.sql`, written NOT applied, verify block at the bottom) is the customer-facing Job notes. The form shows both with helper text and a one-shot save retry that drops customer_notes pre-migration so saves never block. The Google push now composes the event description as internal notes + a `----` separator + an auto-added block (customer name/phone fetched from the linked lead/customer, plus an `/?appt=<id>` deep link that renderAuthUI consumes at boot to open that appointment); customer_notes is NEVER pushed. The reminder engine appends the scrubbed job note to customer messages on BOTH channels, after the template and before the SMS STOP line; salesperson bells never carry it. The pull strips everything from the separator down before ingesting a Google-side description edit into notes, so the auto block can never clobber the human-typed part, and never writes customer_notes.

FEATURE 2 (phone on details): shared `pecPhoneActionsHtml` (tel: link + Text button) wired by ONE delegated document listener, on: the job detail header (its Text routes to the job's own Messages & Calls tab, the canonical text-the-customer surface), the printed Crew Work Order's Job Identity grid (the prompt's `renderJobCard` anchor does not exist; the notes-box line it pointed at IS the work-order sheet, so the phone landed there as a tel: line in the formerly blank pair), the lead kanban card and lead detail, and the appointment popup (phone fetched async from the linked lead/customer). Everything else routes through `pecOpenTextTo` -> the EXISTING Messages thread; `openMessageThread` now synthesizes an empty seeded thread for a number with no history, with the send path unchanged (customer_id when known else raw number) so consent/STOP and logging stay in the one place. No phone = a muted note, never a dead link.

FEATURE 3 (combined send): one shared split control (`pecSplitSendHtml`/`pecWireSplitSend`), primary click = Email + Text, caret = one channel, on BOTH the invoice page and the estimate detail. Nothing sends on the click itself: "both" shows the text confirm FIRST (declining quietly downgrades to email only), then the email compose; the text leg fires only after the email actually sent, so a canceled compose sends nothing. Missing channels never hard-block (no email on file falls through to text-only, no phone/opt-out/no-link sends email with a "text skipped" note). Invoice: same code as before refactored into openInvoiceEmail/doInvoiceTextSend (kind='invoice', STOP line, server opt-out authority, invoice_first_sent_at stamp + invoice-drip enroll on either channel). Estimate: the TEXT CHANNEL IS NEW. pec-send-sms's kind='estimate' 501 seam is now real: lookup by public_token, server-built body with the /e/<token> review-and-sign link + STOP line, opt-out enforced for the linked lead (opted_out) AND its customer (sms_opt_out), logged kind 'estimate' with customer attribution resolved through the lead (stays out of Last-invoiced). CRITICAL side-effect parity: `markEstimateSent` is the one shared flip (sent_at + status 'sent' + estimateSentLeadEffects), so a TEXT-only estimate goes live and the lead metrics/drip handoff stay right; the combined path passes skipFlip on the text leg so sent-state stamps exactly once, and a text-that-sent-but-flip-failed says so loudly (the customer's link would 404). The blank-scope BLANK warn gate is extracted and fires on ANY channel.

VERIFIED: npm test 142; appt-reminders 44 (adds: job note on both channels with em-dash scrub + STOP line last, bell never carries it, pre-migration no-op); google-pull 22 (adds: compose/strip round-trip, Google-side edit survives above the separator, block-only strips to null notes, mapping ingests only free text); drip suites 55 + 60; node --check clean on pec-send-sms.cjs, pec-appt-sync-push.cjs, pec-google-calendar-pull.cjs, _pec-appt.cjs, _pec-google.cjs; all 7 inline index.html JS blocks parse; features.json + whats-new.json validate; zero em dashes in customer-facing additions. NOT verified live: the estimate text send (new Quo path) and the composed-Google-description round-trip need one real-world pass (handoffs below).

## [2026-07-20 MST] Appointments calendar + Google two-way sync + address autocomplete (prompt 37, BOTH phases)
By: Claude Code
Changed: Shipped all of prompt 37 in eleven commits, keeping the prompt's commit boundaries so the Google layer (Phase B) can be reverted without touching the calendar. Phase A: the migration (80a2bdd docs + 3b09aa9), the native Appointments view (79d125b), the vanilla Places helper wired into the appointment form (9923364), lead-form autocomplete + split city/state/zip (20e38c9), Schedule Estimate from the lead card/detail (f17d373), booking notifications (a731347), and the scheduled reminder runner + fixture tests (ce80229). Phase B: per-member Google OAuth (1564349), push TopCoat->Google (2eb61ba), the scheduled pull (657d1f0), and the Settings > Appointments panel (e09a2af). Plus this docs commit (features.json x3, whats-new x4).

HOW IT FITS TOGETHER: `pec_appointments` is the one table; `renderAppointments` (new Sales nav item, all staff) renders it with FullCalendar 6 lazy-loaded from cdnjs (Chart.js pattern; a blocked CDN degrades to a month-list that still creates/edits, because the write path never touches the render library). `openAppointmentForm` is the single create/edit/cancel/delete modal with a prefill + onSaved seam; everything after any write funnels through `apptPostWrite`: refresh the surface, on NEW bookings fire `apptBookingSideEffects` (bell + confirmation kick), and kick the Google push. The reminder engine (`_pec-appt.cjs` runApptReminders) is shared by the immediate on-book kick (pec-appt-notify, staff JWT) and the 15-minute pec-appt-reminder-runner: claim-first inserts into the pec_appointment_reminder_sends ledger (unique index = exactly-once per appointment/rule/channel), consent re-checked from the live row at send time (lead: positive sms_consent + not opted_out, email_consent; customer: opt-out-only), SMS held outside 8am-8pm Phoenix with NO ledger row so the next in-window tick releases it, em dashes scrubbed in code, sends mirrored into pec_sms_log / pec_email_log with kind/template_key 'appointment'.

DECISIONS I MADE THAT DYLAN SHOULD KNOW ABOUT:
1. STAGE MAPPING: the locked decision said Schedule Estimate "advances the lead to the estimate stage", but LEAD_STAGES has no such stage, and the closest key (estimate_sent) is stamped only when a real estimate document goes out; it feeds the conversion metrics and the drip kill-switch, so faking it at booking time would corrupt both. A NEW lead therefore advances to 'contacted' (through commitLeadStage, so the first-touch timestamp and stage_change event are real) and anything at/past contacted keeps its stage. If Dylan wants a real 'estimate_scheduled' kanban column, that is a follow-up prompt (it touches LEAD_STAGES, the kanban, and the drip stage rules).
2. BELL PATH: client JS cannot insert pec_notifications under RLS (the "insert shape" the prompt pointed at is really the SECURITY DEFINER RPC pattern, per log_customer_deleted). The migration adds log_appointment_booked; the on-book salesperson bell goes through it instantly at booking time, and the seeded on-book salesperson RULE was removed so the runner can never double-notify. Salesperson rules added later in the editor (e.g. in-app 60 min before) are handled by the runner. notifTarget routes 'appointments' bell taps to the calendar and opens that appointment.
3. GOOGLE DESIGN: built the recommended dedicated-calendar model. Connect creates (or reuses) a "TopCoat" calendar in the member's own account; push writes only there, pull reads only there, personal calendars are never touched. The optional read-only primary-calendar overlay was NOT built (it was additive and unconfirmed); if Dylan wants the greyed personal blocks, that is a small follow-up on the pull runner. Pull is incremental syncToken polling every 15 min (410 = drop token, full resync), NOT watch channels. Echo/loop prevention: push stores the event's etag/updated on the row; a pulled event whose updated is not newer is our own echo and is skipped; newer wins (LWW). Reassignment deletes from the old member's calendar before inserting on the new one. Tokens live in pec_sales_member_google_tokens: RLS ON with ZERO policies (service-role only); the UI reads only the roster flags.
4. CONFIRMATION SENDS ARE LIVE ON ARRIVAL: the two seeded customer rules (on-book confirmation, 1-day reminder, both channels) ship enabled, per the locked decision that booking sends are wanted. They only fire for consented recipients, and only once per appointment. If Dylan wants to review wording first, the Settings > Appointments editor can disable or edit them the moment the deploy is live (sending also cannot start before the migration is applied).
5. QUIET-HOURS EDGE: an evening booking's confirmation SMS is held to next morning 8am (the runner releases it); the email goes immediately. A booking whose appointment start has already passed never messages the customer (skipped_past).

## [2026-07-19 MST] Blasts + metrics: the manual blast tool and the drip/blast performance cards (prompt 35, Phase 3, ship set 2 of 2, PHASE 3 COMPLETE)
By: Claude Code
Changed: Ship set 2 of 2 for prompt 35 (Parts D-E; ship set 1 is the next entry down). Four commits: the blast drain engine + pec-blast-run (0bfbdc4), the compose wizard UI + contact-count fold + AI draft action (edc4f6a), the metrics cards (b2faf61), and this docs commit. No new migration: ship set 1's 2026-07-19_drip_phase3.sql already carried pec_blasts, blast_id, and the 'sending' status, so prod needs exactly ONE migration for all of Phase 3. SHIPS SAFE: blasts are gated by the same master switch (still 'false'); a confirmed blast with the switch off just queues and says so.

THE SHARED-LEDGER DESIGN (the load-bearing idea): a blast is ONE composed message to a chosen audience, not an enrolled sequence, so it never touches the runner loop. At confirm time the wizard materializes every recipient as a status 'queued' pec_drip_sends row (blast_id set, enrollment_id null, lead_id set for lead recipients). That queue IS three things at once: the resumability story (a failure mid-way leaves queued rows; any later pass finishes them), the no-double-send guard (the drain claims each row queued->'sending' with the same conditional-PATCH atomicity as the drip runner; a claimed row is never claimed again, and a crashed pass's stale 'sending' rows are swept to failed after an hour, NEVER re-queued, because the first send may have landed), and the metrics/contact-count source (lead-directed blast sends flow into the Phase 1 outbound-touch count through the same ledger the drips use; the pec_sms_log/pec_email_log mirrors carry kind/template_key 'blast' and the counter skips them, so one send counts exactly once).

THE COMPLIANCE GATE, in order: (1) consent hard-filter BEFORE the count is shown: leads need positive sms_consent and not opted_out for texts (email_consent for email); customers are opt-out-only (sms_opt_out); removed-for-consent and removed-duplicate counts are displayed. (2) De-dupe by phone tail + lowercased email, leads winning collisions so sends keep lead attribution. (3) Per-recipient deselect checkboxes. (4) A confirm step stating the EXACT per-channel counts ("42 texts and 57 emails to 61 recipients"), with quiet-hours and master-off warnings inline, then a final typed confirm; the header's total_queued equals the confirmed count by construction (rows and counts come from the same picked list). (5) Consent RE-CHECKED at send time from the live lead/customer row, so a STOP that lands between confirm and send wins ('opted_out_after_queue'). (6) Quiet hours: outside 8am-8pm Phoenix the drain simply does not claim SMS rows; email flows; held texts go at the next in-window pass. (7) Master switch OFF = nothing moves. Blasts have NO dry_run mode on purpose: the human confirm IS the review gate.

SENDING: two callers, one engine. pec-blast-run (staff JWT, ~20s budget, loops drain passes) is the immediate kick after confirm; the 15-minute pec-drip-runner tick drains one pass as the safety net (crash resume, quiet-hours release, switch-flipped-later). Re-kicks are always safe (claims make them idempotent). BLAST_BATCH=25 per blast per pass is deliberately separate from the drip RUN_CAP so a 500-person blast can never starve the drips, and big blasts finish over successive passes/ticks. Bodies are personalized at CONFIRM time ({first_name} token only, STOP line guaranteed on every text) and sent verbatim by the drain: no AI at send time, and the ledger stores exactly what was sent. Destinations are deliberately NOT frozen at confirm (re-resolved at send so a corrected phone/email is honored). "Draft with AI" rides pec-lead-ai's new draft_blast action: draft-only, scrubbed server-side, forbidden from inventing offers/prices/dates the typed goal does not state.

That SCHEMA.md regen also answered a standing question: the Phase 2 drip migration IS applied to prod (all four pec_drip_* tables live, 1 seeded campaign, 8 steps, 0 enrollments), so the Cowork handoff below only needs the NEW migration.

SUBJECT GENERALIZATION (the schema move everything else stands on): pec_drip_enrollments and pec_drip_sends now carry (subject_type, subject_id). WHY: Phase 2 hard-keyed everything to lead_id, which cannot represent a job-based invoice reminder, and its one-active-per-LEAD unique index broke the moment a lead needed a nurture drip and an estimate drip at once. The new partial unique is one active per (subject_type, subject_id, campaign_id). lead_id went nullable but STAYS POPULATED for lead subjects, deliberately: the Phase 1 contact counter and the Quo STOP webhook both join on it, so keeping it beats migrating those readers. subject_id has no FK (polymorphic); the runner treats a missing subject as a stop, so orphans self-clean. The migration also ships the pec_blasts table + pec_drip_sends.blast_id + the 'sending' claim status for ship set 2, so prod needs ONE migration for all of Phase 3.

HOW ESTIMATE DRIPS ENROLL AND STOP: the client-side "Send to customer" flow already funnels lead bookkeeping through estimateSentLeadEffects; that now stops any active lead-nurture enrollment (stop_reason 'estimate_sent', so one person is never on two nurture tracks, and the specific reason beats waiting a tick for the stage_advanced kill-switch) and enrolls the estimate taper (days 1,3,7,14). Stops at send time: any estimate accepted OR interim 'signed' (the e-sign CAS writes 'signed' before 'accepted'; checking only accepted would nag a customer who just signed) -> 'accepted'; all estimates rejected/reverted or lead lost -> 'lost'; a portal change request -> 'replied' (the customer engaged, a human takes over); inbound text/call -> 'replied'; opted_out; max_touches. A re-send after a stop starts a fresh taper on purpose (revised estimate, fresh clock). The signing link is appended by CODE from public_token AFTER the scrubber runs (scrubCopy strips model URLs by design), with the SMS cap shortened so link + STOP line can never truncate; the model may state the price only when the record carries one.

HOW INVOICE DRIPS ENROLL AND STOP: both invoice-send paths stamp jobs.invoice_first_sent_at first-send-wins, and the null->set transition enrolls the JOB exactly once (taper 0,+3,+7,+14 anchored to the send moment; no due-date column exists anywhere, and enrollment is never backdated because a backdated anchor would fire four reminders in an hour). BUG FIXED ALONG THE WAY: the Text-invoice path never stamped invoice_first_sent_at at all, so a text-only invoice was invisible to the AR-timing metric and would never have enrolled; it now stamps identically to the email path. The recipient is the job's customer via the new resolver (opt-out-only consent model, matching pec-send-sms: STOP silences the SMS leg, email reminders continue). THE BALANCE IS RECOMPUTED EVERY RUN from jobs.price minus sum(pec_payments.amount), never cached and never via the pec_job_ar view (security_invoker + authenticated-only grant makes the view unreliable for the service role): a partial payment keeps reminders coming with the real remaining balance in the copy, and the payment that clears it stops the enrollment 'paid' on the next tick. Voided/archived jobs stop 'job_closed'. Balance + pay link are code-appended; the model can never invent an amount. MONEY GUARDRAIL: the invoice campaign ships dry_run and should stay there until Dylan has read several days of generated copy; once live + master switch on, these send automatically (said plainly in What's New).

## [2026-07-19 MST] Drips: the automatic AI-tailored lead drip engine (prompt 34, Phase 2 of 3 delivered)
By: Claude Code
Changed: Delivered claude-code-prompt-34-lead-drip-engine-phase2 (archived to docs/archive/prompts/). Six commits in revertable units: migration (schema+seed), runner core + scheduled function + 55-check fixture (7d68619), enrollment wiring + Quo STOP (1bb78c3), contact-count fold (dc2eb86), UI (b247b16), and this docs commit. SHIPS SAFE-BY-DEFAULT: the master switch (settings key drip_sending_enabled) is seeded 'false' and the seeded campaign is in dry_run, so NOTHING can send until Dylan reviews the dry-run copy and flips both. The migration is NOT applied (Cowork handoff below); until it is, every drip surface degrades cleanly (no chips, no card, Drips view shows an apply-migration notice, intake enrollment is a swallowed no-op). Log-integrity note: Cowork's 2026-07-19 verification entry (below) was written against a stale checkout missing the two committed leads-robustness entries; committing that working file verbatim would have DELETED committed history, so it was merged onto HEAD's intact log instead (commit 5780ca4). The "missing" Phase 1 ship entry was never lost; it is in 2354d52.

HOW THE ENGINE WORKS: pec_drip_campaigns (kind lead/estimate/invoice, status, mode dry_run/live, max_touches) -> pec_drip_steps (the seeded 8-step taper: days 1,2,4,7,11,16,22,30 from enrollment, channels alternating sms/email/both, per-step ai_guidance the model tailors from) -> pec_drip_enrollments (ONE active per lead via partial unique index; next_step_index + next_send_at drive the runner) -> pec_drip_sends (the ledger: one row per channel leg per step, statuses queued/sent/failed/skipped/dry_run; also the 4th contact-count source). All logic lives in _pec-drip.cjs behind injected deps; pec-drip-runner.cjs is a thin scheduled function (netlify.toml, every 15 min, pec-auto-progress posture: an outside call just triggers an ordinary idempotent tick). New leads auto-enroll at intake (server-side, after both dedupe paths, best-effort so Zapier can never see a drip failure) and on manual add (client-side enrollLeadInDrip; the partial unique index is the backstop). NO retro-enrollment: leads already in the pipeline when this deploys do not enroll (per the prompt; the Enroll button on the lead page is the manual path if Dylan wants one in).

KILL-SWITCHES, RE-CHECKED AT SEND TIME (never trusted from enrollment): (1) replied: any inbound pec_sms_log or pec_call_log row matching the lead's customer_id or phone tail since enrolled_at; (2) stage advanced past 'contacted' (estimate_sent/presented/accepted) or 'lost'; (3) opted_out; (4) max_touches -> completed. WHY re-check at send time: a drip that texts a lead who replied an hour ago is the fastest way to look like a robot; the check runs in the same tick as the send, so the window is minutes, not days. The Quo STOP path now also flips leads.opted_out on the indexed phone_norm (the old customer-only patch missed pre-conversion leads, which have no customer row) and stops the active enrollment immediately; START clears the flag but never auto-resumes (re-entry is the human Enroll button).

DELIBERATE DESIGN CALLS (each documented in-code too):
- Consent reading of the "skip/stop" guardrail: opted_out stops the WHOLE enrollment (do-not-contact); sms_consent=false only SKIPS the SMS leg (ledger row 'skipped', email drip continues). Most leads arrive with sms_consent=false, so the literal stop-on-first-sms-step reading would gut the email sequence.
- Concurrency is CLAIM-FIRST: the conditional PATCH advancing next_step_index (guarded on current value + status=active) is atomic; the winner sends, the loser sees zero rows and walks. Double-send is impossible; a crash after claim loses at most one touch. Never-double-text beats never-lose-a-touch for marketing.
- Failure policy: AI-render or provider failure records 'failed' and the sequence continues at the NEXT step; the same rendered message is never auto-retried (non-idempotent-write discipline: a retry can double-send if the first landed).
- Quiet hours (8am-8pm America/Phoenix, fixed UTC-7): a LIVE step with an SMS leg due outside the window is deferred to the window open (whole step, so sms+email stay a pair); email-only steps send anytime; dry-run ignores quiet hours so review copy shows up promptly.
- CONTACT-COUNT DE-DUPE RULE: live drip legs mirror into pec_sms_log (kind 'drip') / pec_email_log (template_key 'drip') so conversation threads stay complete, and the Phase 1 counter DROPS those mirrors and counts pec_drip_sends status 'sent' instead (lead_id attribution beats phone/email matching). Dry-run and failed rows never count. contacted_at stamps only when null (write-once first-touch column; speed-to-lead depends on it) and only on a real send.
- AI copy: one Anthropic call per touch (renderCopyReal, same model default + textFromMessage discipline as pec-lead-ai). System prompt forbids invented prices/dates/warranties/facts/links and em dashes; scrubCopy strips dashes and links anyway and capSms hard-caps length. First drip SMS gets " Reply STOP to opt out." appended once (dry-run rows count toward "first" so review copy matches reality). Drip emails are deliberately personal-note plain (not the invoice chrome) with a human opt-out footer line; email replies are not machine-tracked (the replied switch reads sms/call logs), so that footer invites a reply staff acts on with Stop drip.
- Scoring/analysis still never send (grep-verified: no send calls in pec-lead-ai/pec-metrics-ai); drip copy is the one scoped auto-send exception, exactly as Dylan locked.

UI: admin-gated Drips view under Sales (master switch card with confirm-on-ON and one-click OFF, per-campaign dry_run/live + pause toggles with confirm-on-live, read-only step list, active-enrollment counts, recent-activity table with expandable message bodies). Lead detail: Drip card (Active: step X of N + next touch / Stopped: reason / Not enrolled) with Stop drip (guarded on status=active) and Enroll (blocked for opted-out leads); the ledger merges into the Activity timeline as drip_send pseudo-events, dry-run entries labeled "nothing sent". Board cards show a purple Drip chip on active enrollment.

VERIFIED: production/drip-runner.test.cjs, a 55-check fixture driving the REAL runDrips/enrollLead against a mini-PostgREST stub (the exact operators the engine uses, incl. the partial-unique 409) plus stubbed providers: master-off short-circuit, dry-run writes copy + never touches providers + never stamps contacted_at, every kill-switch (replied by text AND call, stage_advanced, contacted keeps dripping, lost, opted_out, max_touches), live happy path (sender resolution, STOP line once, ledger + mirror rows, provider ids, contacted_at write-once), quiet-hours deferral + email-only exemption + the quietHours math, consent skip on both/sms-only steps, AI + provider failure policy, the two-racing-runs double-send test (exactly one send per channel), paused campaign holds, enrollment + conflict + no-campaign no-op, scrubbers. 55/55. Also: node --check clean on all four touched/new .cjs; all 9 inline index.html script blocks parse; both production suites green (187 calculator + 142 estimate); whats-new.json validates; zero em dashes in customer-facing strings (drip copy is scrubbed in code). Env: the runner reuses ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, QUO_API_KEY, RESEND_API_KEY, SUPABASE_* already set in Netlify for the existing senders/AI; optional PEC_DRIP_AI_MODEL override; no new secret needed.

Why: Phase 2 of the leads-robustness plan (Dylan's ask scoped by Cowork 2026-07-19); Phase 3 (estimate/invoice drips on the same engine via kind, the manual blast tool, drip/blast metric cards in the Phase 1 placeholder) is NOT built.

By: Claude Code
Changed: Delivered claude-code-prompt-33-leads-pipeline-phase-1 (archived to docs/archive/prompts/). Three independent commits so any part can revert alone: Part A (15d37de) times-contacted on the board card + lead detail; Part B (290034b) Hot/Warm/Cold score badges + hot-first sort; Part C (ddc92db) Metrics chart redesign + outbound-touch stat card; plus this docs commit (What's New x3, features.json, prompt archive, log). NO migration, NO new index, NO prod data change; everything ships as code. Phases 2 (drip engine) and 3 (estimate/invoice drips, manual blast, drip/blast metric cards) are NOT built; a commented PHASE 3 SLOT sits in the Metrics Sales section where those cards will land.

CONTACT-COUNT MATCHING DECISION (Part A): computed CLIENT-SIDE from three narrow selects (pec_call_log direction=out, pec_sms_log direction=out excluding status failed, pec_email_log excluding failed), not a new aggregate query, because the logs are hundreds of rows total; that is why no index and no Cowork migration handoff exists. The one loader (loadOutboundTouchLogs) + one matcher (leadContactStats) are shared by the board, the lead detail, and the Metrics card. Matching per LOG ROW, attributed at most once: customer_id first, then normalized phone (the exact strip-non-digits last-10 rule of the stored leads.phone_norm/customers.phone_norm generated columns, mirrored client-side as contactPhoneNorm; the customer side of an outbound row is to_number/to_email), then email for the email log, so a row whose customer_id AND phone both point at the same lead can never double-count. WHY failed rows are excluded but no-answer calls are not: a failed send never left our system; a no-answer outbound call still shows the customer a missed call, so it is a real touch attempt. Last-contacted on the detail page is DERIVED from the max matched log timestamp, NOT leads.contacted_at, because that column is a first-touch stamp written once by the first stage move and never updated. Log-read failure renders NO chip rather than a false "Not contacted". leadContactStats has a marked PHASE 2 EXTENSION POINT where drip sends join the tally as a fourth source. Selects ride PostgREST's default 1000-row cap, fine at today's volumes; noted in-code to revisit with the Phase 2 drip engine.

HOW PART B WORKS: leadScoreBand/leadScoreBadge are now the ONE place the cutoffs live (hot 70+, warm 40-69, cold under 40, the same thresholds the old color-only number chip used); the badge carries the band WORD so meaning never rides on color alone. Board card, lead-detail header (badge beside the name, AI score_reason under it), and the AI panel all use the shared helper. The filter bar gains a Sort select (urgency default vs "AI score: hot first"), stored on state.leadsFilters like the other filters, applied in every column with unscored leads last and the default order as tiebreak, applied on change (a view preference, not a query filter). Scoring untouched: pec-lead-ai still runs only on intake and the detail Refresh button; nothing auto-sends.

HOW PART C WORKS: Chart.js was ALREADY integrated (lazy cdnjs load pinned at 4.4.1, CSS-bar fallback, three weekly charts upgraded, shipped in an earlier build), so Part C extends that path instead of adding the prompt's new script tag; no CSP exists in netlify.toml or index.html, so no header change either. Read the dataviz skill first per the prompt: every Metrics chart is single-series, so the brand accent is the single hue (no categorical palette, no legend needed), lines are 2px with a gradient-area wash and surface-ringed >=8px markers, bars cap at 24px with 4px rounded data-ends, gridlines are recessive hairlines, and chart text wears ink tokens read from the LIVE CSS variables at init (metricsChartInk), so charts stay legible under whichever skin is active rather than hard-coding light-mode hex. Speed-to-lead and price-per-sqft upgrade to gradient trend lines ($/sqft keeps its per-month drills; speed-to-lead never had drills); conversion by source gains a horizontal rate chart above its tables (tables stay as the full record and the no-CDN fallback). Sales volume, Revenue collected, and Jobs completed KPI cards get pure-SVG sparklines (gray trend, accent last segment per the stat-tile contract; SVG so they render even if the CDN fails); cards without an honest weekly series (avg job size, callback rate, invoice timing) deliberately get none. New Sales card "Outbound touches": avg touches to win (touches stamped on or before accepted_at) and to estimate out (estimate_sent_at, the closest thing to "booked"), plus open leads never contacted; zero-touch milestone leads are excluded from the averages because the logs only reach back to the Quo integration (a data gap, not a zero-touch win), and a not-enough-data state shows when nothing qualifies. No metric's meaning or computation changed; openMetricsDrill and pec-metrics-ai untouched; drill modals still go through openModal/#pecModalRoot only.

## [2026-07-17 MST] Invoicing: batch change-order approval (2+ pending COs = one link, one page, one signature)
By: Claude Code
Changed: Delivered claude-code-prompt-31-batch-change-order-approval. When a job has 2 or more pending (unsigned) change orders, they now go out as ONE approval request: one stable link per job (/co/batch/<token>), one stacked page, one typed-name + drawn signature that approves all of them. With exactly 0 or 1 pending CO, everything renders and behaves byte-for-byte like before (per-CO link, page, badges, Email/Text/Copy/View). Delivery and signature UX only: billing still hits jobs.price and the invoice at CO save, and unsigned COs never block billing.

HOW IT WORKS (four pieces):
1. New table pec_change_order_batches (migration supabase/migrations/2026-07-17_change_order_batches.sql, NOT yet applied, Cowork applies). One row per approval request: job_id, unique token, status pending/signed, the signature fields (signed_name, signature_data data URL, signed_at, signer_ip, signer_user_agent), and signed_co_ids uuid[]. A PARTIAL UNIQUE index (one pending batch per job) is what makes the link stable: the dashboard card get-or-creates the job's pending batch and every send reuses its token. Signed batches accumulate as history; a later pair of new COs mints a fresh pending batch. pec_change_order_signatures gains a nullable batch_id FK so a batch-signed CO points at the row holding its signature. RLS mirrors the sibling table: staff FOR ALL via is_admin_staff(), NO anon policy, the public signing write goes through the service-role function only.
2. The batch row stores NO snapshot of which COs it covers at creation, on purpose: the link is LIVE (Dylan decision 4). The public page renders whatever COs are pending at view time, so a CO added after the link was texted simply appears on the next open. The covered set is captured AT SIGN TIME: the sign POST re-reads the job's pending COs, writes their ids into signed_co_ids, and flips exactly those rows. A CO signed some other way in the meantime is excluded by its own status=eq.pending guard; a CO added seconds before the click is included.
3. New public page netlify/functions/pec-public-change-order-batch.cjs at /co/batch/<token> plus POST /api/co/batch/sign (netlify.toml rules added ABOVE /co/*, which matters: Netlify takes the first matching redirect and /co/* would otherwise swallow the batch path and treat "batch/<uuid>" as a single-CO token). Server-rendered static HTML, noindex, brand-styled and printable like the single-CO page. Pending render: each pending CO as its own stacked section (title, scope, system + sqft, its own price), already-signed COs greyed as read-only "already approved" context, a grand total of what the signature covers, one signature block. Signed render: the signed document (exactly the covered set from signed_co_ids, the one signature block, their grand total). Signing is verify-then-write with NO blind retry (payment-path discipline): the batch PATCH carries status=eq.pending and is checked for an actual row transition (return=representation), so a replay or double-click gets 409 and can never overwrite a signature. If the follow-up CO flip fails after the batch row landed, the endpoint still returns ok (the signature of record exists and a customer retry would only hit a confusing 409) and logs the batch id + CO ids loudly for staff.
4. Card (mountChangeOrderCard, both surfaces: Invoicing detail and job-detail Estimate): with 2+ pending, the pending boxes collapse into one batch box listing every pending CO as a line (own price each) with the grand total in the footer and ONE action row (Copy batch link / Email batch / Text batch / View, wired via new data-co-batch-* attributes; the per-CO data-co-* contract is untouched and still serves the signed boxes below). CO numbering stays the created_at position across ALL rows, so #N never renumbers when a CO moves between the batch box and the signed list. A batch-signed CO's badge works unchanged because the sign endpoint stamps signed_name/signed_at on each covered CO row; the drawn signature image lives only on the batch (decision 9). Sends reuse pecSendEmail (log_template_key change_order) and pecSendSms (kind change_order with a new co_batch_token input the function resolves to N pending + live grand total + the one link), so the prompt-9 Last-invoiced predicate (compose/invoice keys, sms kind invoice) never counts a batch send. Pre-migration the batch table probe fails, the card falls back to today's per-CO boxes with a one-line note, and nothing breaks.

VERIFIED: node --check clean on pec-public-change-order-batch.cjs and pec-send-sms.cjs; all 8 inline index.html script blocks parse clean (module-aware extraction, importmap validated as JSON); help/whats-new.json validates (new entry batch-change-order-approval); zero em dashes in the diff. Plus a 28-check fixture driving the REAL batch handler against a stubbed Supabase REST layer: pending page stacks both COs with per-CO prices, pending-only grand total, greyed already-approved context, and exactly one sign form; garbage token 404s; missing name / bad signature 400; happy-path sign returns signed=2, captures exactly the pending set into signed_co_ids, stores drawing + audit fields on the batch, flips both COs with batch_id + name/date but NO drawing on the CO rows, and leaves the previously signed CO untouched; both PATCHes carry their status=eq.pending guards; a replay gets 409 without overwriting the signature; the signed page renders exactly the covered set with the one signature block, the approved total, no sign form, and the print button. 28/28 pass.

Why: Dylan's feedback ("if there are multiple change orders, bunch them together so they can get sent for approval all at once"), scoped by Cowork 2026-07-16 through 12 locked decisions (see the 2026-07-16 Cowork scoping entry below).
Files touched: index.html, netlify.toml, netlify/functions/pec-public-change-order-batch.cjs (new), netlify/functions/pec-send-sms.cjs, supabase/migrations/2026-07-17_change_order_batches.sql (new), help/whats-new.json, PROJECT-LOG.md

## [2026-07-16 MST] Settings: product cost basis is now explicit (per gal/box/pack vs per kit)
By: Claude Code
Changed: Delivered claude-code-prompt-30-product-cost-basis. Feature commit 37d86a9 (index.html, help/whats-new.json, plus the prompt file), this docs commit. Labels-and-input-only change: NO cost value, calculator math, costing snapshot, or historical pec_prod_material_lines row changed, and no migration was needed (unit_cost was already stored per kit and stays the canonical value).

HOW IT WORKS (the two-field editor): the product editor now shows "Cost per gal/box/pack" (new input pmCostUnit) next to "Cost per kit" (the existing pmCost input, id kept so the save path and validation are untouched). Typing in either fills the other live using the current Kit size (per-kit = per-unit x kit size, per-unit = per-kit / kit size, both rounded to 2 decimals). Changing Kit size re-syncs anchored on whichever cost field was edited last; if neither was touched, it re-derives per-unit from the stored per-kit, so opening and saving an unchanged product round-trips the exact same unit_cost. A blank or 0 kit size makes the sync a no-op (no divide-by-zero) and the existing "Kit size must be > 0" save validation catches it. Only the per-kit field is persisted to unit_cost; the per-unit number is derived, never stored (no new column). The unit word (gal/box/pack) comes from unitFor, which was hoisted out of renderProducts to shared scope so the modal can use it too, and it now updates live when the material type changes (the spread rate label follows the same unit). For dry goods with kit size 1 the two fields simply mirror each other. One small bug caught during self-review: a NEW product's placeholder unit_cost is an empty string, which passed a null-only check and would have prefilled the per-unit field with 0; guarded explicitly.

LABELS (basis now stated everywhere cost or kit quantity shows, values untouched): product table Cost / Kit cell now reads "$165 / kit" with a muted derived "$55 / gal" beneath it (dash when cost is null, hidden when kit size is 0); the toolbar note states that cost per kit is what job costing uses and either number can be entered in the editor. Costing screens: the unified job costing material table headers are now Qty (kits), Order Qty (kits), Unit $ / kit, Actual Used (kits); the Actual Used input STAYS in kits (fractional allowed) per the locked decision, only its header changed. Same kit wording applied to the older costing modal's Material Lines table, the job-card materials table, the Material Pull table, the "+ Add material" modal (Quantity (kits), Unit $ / kit), and the Ordering lines table (Qty (kits), Unit cost / kit, plus its custom-blend tooltip and footnote now say per-kit).

VERIFIED: both suites pass (187 calculator, 142 estimate), all 7 inline script blocks parse clean via node --check (module-aware; the importmap block validated as JSON), help/whats-new.json validates (new entry product-cost-basis-per-unit-vs-per-kit), no em dashes in any new text. Plus a 10-check fixture that drives the REAL sync block extracted from index.html through fake DOM inputs: 55/gal x kit 3 fills 165/kit and back, rounding to 2 decimals, kit-size changes anchor on the last-edited cost field (and on per-kit when untouched), blank/0 kit size is a no-op, clearing one field mirrors blank, and an unedited product's per-kit value round-trips byte-for-byte. 10/10 pass.

Why: Dylan reported the Settings product cost field could be read as either price per kit or price per gallon with no label saying which, risking under-costed jobs (a per-gallon number in a per-kit field divides the real cost by the kit size); scoped by Cowork with locked decisions (two-field editor, per-kit stays canonical and stored, costing math and Actual Used kits basis unchanged, history frozen).

## [2026-07-16 MST] Estimator: Zip field no longer renders off-screen on desktop
By: Claude Code
Changed: Delivered claude-code-prompt-29. One commit, fbb71ee, a 2-property CSS fix in apps/estimator/src/styles.css. Build passes (tsc plus vite).

ROOT CAUSE (how it works, for future reference): the estimator's base `select, input` rule set no width, so every text input kept the browser's intrinsic default width (roughly 20 characters, about 150px). CSS grid items default to `min-width: auto`, which means a grid track cannot shrink below its content's intrinsic width. On desktop the customer card is only half the viewport (`.cols` goes two-column at 760px), so the City / State / Zip row (`.cust-csz`, tracks 2fr 1fr 1fr) needed three ~150px minimums plus gaps, more than the card had. The row overflowed rightward and Zip was pushed past the card edge. On a phone the card is full width, so the three minimums fit, which is exactly why Dylan saw it on desktop only.

THE FIX: `width: 100%` on the base `select, input` rule (inputs now fill their field instead of asserting an intrinsic width, matching what `.custom-scope` and `.addr-ac input` already did), and `min-width: 0` on `.field` (so any field inside a grid row can shrink below its input's intrinsic width). Applied to `.field` generally rather than only `.cust-csz .field` because `width: 100%` now applies to inputs in every grid row (.slots, .wo-grid, .addon-nums, .area-top), and they all share the same intrinsic-minimum failure mode. The checkbox overrides (`.area-mvb input`, `.check input`) are later and more specific, so checkboxes keep their fixed 1rem size.

VERIFIED IN BROWSER (static fixture with the real built CSS and the exact customer-card markup, measured with getBoundingClientRect): at desktop width the old CSS put Zip's right edge 101px past the card edge; with the fix, every input row (.cust-csz, .area-top, .slots, .wo-grid, .addon-nums) sits fully inside its card at both desktop and 390px phone width, with no horizontal page scroll. No dashboard What's New entry: this changelog is for index.html, and the estimator is a separate app.

Why: Dylan reported the Zip field rendering partly off-screen on desktop; scoped by Cowork 2026-07-16 (prompt 29).
Files touched: apps/estimator/src/styles.css, PROJECT-LOG.md
Next steps: Deploy as usual; the estimator build output regenerates on deploy (repo-root /estimator is gitignored).

## [2026-07-16 MST] Build 28: personal To-dos (private per-user checklist in the left nav)
By: Claude Code
Changed: Delivered claude-code-prompt-28. Two commits: 1f58375 (new migration, WRITTEN not applied) and d7c7f3f (nav + view + What's New), plus this docs commit. Touched index.html, help/whats-new.json, and ONE new migration supabase/migrations/2026-07-16_personal_todos.sql. Both suites pass (187 calculator, 142 estimate), all inline script blocks parse clean, whats-new.json validates, no em dashes in the new text.

THE SHAPE. New table pec_user_todos (id, admin_user_id FK admin_users on delete cascade, body, done, created_at, done_at) with RLS ON and OWNER-ONLY policies for all four verbs, mirroring exactly how user_permissions and pec_whats_new_acks map the signed-in auth.uid() to the admin_users row. There is deliberately NO admin-wide policy: an admin signed into the app sees only their own list, same as everyone else. The UPDATE policy carries both using AND with check so a user cannot re-home a row to another user. The client filter .eq('admin_user_id', me) is belt-and-suspenders; the RLS is the actual privacy boundary.

THE VIEW. A To-dos button joins the Overview flyout in #pecSubnav (the prompt said "top-level Menu group"; since build 19 the sidebar is an icon-per-group rail where EVERY destination lives inside a group flyout, Overview is the top group and the closest faithful mapping, and the page title picks up "To-dos" automatically from the active button text). No pec-role-admin class and no capability gate, so every signed-in user sees it. switchView routes todos -> renderTodos. The view reads the current user's rows on entry (withFreshSession, newest first), renders open items on top and completed ones struck through under a Completed divider, and re-enters renderTodos after every successful mutation so the DB stays the single source of truth. Empty state: "No to-dos yet. Add one above." A failed read degrades to a short "Couldn't load your to-dos" note and never breaks the shell (which also covers the deploy-before-migration window). In-band PostgREST errors are checked on every read AND write, the build-26 lesson.

WRITE-WRAPPER CHOICE (one deliberate deviation from the prompt): the prompt said withFreshWriteRetry for writes, but an INSERT is an accumulating write, and the standing rule from the payment path (CLAUDE.md gotchas) is that a blind recover-and-retry can double-record if the first request actually landed. So Add uses plain withFreshWrite (bounded, no retry, clean toast on a stale session), while toggle (full-value update to the same values) and delete (re-deleting a gone row is a no-op) are idempotent and use withFreshWriteRetry as the prompt asked. A duplicate to-do would be low stakes, but the codebase rule exists precisely so nobody has to re-derive the stakes per call site.

BADGE: skipped, per the prompt's "only if trivial" clause. It is not trivial here: the rail hides destinations inside flyouts, so a live open-count badge would need its own pec_user_todos query on every auth render plus new railSync plumbing, for a number the user sees the moment the view opens.

RLS VERIFICATION NOTE (prompt acceptance): a service-role query (Supabase Studio SQL editor, MCP tools) BYPASSES RLS and sees every user's rows, so seeing all rows there proves nothing about privacy. The real check is two AUTHENTICATED sessions: user A adds items, user B opens To-dos and must see none of them, and vice versa. This note also lives in the migration's footer comment for Cowork.

Why: Dylan wants a personal to-do list; scoped by Cowork 2026-07-16 (prompt 28, decisions: every user private, nav item + dedicated view, simple checklist, DB-backed and synced, no due dates or reminders).

## [2026-07-16 MST] Build 27: bell notifications are clickable and route to their source (costing notifications land on the job's costing view)
By: Claude Code
Changed: Delivered claude-code-prompt-27. Two commits: 05c4608 (new migration, WRITTEN not applied) and 29ddd8e (client routing + What's New), plus this docs commit. Touched index.html, help/whats-new.json, and ONE new migration supabase/migrations/2026-07-16_notification_targets.sql. Both suites pass (187 calculator, 142 estimate), all 8 inline script blocks parse clean, no em dashes in the new text.

THE SHAPE. A notification row can now say WHERE a click lands, not just carry a public.jobs id: two new columns on pec_notifications, target_view ('jobs' | 'costing' | 'invoicing') and target_id (the id to open in that view). Why target_id has NO foreign key: which table it references depends on target_view (costing ids live on pec_prod_jobs, jobs/invoicing ids on public.jobs), and one FK cannot point at two tables; a dangling id just renders the view's normal not-found state. The old job_id column and every old row keep working untouched.

WHY COSTING WAS NEVER CLICKABLE (the root of Anne's complaint): pec_notifications.job_id FKs public.jobs, but costing jobs are pec_prod_jobs rows (the parallel table, see CLAUDE.md). The costing RPCs left the link off ON PURPOSE because there was no column that could legally hold a pec_prod_jobs id. target_view/target_id is that column pair. log_costing_submitted and log_costing_sent_back gain p_job_id (default null) and write target_view='costing'; signature changes, so the migration DROPS the old single-overload functions first (create-or-replace would have left an ambiguous overload PostgREST refuses to dispatch; confirmed live that exactly one overload of each exists today).

CLIENT ROUTING. One resolver, notifTarget(n), decides per row: explicit target wins (costing -> openUnifiedJobId + switchView('costing'), invoicing -> openInvoiceJobId, jobs -> openJobId), legacy job_id falls back to today's job-card behavior, anything unresolvable renders as plain text. Permission rule: a costing target only resolves for users holding can_view_job_costing (the same capability that shows the nav button), so a user without it sees the sent-back text but cannot tap into a blocked view. The pointer cursor and nav data attributes now key on the resolved target, not on job_id.

DEPLOY ORDER CANNOT BREAK IT (both directions, the build-26 lesson applied): if the client deploys before the migration, loadNotifications retries with the legacy column list when the target columns 400 the select (a missing column fails the WHOLE PostgREST query, in-band, no throw), and both costing callers retry the RPC with the legacy argument shape, so the bell stays lit and no notification is lost. If the migration lands first, the old deployed client calls the new functions through their p_job_id default. Still, apply the migration first; only then do new rows carry targets.

PRODUCER AUDIT (which types route where, and why):
- costing_submitted / costing_sent_back: target_view='costing' via the updated RPCs. The whole point of the build.
- payment_edited: was completely non-clickable (it never wrote job_id despite having p_job_id in scope); now writes target_view='invoicing' so the click opens the invoice, which is where payments live. payment_deleted: same invoicing target added, and it keeps writing job_id so old clients still get the legacy job-card click.
- portal_view / colors_confirmed / colors_collision: DELIBERATELY untouched. They already write job_id, and the job card is their sensible destination, which the legacy path already serves. Redefining portal_set_area_colors would mean copying its 100+ line collision function for zero behavior change (drift risk for nothing).
- customer_deleted: DELIBERATELY text-only. The customer is gone; there is nowhere sensible to land.
Delivery is unchanged per Dylan's decision 3: badge only, no realtime toast.

Why: Dylan's report that Anne cannot click a costing send-back notification; scoped by Cowork 2026-07-16 (prompt 27, entry below).

## [2026-07-16 MST] Build 26: last-sent column fixed (phantom created_at column, not RLS) + Communication history panel on the invoice page
By: Claude Code
Changed: Delivered both parts of claude-code-prompt-26. Two feature commits, b967671 (Part A read fix) and 9e26286 (Part B panel + What's New), plus this docs commit. Touched index.html and help/whats-new.json only. NO migration and NO prod DB change: the leading RLS hypothesis turned out to be wrong, the fix is pure client code. Both test suites pass (187 calculator, 142 estimate), all 8 inline script blocks parse clean, whats-new.json validates.

ROOT CAUSE (Part A, confirmed against live prod before editing, per the bug workflow). The last-sent read in renderInvoicing selected three columns from pec_email_log: job_id, sent_at, created_at. But pec_email_log has NO created_at column (sent_at is its only timestamp; it is the SMS log that uses created_at, and the query was written as if both tables shared that shape). Asking PostgREST for a column that does not exist fails the WHOLE query with a 400. Here is the part that made it invisible: supabase-js does not throw on a query error, it resolves normally with the error tucked inside the response object. The read was wrapped in try/catch with a console.warn, but the catch never fired because nothing was thrown, and the next line mapped any errored response to an empty list by design. So every render, for every job, the email history quietly came back as nothing. The SMS side of the read was schema-correct but prod has ZERO outbound invoice texts (56 sms rows, none with kind=invoice going out), so no job ever got a date from either source. That is exactly Dylan's symptom: only "never sent" or a dash, forever.

HYPOTHESES RULED OUT with service-role queries on prod (zdfpzmmrgotynrwkeakd): (1) RLS/grants, the leading hypothesis: both tables have their staff SELECT policy (pec_email_log_read / pec_sms_log_read, qual is_admin_staff()) and the authenticated grant, and the Settings > Email tab already reads pec_email_log successfully with select('*'), which also explains why THAT log always worked while the invoicing column never did (select star cannot name a missing column). (2) Write-side data: Dan Patterson's 2026-07-16 row exists and is perfect (job ace46017, template_key compose, status delivered, sent 14:48 UTC = 7:48 AM Phoenix). (3) URL length from .in(job_ids): moot once the real 400 was in hand, and the fix keeps the same batched shape.

THE FIX (Part A): the select now asks only for job_id and sent_at, the dead created_at fallback in the timestamp loop is gone, and both reads now console.warn when the RESPONSE carries an in-band error (not just when something throws). Why the warns matter: the silent error-to-empty-list mapping is the reason this bug shipped invisible; degrade stays graceful (the page never breaks) but a broken read now says so in the console.

THE PANEL (Part B): a Communication history card sits under Payments on the invoice detail page (renderJobInvoice). It merges two batched reads for the open job, invoice emails (pec_email_log, template_key compose or invoice) and invoice texts (pec_sms_log, kind invoice, direction out), into one newest-first table: Phoenix date+time, channel, recipient, subject or text preview, status, and which staff member sent it. Same filter contract as the list column so the two surfaces can never disagree, with ONE deliberate difference per Dylan's decision: the panel also shows failed attempts, labeled in red with the error message. Estimate and change-order emails stay excluded on purpose (they log under their own template keys precisely so invoice features skip them). How the pieces reuse existing plumbing: sender names come from qoStaffNames (the cached auth-uid to name map the Messages inbox already uses), status colors match the Settings email log (red for failed/bounced/complained, green for delivered/opened/clicked, muted otherwise), and times go through a new module-scope phxDateTime helper that uses the same fixed UTC-7 shift as invToday/phxDay (Phoenix has no DST, so the constant offset is always right). Delivery statuses are already richer than sent/failed: the Resend webhook (pec-webhook-resend.cjs) upgrades rows, and prod holds 20 delivered / 2 sent / 1 failed today, so the panel shows real delivery states from day one. Empty state and a couldn't-load degrade note per the prompt; a code comment marks the phase-2 seam where customer "viewed" rows will merge in once pec-public-invoice records views (explicitly out of scope this build). Small companion fix: sending a TEXT invoice now re-renders the invoice page the way the email path already did, so the panel picks up the send immediately.

Why: Dylan's Dan Patterson report, scoped by Cowork into prompt 26 (entry below).
Files touched: index.html, help/whats-new.json, PROJECT-LOG.md.
Next steps: deploy; no migration to wait on.

## Handoff to Dylan
Good news, the fix needed no database change, so there is nothing to wait on Cowork for: deploy and it lights up. Plain English on what was wrong: every send WAS being recorded correctly (your Dan Patterson email is in the log, and Resend even confirmed it delivered). The list page just asked the database for a timestamp column that does not exist on the email log table, the database rejected the whole question, and the code treated the rejection as "no sends found" without telling anyone. After the deploy: (1) open Invoicing and confirm completed jobs you have invoiced show real dates in the last-sent column ("never sent" should now only mean truly never sent); (2) open Dan Patterson's invoice and scroll down to Communication history: you should see his Jul 16, 2026, 7:48 AM email to dpatterson@unacem-na.com, subject "Invoice 2925460 from Prescott Epoxy Company", status delivered, sent by you.

By: Cowork

The Email invoice button (index.html:9609-9684) sends in compose mode and pec-send-email.cjs writes pec_email_log on success with status 'sent', the job_id, and template_key 'compose' (pec-send-email.cjs:255-257), using the service-role key (bypasses RLS). By: Claude Code

The estimator app (apps/estimator) needed zero changes: it never read the pairings table.

THE SHAPE. The flake-to-basecoat pairing stops being its own table-with-a-tab and becomes ONE field on the flake product: default_basecoat_product_id on pec_prod_products, edited as a "Default basecoat" dropdown that appears in the product modal only when the material type is Flake. The standalone Color Pairings tab is retired (Catalog nav is now Products / System Types / Add-ons, with a fallback so a stale saved tab value can never render a dead tab). pec_prod_color_pairings is NOT dropped; it sits dead in the DB so this is reversible.

ONE MAP BUILDER, FIVE CALL SITES. The defaultBasecoatByFlake map (flake id to basecoat id) was being built inline from pairings in five places: the change-order modal, the job detail page, the work order, Job Costing, and the production module's catalog helper. All five now call one shared helper, flakeBasecoatDefaults(products), canonical in production/calculator.js and mirrored on window in index.html (same bridge pattern as computeMaterialPlan). How it works: the helper walks the product rows and keeps Flake rows that carry default_basecoat_product_id, so the map's SOURCE moved from the pairings table to the product column while every consumer downstream (the ~12100 auto-fill, computeMaterialPlan's area resolution, costing estimates) is byte-identical. Why one helper instead of five inline loops: the five loops were already drifting bait, and a source change like this is exactly when a sixth copy would have been missed. Rep-facing behavior is unchanged: picking a flake still auto-fills its basecoat, quartz still gets a manual per-job basecoat pick (no pairing field on quartz, per Dylan).

REQUIRED BASECOAT ON SAVE. A Flake product cannot be saved without a default basecoat. The gate is flakeProductSaveError(payload) (canonical + tested in calculator.js, mirrored on window): returns "Pick a default basecoat for this flake color." for a Flake with no basecoat, null otherwise, with "Special Order Flake" exempt BY NAME (its whole point is a per-job pick). Existing flakes are grandfathered automatically because the rule only runs on save. The dropdown lists active basecoats (Special Order placeholders excluded) and quietly appends the currently-saved basecoat if it has since gone inactive, so editing an old flake never silently drops its pairing. Prod audit (Cowork, 2026-07-16): 20 of 23 real flakes backfill 1:1 from their default pairing; the 3 placeholder flakes with no pairing stay empty on purpose.

REQUIRES FLAGS REMOVED, SLOTS ARE TRUTH. The system modal's "Requires flake / Requires basecoat" toggles are gone, along with requires_flake_color / requires_basecoat_color in the payload and every read in the file. The estimator's color pickers now derive PURELY from recipe slots (sysHasSlot): a Flake slot means the system needs a flake, and so on. Why this is safe: the pickers already derived from slots, with the flags only as a legacy OR fallback, so this was a fallback removal, not a rewrite. The one divergence is the INACTIVE "Grind and Seal - Urethane" (flag set, zero slots), which would lose its basecoat picker; irrelevant while inactive, and the fix if ever reactivated is to add a Basecoat slot. The DB columns stay (dead, reversible).

SYSTEM TYPES COLLAPSE. Every system now renders as one compact row: drag handle, chevron, name, (inactive) marker, and a read-only pricing summary (Target GP / Labor / Materials %, dash when unset), plus Edit. Clicking the row expands the recipe-slots table and + Add slot; clicking again collapses. Expanded ids live in state.expandedSystemTypes (an in-memory Set, starts empty so everything begins collapsed) so a re-render after a slot edit keeps the row open. The drag handle and Edit button are excluded from the click-to-toggle, so reorder and Edit behave exactly as before; pricing stays editable only in the Edit modal.

DEPLOY ORDER MATTERS. The product-modal save now always writes default_basecoat_product_id, so if the deploy beats the migration every product save fails on an unknown column. Cowork applies the migration FIRST, then Dylan deploys (same discipline as build 24).

## [2026-07-15 MST] Build 25 phase 3: live proposal panel in the estimator (auto-first AI write, then manual Regenerate)
By: Claude Code
Changed: Delivered build prompt 25 phase 3 (live in-module proposal for STANDARD estimates). Three commits: 0b4b694 (save/load plumbing), ab9cd46 (the live panel + trigger logic), a23a40b (estimate-page stale banner + What's New), plus this docs commit, pushed to main per Dylan's mid-session "git push all" (the build-24 migration was confirmed applied by Cowork first, so the push is safe). Touched apps/estimator/src (EstimatorScreen, offline/estimates.ts, lib/estimateLoad.ts), index.html (two small scope-card touches), production/estimate15b.test.js, help/whats-new.json. NO migration (reuses scope_of_work, scope_edited_at, scope_stale, scope_answers exactly as the prompt expected). NO change to pec-estimate-scope.cjs: the assembly-not-authorship contract and the never-overwrite/force rule are untouched; this build only moves WHERE and WHEN the existing writer is called. 142 tests pass (134 before, 8 new assertions), estimator builds clean (tsc + vite).

THE SHAPE. A "Proposal / Scope of work" card sits right under "Finish the scope" in the estimator (standard mode only; custom mode has its own typed scope from build 24). It is one editable textarea whose text has three owners, in precedence order: the rep's hand-edits, the server-assembled document, and (before either exists) an instant LOCAL template preview. The preview is assembled client-side from the same pieces the server uses (scope_template / scope_template_mvb per area, add-on scope_snippets, the shared production/scope.cjs applyAnswers), in the same document shape (## line label + body, --- separators), so what Dylan watches build IS the proposal, just before the model's fact substitution (sqft, stem walls is/is-not, flake color) has run. Unanswered questions show the literal word BLANK on purpose, same as today, with a red note.

AUTO-FIRST, THEN MANUAL (Dylan's locked trigger decision: cost + never clobber edits). The one automatic generation happens on the save where the estimate has scope templates, every BLANK question is answered, and no document exists yet; the panel shows the polished result the moment it lands (the old fire-and-forget triggerScope became generateScope, which also reads the response instead of dropping it). After that, saves NEVER regenerate: they flip scope_stale (new: also for machine-written text, since "the estimate moved under the document" is now possible), the panel shows a stale warning, and the "Regenerate proposal" button is the only writer. Regenerate saves first when the form has unsaved changes (so the doc always re-assembles from what the rep is looking at), asks the exact "this replaces your edited text" confirm the estimate page asks when the scope was hand-edited, and only then sends force=true. Same endpoint, same force semantics, both pages, zero duplicated generation logic.

EDIT SAFETY (both directions). Typing in the panel marks the text edited; the next save carries it via a new saveEstimateOffline arg (editedScope) that writes scope_of_work + scope_edited_at + scope_stale=false in ONE row write, the identical lock custom mode and the estimate page's "Save text" use. So a panel edit is protected by the server's existing 409-without-force rule even against a buggy caller. Two session flags, deliberately separate: panelEdited (this session's words must ride the next save) vs dbScopeEdited (force/stale semantics for text edited earlier or elsewhere); collapsing them would either re-stamp scope_edited_at on every save (wrongly clearing staleness) or drop edits.

OFFLINE. The panel's local preview works fully offline with a note that the polished proposal writes itself once online; that note is now literally true in-session: an offline save parks the estimate id in a ref and the existing reconnect-drain effect fires the owed generation right after the outbox lands the rows. If the app was closed before reconnecting, the estimate page's Generate button covers it, as before.

ESTIMATE PAGE SYNC (task 3). Both UIs read/write the same columns and call the same function. Two index.html touches: the stale banner now also renders for a stale MACHINE-written scope (previously impossible, so it only handled the edited case; without this the estimate page would silently show an out-of-date doc), and the "runs automatically on save" copy now says it runs on the estimator's FIRST save once the scope questions are answered.

WORTH KNOWING (pre-existing, unchanged, now more visible): re-saving a brand-new estimate in the same full-page session mints a NEW estimate row (saveEstimateOffline only reuses an id when editing via ?estimate_id). The live panel invites iterate-and-resave, so this wart will surface more; fixing it means an in-place child rewrite for same-session saves, which is unsafe while rows sit in the offline outbox, so it was deliberately NOT bolted onto this build. Flagging for a future prompt.

Why: build prompt 25 (Dylan + Cowork, 2026-07-15), phase 3 of the estimator fine-tune; phases 1 and 2 are live and their migrations applied.

## [2026-07-15 MST] Build 24 phase 2: estimator custom estimate mode (typed scope + price, optional AI polish)
By: Claude Code
Changed: Delivered all of build prompt 24 phase 2 (custom estimate mode). Two feature commits (f3469fd schema + save/reload, 4e92498 custom-mode UI + polish endpoint) plus this docs commit. Touched apps/estimator/src (EstimatorScreen, offline/estimates.ts, lib/estimateLoad.ts, styles.css), new netlify/functions/pec-estimate-custom-polish.cjs, production/estimate15b.test.js, help/whats-new.json, one new migration. Migration WRITTEN but NOT applied (do-not-touch-prod); Cowork handoff below. 134 tests pass (119 before, 15 new assertions in 2 new sections), estimator builds clean (tsc + vite), node --check clean.

THE SHAPE. A Standard/Custom segmented toggle sits at the top of the estimator (same visual language as the Residential/Commercial toggle). Custom turns the WHOLE estimate custom: the areas/systems flow, the "Finish the scope" questions, the More detail panel, comps, and the AI price read all hide (they are template/engine concepts), and in their place Dylan gets a large "Scope of work" textarea plus one manually typed Price input. Customer card, salesperson, and add-ons/one-offs stay, so a custom job can still carry add-on lines. Three additive columns on estimates (2026-07-16_estimate_custom_mode.sql): is_custom, custom_scope, custom_price.

HOW THE ENGINE STAYS OUT OF THE WAY (one branch, not many). The computeEstimatePricing memo returns null when isCustom, so everything downstream of `pricing` (hasPrice, finalSell, GP, the sell/discount override, the AI-read effect) goes dormant off that ONE null instead of each guarding isCustom separately. A new `sellPrice` is the typed custom price when custom, else the existing finalSell; totals build from it. GP is shown as not-applicable (there is no material or labor cost basis for the custom work, and a made-up GP would be worse than none); commission IS computed (standard pct of the total, which is well-defined). canSave in custom mode = salesperson + customer identity (last name or company, phase 1's gate) + custom_price > 0. No areas, no materials, no calculated price required. The toggle is NON-destructive: hidden area/answer state survives a round-trip, which is also how the calculator stays "optionally available" per Dylan's decision (price in Standard, note the number, switch to Custom).

COMPOSITION (the reason no downstream reader changed). Same safety-net pattern as build 23's customer_name/customer_address: the custom truth composes the standard columns on every save. custom_price rides estimates.price (plus included add-on lines) so the estimate list, the proposal page total, the PDF, and accept-to-job all read the right number; custom_scope is written to scope_of_work, the exact column the accept path already copies to jobs.scope and into the crew notes on pec_prod_jobs. One composed line item (label "Custom scope of work") carries the typed price + scope so pec-public-estimate and the PDF render a row; the edit loader filters that line back OUT of the add-on forms by label (it is regenerated from custom_scope/custom_price on every save, exactly like system lines are regenerated from areas). system_type_id is written NULL on a custom estimate (the column is nullable and every reader tolerates it; writing the dominant system would attribute revenue to a system the job does not have). Verified by reading the actual readers: renderEstimates (blank System cell), renderEstimateDetail (empty areas array), scopeRowsHtml/customerDisplay on the public page, and ensureJobCreated (guards `if (areas.length)`).

THE SCOPE-OVERWRITE TRAP (worth remembering). The estimator normally fires pec-estimate-scope after save, and the estimate page has Generate/Regenerate buttons. If a custom estimate carried catalog add-ons with scope snippets, a generate would ASSEMBLE a doc from just those snippets and clobber Dylan's typed scope. Two defenses, both riding EXISTING rails: custom saves never trigger triggerScope, and the save stamps scope_edited_at, which is the never-overwrite lock pec-estimate-scope already enforces server-side (409 without force). So the typed text is protected by the same rule that protects hand-edited scopes, with zero new server logic.

POLISH, NOT AUTHORSHIP. New pec-estimate-custom-polish.cjs: pure text in, text out (no estimate row read or written; nothing persists until Dylan saves). The system prompt orders the rules: preserve meaning and every exclusion, keep dollar figures/quantities/dates verbatim, fix only grammar/structure/formatting, never add scope, warranties, or cure-time claims, no em dashes. Same auth (badSecret or Supabase JWT), same textFromMessage lesson (never index content[0]), same 25s abort, same PEC_SCOPE_AI_MODEL env as the scope writer. The button never fires automatically, disables offline, and keeps the pre-polish text for a one-click "Undo polish".

Why: build prompt 24 phase 2 (Dylan + Cowork, 2026-07-15). Phase 1 (split customer fields) shipped and its migrations are applied, so the save/reload paths this touches were the landed ones. Phase 3 (live AI proposal writer for STANDARD estimates) is a separate prompt and its triggerScope behavior was deliberately untouched.

## [2026-07-15 MST] Build 23 phase 1: estimator split customer/company/address + Google address autocomplete
By: Claude Code
Changed: Delivered all of build prompt 23 phase 1 (estimator customer restructure). Three feature commits (7a52047 migrations, 02a8afe estimator UI, 49020ad downstream readers) plus this docs commit. Touched apps/estimator/src (EstimatorScreen, lead.ts, estimateLoad.ts, offline/estimates.ts, styles.css, new customer.ts / places.ts / AddressAutocomplete.tsx), netlify/functions/pec-public-estimate.cjs, index.html (one detail row), production/estimate15b.test.js, help/whats-new.json, two new migrations. Migrations WRITTEN but NOT applied (do-not-touch-prod); Cowork handoff below. 119 tests pass, estimator builds clean, node --check clean.

THE SHAPE. The customer card is now a Residential/Commercial toggle (residential = first + last name, commercial = company required + optional contact person; "commercial" IS "has a company", so switching to Residential visibly clears the company and the two facts can never disagree) over a split address (Address 1, Address 2, City, State, Zip). Nine additive columns on estimates (2026-07-15_estimate_customer_fields.sql). The old customer_name / customer_address columns are KEPT and recomposed on EVERY save inside saveEstimateOffline (so offline saves carry them too): name = company, or "Company (Contact)", or "First Last"; address = the five parts joined. That composition is the safety net that made reworking the readers safe; any reader we missed still renders correctly.

AUTOCOMPLETE. Address 1 gets Google Places suggestions via the CURRENT Autocomplete Data API (AutocompleteSuggestion + Place.fetchFields, not the deprecated widget), script loaded with loading=async, one session token per typing burst (billing). Selecting a pick fills street, city, state (short code), zip; city/state/zip take the pick's values outright (stale leftovers would be worse than blanks) while a typed suite number in Address 2 survives. The key is a build-time env var VITE_GOOGLE_MAPS_KEY with NO key committed (rule 7: the restricted key does not exist yet, handoff below). No key, offline, or any Places failure leaves Address 1 a plain input; the estimator's normal habitat is offline at a job site, so autocomplete is strictly an enhancement, never a gate.

RELOAD + LEGACY ROWS. estimateLoad now selects * (an explicit list naming the new columns would 400 every edit-load on a database the migration has not reached; same forward-compat pattern as the dashboard's bonus columns) and maps the split columns into the form, falling back to the same naive split the SQL backfill uses (first token / remainder; whole address into Address 1) so a legacy row still fills the form and recomposes losslessly. The lead link now carries the leads table's ALREADY split address/city/state/zip instead of pre-joining them. canSave gains exactly one identity gate: last name (residential) or company (commercial); the address is deliberately never a gate.

BACKFILL (2026-07-15_estimate_customer_backfill.sql). Only rows whose split fields are all null; NEVER touches customer_name/customer_address; leaves company/is_commercial null (Dylan spot-checks; new saves always write is_commercial as a real boolean, so null = backfilled/legacy is a reliable tell). One deliberate improvement over the naive spec: when the comma-split has no clean trailing "City, ST Zip", the remainder goes into customer_address2 instead of being dropped, because the estimator recomposes customer_address from the split fields on the next save and a dropped remainder would silently vanish from the composed address the first time an old estimate is edited. Parsing logic was validated against prod Postgres with a read-only SELECT over edge cases before committing.

CORRECTION TO THE PROMPT'S PREMISE (important). The prompt said pec_prod_jobs already has a customer_company column (citing index.html:9580) and asked the accept path to write the company there. Verified against prod: pec_prod_jobs has NO such column. What index.html:9580 reads is the pec_job_ar VIEW's customer_company, which is c.company from public.customers, the BRAND (prescott-epoxy | finishing-touch) that drives SMS branding and brand identity. Writing "Acme LLC" into that concept would have corrupted branding, and writing to the nonexistent column would have broken the accept flow outright. The correct existing target is public.customers.company_name (2026-05-04 migration, explicitly "the customer's business; NOT the brand", already edited by the dashboard's customer form): accept now passes first_name / last_name / company_name through to the customers upsert, only when the estimate has values so old estimates never blank an existing customer. The schedule job (pec_prod_jobs) carries the company via the composed customer_name ("Acme LLC (Wile Coyote)"), which is what it displays anyway.

DOWNSTREAM READERS. Proposal page "Prepared for": company bold, "Attn: contact" and the split-composed address under it, verbatim fallback to the composed columns for pre-split rows (test-pinned pixel-identical). Estimate detail in index.html: company bold with the contact under it via the customer row (guarded so a pre-migration database renders the old way). Estimate list and the job-based estimate/invoice PDFs read the composed columns and were left alone on purpose. Tests: the offline-save fixture moved to the split shape and asserts the composed safety nets; three new sections cover the commercial render, the customers pass-through (including that customers.company stays the brand), and the pre-split fallback.

Why: build prompt 23 phase 1 (Dylan + Cowork, 2026-07-15). Phases 2 (custom estimate mode) and 3 (live AI proposal writer) build on these fields and are separate prompts.
Files touched: see Changed above.
Next steps: Cowork applies both migrations (ORDER MATTERS: columns before the deploy, backfill after columns), then Dylan pushes to deploy, then the Google key setup enables autocomplete.
