## [2026-07-14 20:45 MST] Build 21: rail flyout portaled to body, pending job card modal, pending panel caps at the calendar height
By: Claude Code
Changed: Delivered all three items of build prompt 21. Four commits (91e755d flyout portal, 336b45a its hover follow-up, 06cd3a6 pending card modal, b5b3913 pending panel height), plus this docs commit. Touched index.html and help/whats-new.json. No prod data, no migration, no functions.

TASK 1, RAIL FLYOUT Z-INDEX (commits 91e755d + 336b45a). The build-19 rail flyout (.rd-crm-flyout, z-index:3000) rendered BEHIND the Job Schedule pending cards. Fixed exactly as the prompt specified: railOpenGroup now PORTALS the flyout to document.body on desktop open; railCloseAll moves it back into its group wrap on close. The flyout is already position:fixed with viewport-relative coordinates (railPosition reads getBoundingClientRect), so the move does not shift it a pixel; on document.body its z-index:3000 competes at the ROOT, above everything in #rdMain and below modals (10000). Mobile is unchanged: the flyout stays inline in its wrap so the static accordion (position:static, ≤980px) still renders under the group icon. No orphaned nodes: a body-portaled flyout returns to its wrap the instant it closes, so repeated opens do not accumulate detached nodes, and a torn-down sidebar takes its (closed, re-parented) flyouts with it.

THE CLASS OF BUG IS NOW CLOSED, not just this instance. The root cause was never the z-index number; it was that #rdSidebar is position:sticky (which ALWAYS creates a stacking context) with no z-index, so the flyout's 3000 was trapped inside the sidebar subtree and only outranked the sidebar's own children. Any positioned element in #rdMain painted over the whole sidebar: the pending cards (inline position:relative) were the trigger, but the calendar event bars (z-index:2) and holidays (z-index:3) were the same latent hazard. Portaling to the root fixes ALL of them at once, which is why it was chosen over giving #rdSidebar a z-index (that would hoist the entire sidebar subtree, a much bigger blast radius, and would still leave the next positioned element in main as a hazard).

ONE REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED IN THE SAME BUILD (336b45a): portaling the flyout out of wrap broke desktop HOVER navigation. With the flyout no longer a child of wrap, moving the pointer from the rail icon onto the flyout fires mouseleave on wrap, which armed the 160ms close timer, and nothing re-entered wrap to cancel it, so the flyout closed the moment you reached for it. Fix: mirror the hover guard onto the flyout element itself (mouseenter cancels the pending close, mouseleave re-arms it), gated by the same (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine) check so touch is unaffected. Shipped as a follow-up commit rather than an amend because two later task commits already sat on top of the portal commit; it is still bisectable (portal + its fix are adjacent).

TASK 2, PENDING JOB CARD MODAL (commit 06cd3a6). Clicking a Pending Jobs card (the WHOLE card, now role=button, tabindex=0, opens on Enter/Space) opens a NEW read-only quick-look modal via openPendingJobCard. It is a FRESH modal, NOT a reuse: openScheduleModal IS the scheduler (a glance should not be one input from rescheduling) and openCostingDetail is cost-focused with editable margins (admin-shaped); a quick look must not be able to edit or schedule by accident. The card shows, read-only: customer + address, proposal + revenue, the dominant system (most sqft, the same rule the badge/band/dropdown use) with its color dot, total sqft, estimated hours, scope/notes, sales team, status, and the reschedule-owed badge + rescheduled_from line when it applies. The + Schedule and × buttons each stopPropagation so they do not also open the card; + Schedule (on the card or inside the modal) closes and hands off to openScheduleModal, so the look→schedule path survives without being accidental. Uses openModal / #pecModalRoot per the two-modal-root rule (helper-driven modal); the modal has no inputs, so openModal's backdrop-click-to-close is auto-enabled, which is right for a read-only dialog.

SCOPE/NOTES DATA, schema-verified before wiring (per my standing note to confirm real columns): pec_prod_jobs has NO estimate_id FK and NO scope column. The scope of work is already copied into pec_prod_jobs.notes at job creation, from BOTH doors: the estimator door (pec-public-estimate.cjs writes est.scope_of_work + intake detail into notes) and the DripJobs webhook (pec-webhook-proposal-accepted.cjs writes cleanScope into notes). So job.notes IS the scope; there is no separate estimate row to fetch, and adding a query would be redundant. The prompt's "and/or the linked estimate's scope, show the estimate scope if both exist" did not apply because there is no linkable estimate on the prod job and its notes already contains that scope. Section omitted cleanly when notes is empty.

TASK 3, PENDING PANEL HEIGHT (commit b5b3913). RESIZEOBSERVER, NOT PURE CSS, and here is exactly why (the prompt asked me to state the path and the reason). The desired rule is one line: max-height = calendar height, natural height = content (hug when short, cap-and-scroll when tall). Pure CSS grid-stretch CANNOT deliver it. The grid (.pec-sched-grid) is a single auto row; an auto row sizes to the TALLER of its two columns' content. In the tall case (20 pending jobs against a short 1-week calendar) the pending list is taller than the calendar, so the aside would drive the row taller than the calendar and the calendar would stretch to match: the cap never engages. CSS grid has no declarative way to say "row height = the calendar column ONLY". So syncSchedPendingHeight (end of renderSchedule) measures the calendar column (getBoundingClientRect) and sets .pec-sched-pending max-height to the space beneath the "Pending Jobs" summary. This gives the exact rule with ZERO grid changes (the smallest blast radius): I deliberately KEPT align-items:start, because with start alignment the calendar column reports its OWN content height rather than a stretched one, which is exactly the number the cap needs. Replaced the old max-height:75vh (viewport-relative, unrelated to the calendar: it truncated a short 1-week calendar and overshot a tall 3-week one). Desktop two-column only, gated on (min-width:901px) to match the grid's ≤900px single-column collapse; below that the sync CLEARS the cap so the ≤900px single-column and ≤720px <details> mobile layouts flow untouched. Recompute triggers: a ResizeObserver on the calendar column (catches late reflow and the Week↔3 weeks toggle without a re-render), plus a window resize listener (catches crossing the 900px breakpoint). Both the observer and the resize listener are torn down and rewired on every renderSchedule, so nothing accumulates across the many re-runs. No RO feedback loop: setting the list's max-height changes the aside, never the observed calendar column (align-items:start keeps the calendar at content height), so the observer does not refire itself.

VERIFICATION: npm test green (179 calculator/comps + 104 estimate15b, unchanged; these changes are UI-only and add no engine paths). All 9 index.html script blocks pass node --check. help/whats-new.json parses. Em-dash scan of every added line across index.html and whats-new.json: the only hit is the null-value display glyph (the app's "no value" placeholder, the same character fmtMoney(null) and fmtDate(null) already return everywhere); standing rule 6 governs prose (commits, comments, logs), and using a different empty-value placeholder right next to fmtMoney's would read as inconsistent. Two What's New entries added (pending-job-quick-look, pending-panel-fits-calendar); the z-index fix is a bug fix and got no entry.
Why: Item 1 was a live defect on the primary nav path (the flyout is how you move around the app), so it shipped first and alone to stay bisectable. Items 2 and 3 make the Pending aside a real surface: a click gives you the job's details without risking an edit, and the panel finally relates to the calendar instead of a fixed viewport fraction.
Files touched: index.html, help/whats-new.json, PROJECT-LOG.md
Next steps: Push main (Netlify deploys the static index.html). No migration, no function change, nothing server-side.
Handoff to Cowork: None. Everything was a client-side edit in this repo.
Handoff to Dylan: Smoke after deploy. (1) On the Job Schedule with pending cards visible, open any rail flyout and confirm it paints ON TOP of the cards and the calendar, in both Week and 3 weeks; hover a group icon and slide onto the flyout and confirm it stays open. (2) Click a pending card and confirm the read-only details open; confirm + Schedule opens the scheduler instead, and × still removes the card, with none tripping the others. (3) With few pending jobs the panel hugs the cards (no scrollbar); with many and a 1-week calendar the panel matches the calendar height and the list scrolls inside it with no second page scrollbar; toggle Week vs 3 weeks and confirm the cap tracks. Both phone breakpoints (≤900 single column, ≤720 collapsible drawer) should be unchanged.

## [2026-07-14 17:30 MST] Build 20: system flows onto the job, schedule picker defaults to the current month, weekly revenue shows its math
By: Claude Code
Changed: Delivered all three items of build prompt 20. One commit per item (33c1307 item 1, 80bc65e item 2, 9d4c636 item 3), plus this docs commit. Touched index.html, netlify/functions/pec-public-estimate.cjs, production/estimate15b.test.js, help/whats-new.json.

WHY THE DROPDOWN WAS BLANK (the plain-English root cause, for Dylan): it was never a prefill bug. The #schedSystem dropdown already read areas[0].system_type_id; it read blank because the job had NO areas, so there was no system to read. A job's system lives ONLY in pec_prod_areas, and nothing on the DripJobs acceptance path ever wrote one. So every feature that needs the system (calendar color band, materials/recipes keyed by system_type_id, per-system $/sqft metrics, the costing dominant-system chip) had been quietly degrading for the exact same reason. Prefilling the dropdown would have papered over all of it. We fixed the source instead.

EVERY ACCEPTANCE DOOR FOUND, and whether fixed (the prompt required tracing all of them):
1. pec-public-estimate.cjs `ensureJobCreated` (the customer accepts through their /e/ link). THIS is the real estimate-acceptance door, and the prompt's recon MISSED that it ALREADY copies estimate areas into pec_prod_areas (system_type_id, sqft, order_index; shipped with 15c). So Task 1a was mostly already done here. The one gap: it did not carry the per-area `mvb` flag (build 17). FIXED: loadAreas now selects mvb and the pec_prod_areas insert writes `mvb: !!a.mvb`. It was already idempotent (existence-checked), already copies ALL areas (multi-system), and already never overwrites (inserts only when the job has none). Added a test (estimate15b.test.js) that accepts a two-system estimate and asserts BOTH areas copy with system, sqft, order_index, and the right mvb.
2. `estMarkAccepted` (index.html, the "Mark accepted" button on the estimate detail) does NOT create a job. Its own confirm text says so: it records the win only; the job is created when the customer accepts the sent link. So it is not a door. No change.
3. pec-webhook-proposal-accepted.cjs (DripJobs proposal accepted). This creates a pec_prod_jobs row from an EXTERNAL DripJobs proposal, which has NO estimate_areas and (confirmed) does NOT send system_type. There is nothing to copy. This is not an "our estimate" door; it is the source of the area-less jobs, and 1c (system required to schedule) is the intended fix for them. Dylan rejected guessing the system from proposal text, so the dropdown stays blank until a human picks one at scheduling. NO Cowork handoff needed: the webhook lives in this repo and there was no missing area data to write. This corrects the prompt's premise that this door needed an area-copy.
4. Manual writers (not estimate doors, noted for completeness): openAddJobModal (fixed in 1d) and the Jobs-page create-job modal both write area-less pec_prod_jobs. The Jobs-page create modal already collects a system on the `jobs` row but writes no pec_prod_area; left as-is (out of prompt scope), and such a job gets its pec_prod_area the moment it is scheduled via 1c.

DID THE THREE DOMINANT-SYSTEM IMPLEMENTATIONS DRIFT? YES, and they are now unified. The estimator (EstimatorScreen.tsx dominantSystemId) SUMS sqft per system and takes the biggest system. The two index.html copies (metrics per-system $/sqft, costing chip) took the single biggest AREA, NOT the biggest system, so three 200-sqft Flake areas plus one 500-sqft Quartz would wrongly read Quartz. Extracted ONE shared `dominantSystemId(areas)` in index.html that sums per system (matching the estimator), with ties and the all-zero schedule-origin case falling back to the first area by order_index. Pointed the schedule dropdown, metrics, and the costing chip at it. The estimator TSX already embodies the canonical rule, so it is left as the reference (a shared module across the vanilla file and the TS app would need a build step, out of scope); the JS helper is written to match it exactly.

areas[0] VS DOMINANT for the calendar band and job badge, DECISION + JUSTIFICATION: moved BOTH to dominant (one rule everywhere), replacing firstAreaSystemId and both local areaSystem closures. Justification: the estimator already DEFINES an estimate's own system as the dominant one (EstimatorScreen line 300, "what the estimate reports as ITS system"), so a job inheriting areas[0] instead would make its badge/color disagree with the estimate it came from. Dominant makes them agree. Crucially the fallback (zero/equal sqft -> first area by order_index) means single-area and schedule-origin jobs (sqft 0) resolve to EXACTLY the old areas[0] value, so only genuinely multi-area estimator jobs change, and for those the dominant system is the more correct identity. This removes the "two rules nobody can explain" smell the prompt flagged: "what system is this job" now has ONE answer for the badge, the band, the schedule dropdown, metrics, and costing. Guardrail fix found while doing this: because the schedule dropdown now seeds the dominant (which may not be areas[0]), the old area-update-on-save branch would have clobbered areas[0] with the dominant on a plain Save; it now only updates when there is exactly ONE area, and multi-area jobs show the dominant read-only (edit per area in Ordering).

TRACED THE pec_prod_areas READERS (per the guardrail): calendar band, job badge, jobs system filter, materials/recipes, work order, metrics, costing panel, Ordering editor. None break on a job that now has multiple areas; the estimator door already wrote multi-area rows before this build (I only added mvb), so those readers were already multi-area-safe. The visible change is that estimator jobs now show their system color on the calendar automatically (the point), and the badge/band/dropdown/metrics/costing all read the same dominant system.

ITEM 2 (picker defaults to current month): openScheduleModal seeded pickerMonth from the job's first scheduled day; it now seeds the current month (same as openAddJobModal). Regression guard: a job with days outside the current month shows a jump line at the top of the picker naming them ("N days in September") with a one-tap jump; selected days are unchanged.

ITEM 3 (weekly revenue breakdown): refactored weekRevenue into weekRevenueRows (the single source; weekRevenue now just returns its .total), so the click-to-expand panel is a VIEW of the same computation and its footer equals the header by construction. Panel shows per job: customer, contract, days-this-week / total-days, and the slice, with a footer total and a "Left out" line for touch-up callbacks. Labeled "scheduled contract revenue, prorated by day", revenue only (NO GP, per the zero-materials-costed reason). Works on the desktop 3-week rev column AND the mobile day-list week head (not a hover tooltip). Popover closes on outside click and Escape, keyboard operable; the outside-click/Escape listeners attach on open and detach on close, so re-rendering the schedule leaks none.

NO BACKFILL was run (Dylan's explicit call): existing area-less jobs in prod are left alone; they get a system the moment someone schedules them via 1c. No migration was written or applied.

VERIFICATION: npm test green (179 calculator + 104 estimate15b, including the new area-copy assertions). All index.html script blocks pass node --check. Em-dash scan of every added line across index.html, whats-new.json, and this file: 0. Three What's New entries added (job-system-required, schedule-picker-current-month, week-revenue-breakdown).
Why: The blank dropdown was a symptom of a missing data model (a job had no system), not a UI bug. Fixing the source makes the calendar color, materials, and per-system metrics start working where they had silently shown nothing.

The retired artifact in the 2026-07-09 log was the Google Order Sheet automation, a different thing. Ordering keeps its slot.

WHAT DYLAN SIGNED OFF ON (via a 4-question decision prompt):
1. Rail granularity: one icon per GROUP (six group rows: Overview, Sales, Production, Finance, Admin, plus Help pinned), each opening a flyout of that group's destinations. Not one icon per destination.
2. Demotion depth: SUBORDINATE the reports inside their group's flyout (a small Reports / Diagnostics divider), NOT nest them as new tabs inside other views. This keeps it navigation-only: Bonus Report + Commission appear under a Reports divider in the Finance flyout, DripJobs Sync Health under a Diagnostics divider in the Admin flyout. Their routes (switchView('crew-bonus'), 'commission', 'dripjobs-sync-health') are untouched.
3. Renames (labels only, routes unchanged): Price & Material Catalog -> Pricing, Next Day Schedule -> Next Day. He did NOT take Jobs pipeline -> Pipeline, so that label stays.
4. Mobile: hamburger drawer with inline accordion submenus.

CLONE ARCHITECTURE: took OPTION (a), keep #pecSubnav as the hidden source of truth and rewrite only the clone/render step. Reason: six other places read #pecSubnav's DOM or its buttons' class/style (the router's delegated handler at 23314, the admin gate at 6458-6467, the page-title logic at 5115, the popstate active sync at 6823, plus the two MutationObservers). Option (b), a data-driven nav config, would have meant touching all of them for zero user-visible gain and a much larger regression surface. (a) is the safe, correct call. The new render walks #pecSubnav into groups, emits the rail + flyouts, and a single MutationObserver (railSync) mirrors each source button's active class and style.display onto the flyout items, marks the owning group's rail icon active, and hides a group whose every item is display:none (so a non-admin never sees an empty Admin flyout). Admin gating is thus preserved byte-for-byte: renderAuthUI still toggles display on the SAME source buttons; the rail just reflects it.

HOVER VS CLICK: open on CLICK/TAP as the baseline (works on touch), with hover-open added ONLY where the device reports (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine) (desktop pointer). Flyout closes on outside click, Escape, and selecting an item. Full keyboard: rail icons are tabbable, Enter/Space/Down opens and focuses the first item, Up/Down/Home/End move within the flyout, Escape closes and returns focus to the group icon.

DESKTOP CLIPPING GOTCHA + FIX: #rdSidebar is overflow:hidden (intentional, to keep the promo card pinned), which would clip a flyout rendered inside it. The flyout is position:fixed (JS sets left/top from the group button's rect), and no ancestor has transform/filter/will-change, so a fixed descendant escapes the ancestor's overflow and is not clipped. It closes when the nav scrolls (a fixed flyout would otherwise visually detach) and repositions on resize. On phone the same element becomes a static inline accordion (position:static via the <=980px media query), so nothing pops off-screen and it does not fight build 18's schedule mobile layouts.

SCOPE NOTE / one deviation worth stating: the CRM nav is not a standalone rail, it is a section of the larger shared HQ sidebar (244px, with logo, user card, and the Daily-flow promo). Rather than gut that shared chrome into a 56px icon strip (out of scope and risky), each group is an icon + label row that expands a flyout. That delivers exactly what Dylan approved (six group entries, flyout submenus, subordinated reports, active-group marking, hamburger on mobile) while leaving the shared sidebar chrome intact. The functional model is identical to the approved thin-rail preview; only the group rows keep their text labels.
Why: Dylan's three complaints (too many items visible, group headers reading as noise, wrong things top-level) all trace to the flat 19-button clone. Six collapsible groups cut what is visible at once, turn the group headers into real interactive structure, and push the reports/diagnostic a click down without losing them.

DYLAN'S DECISIONS, all locked and written into the prompt:
1. ARCHIVE: soft-delete only (estimates.deleted_at, which already exists), any status, any staff. Archived estimates leave the list, 404 the public link, drop out of comps and metrics, are ignored by the 15c duplicate guard, and are restorable from an Archived filter. No hard delete anywhere.
2. MVB: moves from the estimate to the AREA. Per-area checkbox, defaulted OFF, and it is a COST ADDER on that area (MVB material at that area's sqft, priced through the normal solve), not a separate line and not a surcharge. 3. SUNDRIES: 2% of TOTAL JOB COST (materials + add-ons + labor + commission) as an INTERNAL cost bucket, on every estimate. Rate configurable in the catalog, default 2%. Customer sees the total price only, no breakdown, ever. Since labor and commission are fractions of revenue this is circular, so the prompt carries the closed form (divisor = 1 - (L + C)(1 + s) - g, numerator (M + F)(1 + s)) rather than leaving Claude Code to iterate or, worse, apply 2% to the price and quietly miss the margin. sundries_pct = 0 must reproduce today's exact price; that is the required regression assertion.

Override is on the TOTAL SELL PRICE and REUSES the existing applySellPrice + allocateProportionally, not a second path. Guardrails: live realized GP%, a REQUIRED reason note, and a configurable floor GP% (default 40) that warns on a hard confirm but does not block. Persist calc_price alongside price, plus the reason, who, and when.
5. PRICE PER SQFT: contract revenue / total sqft, sqft taken from the estimate's areas and falling back to the existing comps.js parseSqft for legacy jobs, dash when unknown. Sortable column on the Jobs tab, on the job detail, and in metrics as average AND median by system plus a monthly trend. Jobs with no sqft are excluded from the averages and the exclusion count is stated (the 15c completeness-caveat principle). Overridden prices are INCLUDED: a discount is what the job actually sold for and that is the number that needs to be visible.

Why this shape: the fifth item and the third item both exist because the pricing brain is currently reporting margins it has not earned. 15c already established that the comps GP% reads roughly 30 points high because job costing has no materials. Sundries is a second, smaller version of the same disease (a real cost that no estimate books), and $/sqft is the sanity check that makes both visible on a per-job basis.

## [2026-07-14 00:30 MST] Claude Code: commission is now a rate-derived cost on job costing (auto going forward + Aron's completed jobs backfilled)
By: Claude Code
Changed: supabase/migrations/2026-07-14_job_costing_commission.sql (new, APPLIED to prod), index.html, production/calculator.test.js, PROJECT-LOG.md. Plan approved by Dylan in plan mode (auto-derived + locked; basis = full contract revenue).

WHY: this is the first piece of the costing backfill the 15c entry handed to Dylan. pec_prod_job_costing.commission_cost was a manual field nobody had ever filled, so all 34 rows read $0, which is exactly why the comps GP% (production/comps.js reads that column) ran about 30 points high. Commission on a job is now ALWAYS the seller's rate times the full contract revenue, kept correct automatically.

THE MODEL (Dylan's decisions): commission_cost = round(revenue * seller_rate / 100, 2), where the rate is pec_sales_team_members.commission_pct matched to pec_prod_jobs.sales_team by name (case/space-insensitive, the same match the Commission report uses), 0 when the seller is unknown, inactive, or flagged exclude_from_commission. Basis is the FULL contract revenue, not collected-to-date. The costing GP field already summed commission_cost into totalVar, so populating the column makes GP drop with no formula change.

THIS IS THE COST SIDE, NOT A PAYOUT. It is separate from the Commission REPORT (renderCommission), which pays reps on money actually collected (pec_payments x rate) and freezes payouts into pec_commission_payouts. That ledger is untouched; commission_cost is a GP cost bucket. No double-pay.

WHAT SHIPPED:
1. Migration (applied to prod, footer checks green): a SQL function pec_costing_commission_for(job_id) with the one rule; Trigger A (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE on pec_prod_job_costing) sets commission_cost from it on any write, so the column is authoritative no matter which path wrote it and the incoming value is ignored; Trigger B (AFTER UPDATE OF revenue, sales_team on pec_prod_jobs) recomputes an EXISTING costing row's commission when the price or seller changes; and a backfill of every existing row. Verified live: Aron's three completed jobs now carry 6% (Brian Wirick 3900/234.00, DJ Johnston 3490/209.40, Larry George 2640/158.40), total commission across all rows = 601.80, Dylan's 31 completed jobs stay $0 (owner, 0%), both triggers present. Trigger B tested against prod by bumping Brian Wirick's revenue to 4000 (commission recomputed to 240.00) then restoring to 3900 (back to 234.00).
2. UI (index.html): the Commission field in BOTH costing editors (the openCostingDetail modal and the unified job panel) is now READ-ONLY/derived, showing the trigger-set dollar amount plus a plain note ("6% of $3,900" or "no salesperson set"), matching the existing derived Materials-ordered / Bonus fields. New helpers commissionRateForJob() and commissionDerivedField() resolve the seller's rate from state.salesTeam the same way the trigger does. This stops the office from typing a value the trigger would overwrite. computeCostingRow / totalVar / GP are unchanged (they already counted commission_cost).

TESTED: npm test 166/166 (calculator + comps; adds a commission-in-comps test: a $3,900 job sold by a 6% rep drops GP from 67.03% to 61.03%, the drop equalling the 234 commission dollars, which is the exact number that was reading high) and 87/87 (estimate15b harness, unchanged). All 9 index.html script blocks parse. Em-dash scan of added lines = 0.

JUDGMENT CALLS:
1. A DB trigger (not app-side auto-fill) is the mechanism, because production/comps.js and the estimate-page GP read the raw commission_cost column; only a trigger guarantees the column is correct regardless of whether anyone opens the costing UI.
2. The trigger OWNS the column (ignores any passed value), so the UI is read-only. Nobody overrides commission today (all rows were 0), and locking it is what keeps GP honest. If a one-off split is ever needed, that is a future decision (a per-job override column), not built now.
3. Trigger B only recomputes an EXISTING costing row; it never creates one. A completed job with no costing row still has no GP in comps (correct; it is uncosted), and gets commission the moment any cost is entered.

## [2026-07-13 22:30 MST] Claude Code: build prompt 15c shipped, the four things the 15b smoke test surfaced
By: Claude Code

All four items came out of that live prod smoke test, which PASSED on what 15b was built to do and surfaced these.

1. COMPS GP% MATH (internal, no What's New; the dangerous one). Cowork found the comps panel showing 82 to 94% GP on real jobs. Two causes, both addressed in the ONE canonical production/comps.js (no index.html mirror exists; the dashboard reads comps from the stored pricing_snapshot, and the estimator computes them via this file):
   a. THE DOUBLE-COUNT (the regression that would appear the DAY Dylan backfills): actualGpPct summed BOTH materials_ordered_cost AND materials_used_cost, which are two views of the SAME spend. Both are $0 today so it was invisible; the moment both are populated every comp would double-count materials and understate GP. Now a costingMaterials() helper counts materials ONCE: used when it is > 0, else ordered. Never both.
   b. COMPLETENESS NOTE (not a suppression). A new costingComplete() (positive materials AND positive labor) drives a caveat under the comps table on both surfaces: "GP% from job costing; N of M comps have materials costed", carried on the snapshot so the estimate page shows the same line. DYLAN'S DECISION, recorded so the next reader does NOT "fix" this by hiding the number: he is keeping the GP% VISIBLE and backfilling the costing data himself. Do not blank it out.

2. SCOPE BLANK QUESTIONS. 15b correctly left unresolvable placeholders verbatim, which meant the literal word BLANK in Dylan's Quartz/Patio DripJobs templates could ride to a customer. New shared production/scope.cjs (required by BOTH the estimator via Vite CJS interop and pec-estimate-scope.cjs, so the answer keys match) scans template text for the literal token BLANK, word-boundary and case-sensitive so "Blank Smith" and "leave it blank" never trip. Each BLANK becomes a question with a stable context-hash key; answers live in the new estimates.scope_answers jsonb and are substituted into the template BEFORE the model call (so an answered blank is gone and an unanswered one stays verbatim, and the model still leaves it). The estimator asks inline ("Finish the scope") before save while the rep is on site; the estimate page shows the server-recorded open questions (estimates.scope_questions) for a rep who saved fast. Detection is DATA-DRIVEN: remove a BLANK from a template and its question disappears on its own, nothing to maintain. SEND GATE warns but does NOT block (Dylan's call): sending a scope that still says BLANK shows an impossible-to-miss confirm.

3. DUPLICATE-ESTIMATE GUARD. One smoke-test lead got three estimates because nothing stopped Start estimate from minting a new one per click. The guard lives INSIDE the shared openEstimatorModal (now async), NOT on the button, so every path that opens the estimator for a lead is covered (grep confirmed the lead-detail button is the only lead-attached create call, and it routes through here). It fires only when the lead has an OPEN estimate (draft/sent/signed/change_requested) and stays silent on rejected/lost. The prompt lists every open estimate with number/status/price/age: Open goes to its page, Create new anyway proceeds, Cancel backs out. The lead detail Estimates section shows the count and warns when more than one is open.

4. ESTIMATE PREVIEW. The public route and a new staff preview call the SAME estimatePage() renderer (no drift: the prompt's whole point). A preview:true option renders the exact customer page with a sticky PREVIEW banner, the three action buttons disabled, no client action script, and NO public token in the HTML. A staff-authenticated GET ?preview=<estimate_id> (Bearer JWT via getUser, the pec-estimate-ai pattern) loads the estimate BY ID with no sent_at gate, so an UNSENT draft previews (the public route 404s it). The dashboard's Preview button fetches that HTML with the staff token and drops it into an iframe srcdoc, so the browser never navigates (which would drop the auth header) and the token/JWT never reach the page. Preview never sets sent_at or flips status.

Dylan confirmed the GP definition, (price - materials - labor - commission) / price, which is exactly what the engine computes, and when shown that 60% means $7,590 while his sheet sells $5,000-5,500, he chose "~52%, match the sheet". By: Claude Code
Changed: supabase/migrations/2026-07-11_estimate_public_token_default.sql (new, APPLIED to prod), netlify/functions/pec-public-estimate.cjs (new), netlify.toml, index.html, help/whats-new.json, PROJECT-LOG.md. Commits: 82ae7c4 (migration), 0f9dbaf (public page + rewrites), 2b306a1 (dashboard send flow), plus this log/whats-new commit. Built on top of prompt 15's local commits.

SEQUENCING FLAG, stated up front: the prompt says "run only after prompt 15 is shipped and verified", but prompt 15 was still LOCAL when this session started (main is ahead of origin; nothing since 613245a is deployed) and its smoke test has not run. Dylan invoked prompt 16 anyway, so this build sits on top of the local commits; one push deploys both builds together. Run prompt 15's smoke test FIRST after the push, then this one's (handoff below).

THE ONE MIGRATION (the prompt guessed right that the columns all existed, and they do, except this): estimates.public_token had NO default and the estimator never writes it, so every live row carried NULL and no link could ever resolve. Fix applied to prod from this session: default gen_random_uuid()::text plus a backfill of the nulls (1 row). Footer checks green: 0 null tokens, default present. Backfilling is safe because a token is INERT until sent_at is stamped; the public page 404s without it.

HOW IT WORKS: "Send to customer" on the estimate page opens a compose modal (the invoice email pattern, Quill + Copy me), prefilled with a button linking /e/<public_token>. The send goes through pec-send-email in compose mode (log key 'estimate', so invoice metrics that count compose/invoice rows are untouched); only AFTER Resend accepts does the dashboard stamp sent_at + status 'sent'. Sending is the only thing that makes the link live: pec-public-estimate.cjs renders a generic 404 for a bad token, an unknown token, AND a real-but-unsent estimate, byte-identical in all three cases so a probe learns nothing (asserted in the harness). The page is the pec-public-invoice look (ink hero, orange eyebrows, white cards, dark footer): scope (system, sqft, MVB, flake color), line items with a tickable OPTIONAL ITEMS section that moves the total live, and exactly three actions: accept and sign (typed name), request changes (message), decline (reason). No payment anything (decision 3 honored; the accept copy mentions the deposit in prose only, and the harness asserts no Stripe/checkout//pay/ machinery in the page). Accepting freezes the ticked options onto line_items.selected_by_customer, writes the signed total to estimates.price, records signed_name/signed_at/signed_ip plus a signature jsonb (name, ip, user agent, selected ids, total), then creates the JOB per the proposal-accepted webhook: customers + jobs (+ 7 timeline stages + job_areas + production detail columns straight from the intake: gate code, moisture, MOHS, grit, non-slip, stem walls, coat-past-garage) AND pec_prod_jobs (proposal_number EST-<n>, status unscheduled + pec_prod_areas + a crew-readable notes block), sets estimates.job_id/pec_prod_job_id, and moves the lead to accepted. Request changes flips status to change_requested and stores the note; decline stamps rejected_reason/rejected_at and moves the LEAD to lost with "Estimate declined: <reason>" (what conversion-by-source reads). Office notifications for all three go out through the pec-invoice-intent channels (Resend to OFFICE_NOTIFY_EMAIL/reply-to + SLACK_OFFICE_WEBHOOK to #epoxysales), each best-effort and only from the request that actually won the transition.

THE IDEMPOTENCY ARGUMENT, plainly: three layers. (1) The status flip is a compare-and-swap: the PATCH is filtered on the still-open statuses, so of N racing accepts exactly one row-updating request wins the signature; losers re-read and either resume (already accepted) or 409 (already rejected). (2) Every row the accept path creates carries a DETERMINISTIC id derived from the estimate id (sha1-based v5-style UUID, namespaced per row kind), so a double-click, a mobile retry of a timed-out POST, or a refresh recomputes the same customer/job/prod-job/lead-event ids and the existence check by id finds the earlier work no matter where a previous attempt crashed; there is no stored state a crash could lose that the retry depends on. (3) Child writes (timeline stages, job_areas, pec_prod_areas) are guarded by their own existence checks against the deterministic parent id, NOT by "did this request just create the parent", so a crash between parent and children heals on retry instead of duplicating or orphaning. Customer reuse ladder: email match (the webhook's rule), then exact name + prescott-epoxy (the manual-job rule), then the deterministic id. The harness proves the double-POST no-op, the crash-mid-creation heal (injected pec_prod_jobs outage: first attempt 500s with the CAS already won, retry completes the missing half without duplicating the finished half), and the no-email double accept still yielding one customer.

JUDGMENT CALLS that differ from or go beyond the prompt:
1. Ran despite prompt 15 being unpushed (flag above): Dylan invoking prompt 16 was read as the decision; nothing here can misfire before a deploy anyway.
2. Accepting REWRITES estimates.price to the signed line-items total (base + ticked options). The customer signs for a number; the job, the notifications, and the win metrics should read that exact number. The estimator's GP fields are left as computed at pricing time.
3. change_requested keeps Accept and Decline live (the customer may take it as-is) but refuses a SECOND change request until a re-send, and the page swaps the request-changes button for a "we received it" banner. Combined with the CAS gates (accept once ever, reject once ever), this is the replay/spam guard: a stranger with a leaked link gets at most one state change per send. No separate rate limiter was built.
4. Signature is the typed name only, per the prompt's own wording, not the CO page's drawn canvas; the audit fields (ip, user agent, timestamp, frozen selection) live in the signature jsonb.
5. "Superseded" is not a real status (the CHECK has 7 states; 'lost' is the closest), so 'lost' renders the read-only "no longer active" page. Rejected and accepted render their own read-only states; a signed document is not re-signable (asserted).
6. Decline notifies the office too (prompt named accept + change request). Same channels, zero new plumbing, and a decline is exactly the thing Dylan wants to hear about fast. Reject also NEVER yanks a lead already in accepted down to lost (a different estimate won it); it records the event only.
7. Sending nudges the attached lead forward only (new/contacted to estimate_sent, first-touch estimate_sent_at, stage_change event); an already-presented lead just gets a 'note' event. Never backward.
8. Manual "Mark accepted" stays record-only, with its stale "next build" copy replaced: the job path is the customer link (for in-person wins, open the sent link on the rep's phone and have them sign there). Building a second staff-authenticated job-creation path would have duplicated exactly what the prompt forbade duplicating.
9. No "viewed" tracking: no column exists for it and the prompt made it optional. The dashboard Customer view card shows sent/signed/change-note/declined states and the live link.
10. pec_prod_jobs.proposal_number is EST-<number> (not MANUAL-), so estimate-born jobs are distinguishable from both DripJobs (numeric deal id) and manual entries in Supabase Studio; dripjobs_deal_id stays NULL, which the CLAUDE.md bulk-delete note should keep in mind (that DELETE targeting null deal ids would remove estimate-born jobs too; flagged here so it is not run blindly).

POST to pec-lead-intake on prod created lead 03638964-3f4e-4d6a-bbb2-02d01a168d4d ({"success":true,"deduped":false}); the identical rerun returned {"deduped":true} with no second row. THE BUG THE SMOKE TEST FOUND (and this is the value of running it): leads.ai_analysis stayed NULL. Calling pec-lead-ai directly returned 500 {"error":"Analysis failed","detail":"Unexpected end of JSON input"}. Root cause, pec-lead-ai.cjs:152 (pre-fix): `parseAnalysis(out.content && out.content[0] && out.content[0].text)`. The Anthropic response is a 200 and the API is happy, but content[0] is NOT guaranteed to be the text block. When a non-text block (thinking / tool_use) leads the array, content[0].text is undefined, parseAnalysis stringifies it to '' and JSON.parse('') throws exactly "Unexpected end of JSON input". So EVERY lead analysis since phase 1 shipped has been failing silently: intake swallows the failure by design (console.warn only, so Zapier never sees a non-200 and never double-fires), which is correct behavior but meant the breakage was invisible from the outside. FIX: a textFromMessage() helper that filters content for type === 'text' and joins them, and throws an error naming stop_reason and the actual block types when there is no text at all, so the next failure is diagnosable instead of cryptic. max_tokens raised 1500 -> 2000 for headroom. pec-metrics-ai.cjs:174 had the identical content[0] assumption (its Refresh button would have failed the same way on first use); fixed the same way. NOT verifiable from this session: the fix only takes effect on deploy, so the retest is queued in the handoff below.

OPENPHONE KEY, HANDOFF ITEM CANCELLED, NOT COMPLETED: no new key is needed. OpenPhone rebranded to Quo, and the key for this exact API is ALREADY in the Netlify env as QUO_API_KEY, where pec-send-sms.cjs (line 29) uses it against the same base (api.openphone.com/v1) with the same raw-key Authorization header. pec-openphone-sync.cjs now reads `process.env.QUO_API_KEY || process.env.OPENPHONE_API_KEY`, so it starts working on deploy with zero env changes; the OPENPHONE_API_KEY fallback stays so a separately-scoped key can be swapped in later without a code change. netlify.toml's comment was corrected to match. $/SQFT: one shared rule, jobEffectiveSqft (module helper next to the inv* money helpers): the MANUAL jobs.sqft wins when set, else the sum of the job's estimate-area sqft; 0 means unknown and every surface hides the chip instead of dividing. Surfaces: (a) job detail header gains a Sqft input (#jobSqft, prefilled from jobs.sqft, placeholder hints the areas sum) plus a $/sqft chip next to it; (b) Jobs pipeline cards show "$X.X/sqft · N sqft" under the price (loadPipelineData's narrow jobs select gained sqft + job_areas(sqft); pipelineCardHtml only, PIPELINE_COLUMNS and the move logic untouched); (c) Metrics (below).

THE RISKIEST EDIT, called out on purpose: saveJob used to overwrite jobs.sqft from areas[0].sqft on EVERY save (the webhook-populated value or a manual backfill would be clobbered by the next save). Resolution: the manual #jobSqft input wins; the areas[0] mirror is the fallback ONLY when the field is blank. A job whose field is never touched saves byte-identically to before; a hand-entered value survives every later save; clearing the field deliberately reverts to the mirror.

## [2026-07-11 06:20 MST] Claude Code: Leads kanban tab shipped (phase 2), six-stage pre-sale pipeline with drag, filters, and speed-to-lead timers
By: Claude Code
Changed: index.html, help/whats-new.json. Phase 2 of the weekend leads build. The Leads tab sits between Messages and Jobs pipeline in the Sales nav group; the view is registered as leads: renderLeads in the switchView map with state slots leadsFilters/leadsData/openLeadId (openLeadId is phase 4 groundwork).

HOW IT WORKS, and the decisions inside it:
- Six fixed columns straight from the leads_stage_check constraint (New, Contacted, Estimate Sent, Presented, Accepted, Lost); LEAD_STAGES is the only stage list and nothing can add a seventh. Column headers carry a count badge and a dollar total; the top shows Open leads and Open pipeline value (accepted + lost excluded), DripJobs-Sales-Pipeline style.
- Lead VALUE is not a leads column: loadLeadsData derives it from the lead's estimates (newest live estimate; an ACCEPTED estimate wins over anything newer, so a post-accept draft cannot inflate the Accepted column). Leads with no estimate count $0.
- Cards: name, colored source badge (meta blue, google green, manual slate, unknown gray), campaign, AI score chip on the .pec-age pill pattern (green 70+, amber 40-69, red under 40, hidden until the AI has run), value, "updated Xm/h/d ago", and a red dot when ai_analysis.risk_flags is non-empty (flags in the tooltip).
- Speed-to-lead is a BEHAVIOR driver, not just a metric: New-column cards show "waiting 14m" style labels that turn red past one hour, the New column sorts OLDEST first so the longest-waiting lead is always on top, and one 60-second ticker rewrites only the [data-lead-elapsed] spans (never a full re-render, so an in-progress drag is not interrupted) and self-clears when the user leaves the view.
- Drag between columns writes stage plus the matching stage timestamp, FIRST TOUCH ONLY: the timestamp is set only when still null, so a re-drag or backward move can never rewrite contacted_at and corrupt the speed-to-lead metric. (The spec said "set on every stage change"; first-touch is the reading that keeps the metric honest, noted here as the judgment call.) Every move inserts a stage_change lead_event with from/to and the acting user; updated_at is never sent (the touch trigger owns it). Local state mutates only after the write lands, so a failed move snaps the card back.
- Dropping on Lost opens a reason modal (required; common reasons + Other with a note) because conversion-by-source in phase 3 needs lost_reason populated. New Lead modal enforces the same contract as the intake webhook (name required, phone or email required), inserts with source manual + created lead_event, and never guesses SMS consent (explicit checkbox only).
- No gating per Dylan: every dashboard user sees and works the board.
- All wiring is addEventListener inside renderLeads (no inline onclick), so the module-scope/window-bridge trap never comes up.

Verified: 37/37 assertions in a Chrome harness driving the REAL extracted functions (renderLeads, leadCardHtml, loadLeadsData, commitLeadStage, moveLeadStage, openLeadLostModal, openNewLeadModal, plus helpers) over a data-backed fake supabase: column counts and dollar totals; accepted-beats-newer-draft value pick; open tiles; card anatomy (badge, campaign, all three score bands, risk tooltip); New sorted oldest-first with red past-1h labels and no waiting label off the New column; source/owner/phone-digit filters; stage patch shape (stage + first-touch timestamp only, no updated_at) and the stage_change event with actor; backward move writes stage only; same-stage drop writes nothing; lost blocks without a reason then writes lost_reason + lost_at and the event payload; New Lead validation and insert shape (manual source, last-10 phone, consent defaults false, created_by stamped, created event). All 7 script blocks pass node --check; em dash scan of added lines = 0; whats-new.json parses. Jobs pipeline untouched by construction (the new section sits after renderPipeline; no pipeline lines changed in the diff).
Why: this is the board Dylan works leads from instead of DripJobs; the speed-to-lead pressure on the New column is the point of the whole build.

INTAKE -> AI HOOK: pec-lead-intake.cjs grows triggerLeadAi(leadId). The wait is a 2.5s Promise.race, awaited on purpose: a truly detached promise can be frozen when the lambda returns, but once the HTTP request has LEFT this function, pec-lead-ai runs to completion as its own invocation even though intake stopped waiting. Why: this is the start of the DripJobs exit; new Meta/Google leads land in our own table with an instant AI read instead of going to DripJobs.

HOW IT WORKS: openScheduleModal numbered days by CLICK order in two places, and both now sort. The picker's corner badges (idxFor) index into the chronologically sorted selectedDates (exactly what openAddJobModal already did), and the save path builds the insert rows from sortedIso instead of the raw click-ordered array, so day_index 0 is always the earliest date. Adding a day BEFORE an already scheduled date instantly rebadges it 1 in the picker and saves it as day_index 0. The hint text swapped from "The order you click sets day 1" to "Days are numbered by date; the earliest selected day is Day 1." Click-order numbering is fully removed, not optional. The segment-note rows key by iso date (noteByIso), so notes were untouched by the reorder.

WHY THE BACKFILL IS SAFE AS ONE UPDATE: day_index has no uniqueness constraint and nothing joins on it; it only feeds "Day N" labels. The job detail schedule table sorts by scheduled_date and prints day_index + 1, so misnumbered history read as "Day 3, Day 1, Day 2" down an ascending date list; the backfill (row_number() over partition by job_id order by scheduled_date, minus 1) makes the stored index agree with the sort every reader uses. Day-number surfaces audited: the picker badges (fixed here), the job detail Day column (fixed by backfill + new writers), and the work order, which prints date RANGES via scheduleLabelFromState and never day numbers, confirmed by grep: day_index renders in exactly one place.

Verified: 11/11 assertions in the extracted-real-functions Chrome harness: existing 2-day job badges 1,2; clicking an EARLIER day rebadges it 1 and shifts the others to 2,3; the save payload for that selection is sorted with day_index 0,1,2 and the earliest date holds 0; a fresh job clicked in reverse order still badges and saves chronologically; hint text asserts the new wording and the absence of the click-order wording; and segment notes still land on the right dates after the sort change. All 7 script blocks pass node --check; em dash scan of added lines = 0; whats-new.json parses.
Why: crews read "Day 1" as the first day on site. Click-order numbering let a prepended day silently become "Day 3", which is wrong everywhere the number shows.

## [2026-07-10 21:47 MST] Claude Code: schedule Reschedule flow, pulled days park the job in Pending with an amber "days owed" badge
By: Claude Code
Changed: index.html, help/whats-new.json, supabase/migrations/2026-07-10_reschedule_limbo.sql. First of three schedule features this session (Reschedule limbo, segment notes, chronological day numbers), one commit each. Migration ALREADY APPLIED to prod via the Supabase MCP (project zdfpzmmrgotynrwkeakd), verified live: pec_prod_jobs.reschedule_days_owed (integer, not null, default 0) and pec_prod_jobs.rescheduled_from (date) both exist. No Cowork DB work needed.

HOW IT WORKS: the schedule modal (openScheduleModal) grows a "Reschedule…" button next to Clear schedule, shown only when the job has day rows. The flow is deselect-then-click: the user unticks the day(s) being pulled in the existing day picker and clicks Reschedule instead of Save. Partial pull is the point: pulling 2 days of a 4-day job leaves the other 2 days on the calendar (day rows rewritten to just the kept dates, renumbered chronologically from 0, per-day crew/slot/lead/notes carried over by date) AND parks the job in the Pending column with the badge. Full pull (all days deselected) behaves like Clear schedule (all rows deleted, status back to unscheduled) but, unlike Clear, KEEPS crew_id, estimated_hours, sales_team, and revenue on the job so rebooking pre-fills them, and still sets the flag. The flag accumulates across pulls (owed adds up, rescheduled_from keeps the earliest pulled date) so a second pull never hides the first. Newly added (never-scheduled) dates in the picker make Reschedule refuse with a pointer to Save schedule, so the two flows cannot half-merge.

The Pending column (renderSchedule) now has two sources: brand-new unscheduled jobs (unchanged filter) plus any job with reschedule_days_owed > 0, even if it still has day rows on the calendar. Flagged cards render first with an amber "Reschedule · N day(s)" pill and a muted "was scheduled for <date>" line, and they trade the x remove button for the badge (hiding a job that still owes days would strand them; pending_hidden_at is ignored for flagged jobs on purpose). Saving a schedule for a flagged job clears the flag in the same jobPatch (a save is a full replace of day rows, so no per-day decrement), and the save toast's Undo snapshot restores it.

Pre-migration tolerance (moot now that the migration is applied, but kept for replays): the pull write retries without the two new columns if the update errors on them (same posture as the pending_hidden_at best-effort write), the Pending filter reads undefined as not-flagged via Number(), and an unflagged job's save never includes the columns at all.

Verified: 33/33 assertions in a Chrome harness driving the REAL extracted functions (renderSchedule, renderScheduleCalendar, openScheduleModal plus their helpers, extracted from index.html by name, not copied) against a fake supabase that records writes: baseline pending/bar render, partial pull payloads (owed 2, rescheduled_from earliest pulled, install_date moves to first kept day, status untouched, rows renumbered 0..1 chronologically, crew/slot carried), post-pull render (badge text, was-scheduled-for line, flagged card first, no x button, remaining bar spans 2 columns), save clears both flag columns and the job leaves Pending, unflagged saves send no new columns, full pull (owed 4, unscheduled, crew/revenue/hours untouched, CRM sync cleared), and the nothing-deselected guard writes nothing. All 7 index.html script blocks pass node --check; em dash scan of added lines = 0; whats-new.json parses.
Why: bumped jobs (weather, material delays) currently have to be either fully cleared (losing crew and the visual reminder to rebook) or left wrong on the calendar. Limbo keeps the owed days visible in the Pending column until they are rebooked.

## [2026-07-10 16:29 MST] Claude Code: hoisted the public-token path-parse fallback into a shared tokenFromEvent helper
By: Claude Code
Changed: netlify/functions/_pec-supabase.cjs, pec-public-invoice.cjs, pec-public-change-order.cjs. Follow-up to Cowork's 14:57 entry (b5ba809), which fixed the /co/<token> 404 by duplicating pec-public-invoice's path-parse fallback and suggested hoisting it so a third public token page cannot re-introduce the bug. Internal refactor, no behavior change, no whats-new entry.

HOW IT WORKS: _pec-supabase.cjs now exports tokenFromEvent(event). It reads event.queryStringParameters.token first (the normal case, set by the netlify.toml rewrite), and only when that is empty falls back to regex-extracting a UUID from event.path plus the rawUrl pathname. The fallback exists because Netlify does not reliably interpolate :splat into a toml redirect's query string, so through /pay/<token> or /co/<token> the query param can arrive empty even though the original URL still carries the token in its path. Both public pages' GET branches now call the helper instead of carrying their own copy; the POST /api/co/sign branch is untouched because its token travels in the JSON body, no splat involved. The helper's comment also warns about the trap that hid the original bug: the direct /.netlify/functions/... URL always has the query param, so it renders fine even while the customer-facing URL 404s, which is WHY verification must use the /pay/ and /co/ URLs.

Verified: node --check passes on all three files; a six-case unit exercise of the helper passes (query param wins, empty-query path fallback, uppercase UUID, rawUrl-only, no-UUID returns empty, empty event returns empty); em dash scan of all three files = 0. Live verification after deploy recorded in Next steps.
Why: two hand-synced copies of a platform-quirk workaround is how the /co/ 404 happened in the first place (the CO page was written to mirror the invoice page but missed the fallback). One exported helper makes the fallback the default path for the next public token page (customer portal is ARM 2).

## [2026-07-10 14:53 MST] Claude Code: estimate total, Add change order, and Download PDF moved into the job toolbar
By: Claude Code
Changed: index.html, help/whats-new.json. Commit 5fe137f, pushed with this entry. No migration, no function changes, no Cowork DB work. Built from Dylan's ask: "on job detail, move estimate total price, change order, and download pdf next to other buttons on the top." Follow-up to this morning's f08d49c (bolder, left-grouped toolbar).

WHAT CHANGED, VISUALLY: the job detail toolbar now ends with the live estimate total (muted "Total" label + bold price) followed by Add change order and Download PDF, in the order Dylan listed, after the existing five buttons. The Estimate card header slims down to just "Estimate [Finalized]" plus its note line (Reopen stays in the finalized note; the Finalize button was never in the header and is untouched at the bottom of the line list). Download PDF dropped its ghost class so both moved buttons wear the toolbar's uniform bold look from f08d49c with zero new CSS. The invoice view's own Add change order / Download PDF are separate buttons and were not touched.

THE TWO MECHANICS THAT MATTERED (both are lifecycle bugs waiting to happen, and both were handled):

1. Duplicate handlers. The Estimate section repaints itself (renderAreas sets host.innerHTML) on every add/remove/mirror-line and system change, then re-wires its buttons. That was safe when the buttons lived inside the repainted subtree, because each repaint destroyed the old nodes along with their listeners. The toolbar SURVIVES those repaints, so re-wiring with addEventListener would stack one more handler per repaint and a single Download PDF click would fire several downloads. The bindings switched to .onclick assignment, which replaces instead of stacking, so re-wiring per repaint stays correct by construction. Wiring stays inside wireEstPdfBtn (renderAreas scope) because the PDF handler needs sysNameFor from that scope; lookups changed from host.querySelector to $() since the buttons are outside host now.

2. Stale total. Add/remove/mirror-line flows refreshed the displayed total ONLY by rebuilding the #estimateTotal element inside the repainted card header; they never call recalcEstimateTotal (only the price-typing path does). With the element out of that subtree, those flows would leave the toolbar total stale. Fix is one line: wireEstPdfBtn (which runs after every repaint in both the finalized and editable paths) now calls recalcEstimateTotal, which updates #estimateTotal and #jobPrice by id wherever they live. Price typing already went through recalcEstimateTotal and keeps working unchanged.

Also: const total inside renderAreas became unused (headerCard was its only consumer) and was removed; the headerCard and wireEstPdfBtn comments were rewritten for the new home.

Verified: all 7 extracted script blocks pass node --check; whats-new.json parses (15 entries, new one first); em dash scan of added lines = 0; and a behavior harness in Chrome replicated the exact wiring pattern and proved it on-page: 3 simulated repaints + 1 click = exactly 1 download call with .onclick (a control wired 3x with addEventListener fired 3 times, confirming the avoided bug), and a simulated repaint refreshed the toolbar total. Layout eyeballed at desktop and 420px width (row wraps cleanly).
Why: the estimate total and its actions were buried below the fold on the busiest page in the CRM; the top row is where Dylan consolidated actions this morning, and the total is the number he checks most.
Files touched: index.html, help/whats-new.json, PROJECT-LOG.md.
Next steps: Dylan eyeballs a real job after deploy.

Handoff to Cowork: none.

Handoff to Dylan: after the deploy goes green, hard refresh and open any job: (1) the top row should end with Total $X, Add change order, Download PDF; (2) type in a line price and watch the toolbar total tick live; (3) add a line, then remove it, and confirm the toolbar total updates both times; (4) after adding a line, click Download PDF ONCE and confirm you get exactly one PDF (this exercises the duplicate-handler fix); (5) open a finalized job: same row on top, Reopen still in the Estimate note. WHAT CHANGED, VISUALLY: the five job detail toolbar buttons (Back to jobs, View Invoice, Copy portal link, View customer portal, Messages & Calls) now sit together on the left and read as one uniform row of white buttons with weight-600 ink text, a clearly visible #c9cfd8 border, a soft drop shadow, and slightly larger text. Before, they were white fills with a near-invisible #e6e8ec hairline at weight 500 on the #eef0f3 page (that is the "blend in"), Back to jobs was a transparent ghost at a different size than its .sm neighbors, and the 2026-07-09 comms redesign had split the row with margin-left:auto on View customer portal, pushing it and Messages & Calls to the right edge.

HOW IT WORKS: the toolbar div gained a second class, pec-job-toolbar, and one new CSS block in the crm-light-theme style tag (right after the .pec-btn.sm rule) styles .pec-job-toolbar .pec-btn:not(.primary). Three deliberate mechanics in that selector: (1) :not(.primary) keeps the active Messages & Calls button orange, because without it the new rule ties the .primary rule on specificity and would win by source order, repainting the active state white; (2) the extra classes out-specify the .ghost and .sm rules above, which is what unifies all five buttons including the ghost Back button; (3) the base rule also out-specifies the generic .pec-btn:hover, so the block carries its own :hover (orange border + soft bg, same feedback as before) plus a :disabled rule (opacity .55) so the no-portal-token variant of View customer portal does not read as a clickable bold button. Left alignment is just the two inline margin-left:auto deletions (both the token and disabled branches); .pec-toolbar is already display:flex with no justify-content, so children flow left natively and flex-wrap behaves better without the auto margin. Scoping to pec-job-toolbar means table-row .sm buttons and every other CRM toolbar are untouched; extending the look elsewhere later is one class per toolbar.

ALSO: the stale code comment above the tab containers ("top right, next to View customer portal, per Dylan 2026-07-09") now reflects the left placement, and the 07-09 "messages-calls-inbox-look" What's New entry had its "top right" wording neutralized to "in the toolbar at the top" so a crew member seeing both entries in one popup does not get contradictory directions (changelog content fixes are ordinary commits by design, per the 07-09 22:29 entry; the entry id was not touched, so nobody re-sees an acked popup).

POPUP (decisions 6 + 7): maybeShowWhatsNew() runs fire-and-forget from renderGlobalAuthGate the moment the gate hides, once per page load (token-refresh auth events re-run the gate render but cannot re-pop it). "Got it" upserts one ack row per shown entry (unique admin_user_id + entry_id, duplicates ignored, buttons disabled during the write, so double-clicks and races are moot) and works across devices because the acks are rows, not localStorage. "See all updates in Help" ALSO acks before navigating (judgment call: the entries were shown either way, and re-popping the person who went to read MORE would punish the curious). EVERY failure path (fetch, JSON parse, missing table pre-migration, ack write) degrades silently to no popup; sign-in can never be blocked, per decision 7.

HELP + ASSISTANT (decision 8): the Help tab (the docs view) now opens with a What's New card listing the complete history with dates, ack state irrelevant, filled async from the same JSON with a friendly failure note. The help assistant can answer "what changed" and "how do I use X" questions because its system prompt now carries the flattened entries between the page context and the CRM help doc.

STANDING RULE (decision 1): CLAUDE.md gains rule 9, verbatim from the prompt plus the file path, added AFTER the existing rules so historical rule-number references stay stable: every user-facing change ships with a changelog entry in the same session; internal-only changes do not get entries.

The new tab is the Quo-inbox view Dylan asked for: the customer's texts AND calls in ONE chronological feed (oldest at top, newest at bottom, auto-scrolled to the newest), texts as the same chat bubbles the customer profile shows, calls as inline events with duration, AI summary, next steps, and the transcript behind an expander, plus a composer underneath to text the customer right from the job. A Refresh button reloads the feed; there is deliberately NO background polling, matching every other Quo surface.

WHY CUSTOMER-SCOPED: Quo knows phone numbers, not jobs. pec_call_log has no job_id column and inbound texts log customer_id only, so the feed is the job's CUSTOMER'S full history (exactly what the Quo inbox shows). Texts SENT from this tab do carry the job_id (the server logs it), so job attribution improves going forward for free. kind stays 'manual', which the Last-invoiced column ignores by construction (it counts kind 'invoice' only), so texting from a job can never fake an invoice send.

HOW THE TAB AVOIDS BREAKING THE DETAIL: switching tabs toggles display ONLY, never re-renders, so unsaved Details edits (typed gate codes, estimate lines) and every live handler survive a round trip. The Details wrapper spans the Colors card through the Activity feed; the toolbar and header card stay visible on both tabs. renderAreas/renderBudget/Activity inject by element id and are wrapper-immune. Tab choice persists across the frequent post-save re-renders of the SAME job (state.jobDetailTab + jobDetailTabFor, reset inside the renderer so all 10+ openJobId entry points are covered) and resets to Details when a different job opens. The comms feed mounts LAZILY on first open, so users who never touch the tab pay zero extra queries; a scroll re-assert on switch fixes the hidden-mount case where scrollHeight is 0 under display:none.

REUSE (the drift-proofing): the customer-profile Texts and Calls cards were refactored first (a4fc10d) to expose single-row helpers, smsBubbleHtml and callRowHtml, and both the profile cards and the new tab render through them, so the two surfaces cannot diverge. One deliberate difference, flagged during the design pass: the profile Texts card queries ASCENDING with limit 200, which keeps the OLDEST 200 rows and would silently hide new texts once a thread outgrows the cap; the new tab fetches the NEWEST window (descending, then reversed client-side: 200 texts, 50 calls). The profile card's query was left untouched (out of scope), but it carries that latent cap quirk; worth folding the same newest-window fix into it whenever that card is next touched.

Guardrails: the send is non-idempotent, so the button disables in flight with no blind retry and the server owns the guards (opt-out 409, 50-per-user-per-hour rate limit, 1600-char cap), surfaced verbatim in the toast; opt-out and no-phone banners are copied from the profile card and hide the composer while calls stay visible; per-source degrade (a missing table shows its one-line note, the other source still renders); a job with no linked customers row (manual prod bridges) gets a friendly note instead of an error. node --check passes on all 7 extracted script blocks; em dash scan of added lines = 0; added-line div balance checked (14 opens, 14 closes).
Why: working a job means seeing what the customer said and answering without hopping to the Customers tab; the Quo inbox layout is the model Dylan named.

## [2026-07-09 18:20 MST] Claude Code: prompt 11 shipped, ACH bank payments (async settlement, pending markers, failure alerts)
By: Claude Code
Changed: netlify/functions/pec-stripe-webhook.cjs (rebuilt around event-type routing), pec-public-invoice.cjs, index.html, new migration supabase/migrations/2026-07-09_stripe_pending.sql (NOT applied; Cowork handoff below). Commits e3ecdc4 (migration), 376b5cf (webhook), 7752305 (pay page), 265bc0c (Invoicing chips). Built from claude-code-prompt-11-ach-payments.md in the repo root. Also for the record: prompt 10 was pushed and deployed at the start of this session (4627d11..cc128b8), and one more stale .git/HEAD.lock from Cowork's 18:09 session was removed before committing.

WHY CODE AT ALL (the trap this defuses): enabling ACH is just a Stripe Dashboard toggle because pec-stripe-checkout.cjs never pins payment_method_types (unchanged, per the prompt). But ACH settles in 3 to 5 business days: the checkout session completes with payment_status 'unpaid' and the money arrives later via checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded, an event the old webhook ignored. Flipping the toggle without this deploy would take a customer's money and never record it (no pec_payments row, no commission, job stuck in completed-not-paid). Hence the standing warning, now lifted IN ORDER: deploy, then Cowork's migration, then Dylan flips the toggle.

WEBHOOK (the Quo lesson applied): the old top-level "ignore unless payment_status is paid" guard would have swallowed the async events, so the handler now routes on evt.type FIRST. Four paths: (a) completed + paid is the card path, the recording logic extracted verbatim into recordPayment (idempotent on the PaymentIntent id in reference, deposit auto-flip best-effort, byte-identical behavior); (b) completed + unpaid means ACH initiated, writes ONE idempotent pec_stripe_pending marker row (unique on payment_intent, existence-check then insert with unique-violation tolerated), NO payment row, NO deposit flip; (c) async_payment_succeeded runs recordPayment (received_date = settlement day by construction, since phoenixToday() runs when the event arrives) then flips the marker to succeeded with resolved_at, and a marker-flip failure 500s so Stripe retries the whole delivery, where the reference-key dedupe makes the retry safe; (d) async_payment_failed marks the marker failed (creating it if initiation was never seen) with the bank's reason pulled best-effort off the PaymentIntent (last_payment_error.message, generic fallback), then alerts Slack #epoxysales (SLACK_OFFICE_WEBHOOK) and emails Dylan (OFFICE_NOTIFY_EMAIL env, default dnordby50@gmail.com) via the Resend brand-sender pattern from pec-invoice-intent.cjs; both channels are best-effort and can never fail the webhook response, and alerts fire ONLY on the pending-to-failed transition so a Stripe retry cannot double-ping. Everything else still 200s ignored; genuine DB failures on any recording path still 500 so Stripe retries, and every write is idempotent under those retries.

MARKER TABLE (trust model mirrors pec_call_log): pec_stripe_pending has a staff SELECT policy and NO client write policy; only the service-role webhook writes. payment_intent UNIQUE is the idempotency backbone; status is check-constrained to pending/succeeded/failed; resolved_at stamps when the pending state ended (settled or failed). job_id is the public.jobs id, the same key pec_payments uses.

PAY PAGE: the amber "Payment initiated. Bank transfers take 3 to 5 business days to clear." banner renders whenever an unresolved pending row exists for the job, on EVERY visit, not just the ?paid=1 redirect. Judgment call beyond the letter of the prompt: a customer revisiting mid-clearing would otherwise see "Payment due" plus a pay button, which is a double-payment invitation; checking on every render is one cheap best-effort read and the banner names the in-flight amount. Card success keeps the green banner byte-identical. Nudge copy (decision 9): the primary button now reads "Pay $X online" (it was "by card", which would contradict the checkout offering ACH) and the line under the buttons says bank transfer (ACH) carries no card fees. Stripe still presents both methods; nothing is reordered or surcharged.

INVOICING CHIPS: one batched pec_stripe_pending read over the completed-not-paid section's job ids (the Last-invoiced pattern, never per-row). Pending amounts sum into a muted "ACH pending $X" chip under the Balance so nobody chases a customer whose transfer is clearing; failed rows render a red "ACH failed" chip whose lifecycle is the zero-new-UI option: it clears automatically once a later payment lands for the job (pec_job_ar.last_payment_date on/after the failure day), no new buttons anywhere. Missing table pre-migration degrades to no chips and no banner; the page never breaks, so deploy and migration can land in either order.

NOT TOUCHED, per the prompt: pec-stripe-checkout.cjs session params, the in-app Mark Paid / Record payment modal, supabase client config, timedFetch, wedge recovery. The invoice EMAIL nudge line is not a code change: the email body comes from the DB-stored template Dylan edits in Settings, so that is a one-line Dylan item below. node --check passes on all three touched functions and all 7 extracted index.html script blocks; em dash scan of added lines = 0 across all four commits.
Why: ACH is 0.8% capped at $5 versus roughly 2.9% + 30 cents on cards (about $5 versus $320 on a $10k balance), customers had this option under DripJobs, and the async settlement gap was the one thing making the toggle dangerous.
Files touched: netlify/functions/pec-stripe-webhook.cjs, netlify/functions/pec-public-invoice.cjs, index.html, supabase/migrations/2026-07-09_stripe_pending.sql (new), PROJECT-LOG.md.
Next steps: push/deploy (this session pushes after this entry), Cowork applies the migration, Dylan flips the Stripe toggle and runs the live small-amount test.

Run the verify queries at the bottom and capture: table exists, UNIQUE (payment_intent) constraint, RLS on with exactly ONE policy and it is SELECT-only (no client write policy), status check constraint present. (2) After Dylan's live ACH test settles (3 to 5 business days), verify in PROD: exactly one pec_payments row for the test PaymentIntent (method stripe, received_date = the settlement date, reference = the pi_ id), the matching pec_stripe_pending row is status succeeded with resolved_at set, and the commission line for the job's salesperson appears (it derives from the payment row, so confirming the row exists is the core check).
