## [2026-07-09 11:51 MST] Claude Code: prompt 12 shipped, change orders carry scope (new-area COs, materials + labor flow, native signature page)
By: Claude Code
Changed: index.html, netlify.toml, netlify/functions/pec-public-change-order.cjs (new), pec-send-email.cjs, pec-send-sms.cjs, new migration supabase/migrations/2026-07-09_change_orders_scope.sql (NOT applied; Cowork handoff below). Commits 9437cde (prompt file recovered into the repo), ab4ce83 (migration), 297c999 (signature page + send paths), a62933e (UI). Built from claude-code-prompt-12-change-orders.md, which I recovered VERBATIM from Cowork's session transcript because its workspace folder is not reachable from this machine; the file now lives in the repo root, and future numbered prompts should be committed there too so "run prompt N" needs no pasting.

THE SHAPE (why nothing double-counts, the core design decision): an area-mode change order is TWO things written together. (1) A real job_areas row (is_change_order = true, order_index 500+) that carries the production scope: system + sqft + price. Costing derivation, labor budgets, ordering, and crew paperwork read areas, so scope flows with no re-entry. (2) The SAME is_change_order line item + jobs.price bump the simple mode has always written, which remains the invoice's one-line representation (Dylan: customer sees title + price, materials stay internal). The estimate editor FILTERS CO areas on load and the replaced pec_replace_job_areas RPC's delete SPARES them (is_change_order is not true), so an estimate re-save can neither show, drop, nor re-derive them, and saveJob's regeneration keeps producing exactly one line per CO (the preserved line item). Editor areas keep order_index 0..n, CO areas live at 500+, the ranges cannot collide. Finalized jobs never unlock: the CO writes are direct inserts/updates outside saveJob, exactly like today's simple CO.

MODAL (one modal, two modes, both entry points): openChangeOrderModal serves the Invoicing toolbar button (unchanged placement) AND a new "Add change order" button on the job detail Estimate header; both write the same rows so the surfaces cannot drift, and each re-renders itself on save. Scope mode: title, system selector, sqft, price PRE-FILLED from window.computeEstimatePricing, the byte-identical cost-plus-target-GP engine the estimator uses (same settings keys: estimator_target_gp_pct, estimator_default_commission_pct, estimator_price_increment, estimator_charm_threshold, estimator_charm_band, default_labor_hourly_rate), editable, with the suggestion recomputing on system/sqft change until the price is hand-edited. Simple mode: byte-for-byte today's title + amount append. Write order in scope mode: area insert, then the billing write (line + price, rolls the area back if it fails), then the signature row, then the costing materials push; the last two are best-effort with visible toasts, never silent. Pre-migration, scope mode detects the missing column (the CO-count probe 400s) and disables itself with a run-the-migration note while simple mode keeps working exactly like today.

COSTING FLOW (the two-path bridge): jobs still on DERIVED material lines need nothing, the next costing load re-derives from ALL job_areas, CO included (the crmPlanAreas resolver reads them), and labor budgets follow the price bump (labor pct x revenue). Jobs whose prod twin already has SAVED pec_prod_material_lines get the CO area's lines ADDED: the prod twin is resolved the same way costing resolves it (dripjobs_deal_id, else jobNameAddrKey name+address), the CO area's lines derive via computeJobEstimate, and they insert ADDITIVELY with notes 'Change order: <title>' and order_index continuing the estimate range. Deliberately never delete-then-insert: the Eric Harris doubling (prompt 8) lived in the replace path; an append has no interleave to race and the disabled Save button guards the double-click. No prod twin found = visible toast, never a silent drop. The notes marker is what the PEC Order Sheet / work order skills can key on (Cowork handoff below).

SIGNATURE (native, no vendor, decision 11): /co/<token> is a server-rendered, brand-styled, printable change-order document (pec-public-change-order.cjs, mirroring the /pay pattern: UUID bearer token, generic 404, noindex, no client frameworks). Pending state shows typed-name + drawn-canvas signing (vanilla JS); POST /api/co/sign verifies token then writes ONCE (already-signed returns 409, verify-then-write, no blind retry) with timestamp, IP, and user agent via the service role; pec_change_order_signatures has NO anon policy, so the function is the only unauthenticated path in. After signing the page renders with the signature block filled, so printing it IS the signed document. A code comment notes the e-sign-API upgrade path if certified audit trails ever matter. Billing is NOT gated on signing (decision 10): the price hits at save; the badge just tracks pending/signed.

SENDS (decision 13, distinct keys): the Change orders card (Invoicing detail below Line items + job detail under the Estimate header) lists every tokened CO with its pending/signed badge and View / Copy link / Email link / Text link actions. Email goes compose-mode through pec-send-email.cjs with a new sanitized log_template_key ('change_order'); text goes through pec-send-sms.cjs's new change_order kind, which builds the approval link from the CO token server-side (never staff-typed) with the identified-sender + STOP line. Both log under their own keys BECAUSE the Last-invoiced column counts template_key compose/invoice and sms kind invoice; CO sends stay out of that predicate by construction. Opt-out and rate-limit guards inherit from the existing send functions. No auto-send at save (decision 14).

Guardrails respected: supabase client config, timedFetch, wedge recovery, payment paths untouched; the modal uses openModal/#pecModalRoot like its Invoicing sibling; non-idempotent writes (area insert, line+price, signature mint, materials insert) are bounded withFreshWrite with disabled buttons, no blind retries; legacy line-item-only COs keep rendering everywhere they do today (the signature card lists only tokened COs). No em dashes in any added line; node --check passes on every extracted script block and all three touched functions.
Why: a change order was a name and a dollar amount; production, costing, ordering, and the crew learned nothing when scope changed mid-job. Now scope-mode COs price themselves like the estimator, flow to every production surface, and carry a customer-signable document.
Files touched: index.html, netlify.toml, netlify/functions/pec-public-change-order.cjs (new), netlify/functions/pec-send-email.cjs, netlify/functions/pec-send-sms.cjs, supabase/migrations/2026-07-09_change_orders_scope.sql (new), claude-code-prompt-12-change-orders.md (new, recovered), PROJECT-LOG.md.

THE CORRECTION: the 20:46 entry (and my live guidance) said subscribing the three call.* webhook events before deploying was safe because "the endpoint verifies and quietly ignores them." WRONG for one case: the THEN-DEPLOYED webhook classified inbound events with (/received|incoming|message.received/ on the TYPE) OR (/incoming|inbound/ on the DIRECTION), and a call.completed event for an incoming call carries direction 'incoming', so the second clause matched and every incoming CALL logged as a blank inbound TEXT. Since the events went live this morning, 26 blank rows accumulated in pec_sms_log (verified in PROD: 26 empty-body inbound rows, first 07:31 MST, last 21:15 MST; 7 real texts are fine). Dylan's own 21:15 test call overwrote his 21:09 "Test" as his number's newest message, which made the Messages list preview look blank, hence "text not working."

THE FIX: the pushed build routes every call.* event away from the message path before the inbound test runs (they now upsert pec_call_log instead), so the pollution stops the moment Netlify finishes deploying, even before the call-log migration is applied (pre-migration the call events fail softly into the 200-never-retry path and write nothing). Lesson recorded for future me: "the endpoint ignores unknown events" must be verified against EVERY clause of the classifier, not just the event-type match.

## [2026-07-06 20:46 MST] Claude Code: Quo call summaries + transcripts on the customer profile
By: Claude Code
Changed: netlify/functions/pec-webhook-quo.cjs, index.html, new migration supabase/migrations/2026-07-06_quo_call_log.sql (NOT applied; Cowork handoff below). Commit a9db570. Built live during Dylan's Quo webhook setup session (he asked: "can we add the transcripts to the customer profile, so we can see summaries of calls instead of just duration?").

WHAT SHIPPED: Quo (OpenPhone) natively generates AI call summaries and transcripts and fires webhook events when each is ready. The already-verified /api/quo/webhook endpoint now ingests three call events into a new pec_call_log table, and the customer detail page grew a Calls card that shows each call's direction, time, duration, brand, Quo's AI SUMMARY and next steps, with the full transcript behind a collapsed expander. No more "just duration": the substance of the call is on the profile.

HOW IT WORKS (plain English):
1. Events can arrive in ANY order (a summary can beat its call record), so every event UPSERTS by the Quo call id: PATCH what this event knows onto the existing row, else insert a fresh one; each event fills only its own fields so none can blank out another's work, and the unique index on quo_call_id backstops a race between two inserts (the loser re-PATCHes).
2. call.completed carries the base facts (direction, from/to, duration, when); the webhook matches the CUSTOMER side of the call to a customer row using the exact phone-matching logic texts use (normalized E.164 with a 10-digit-tail fallback; extracted into a shared helper so texts and calls attribute identically), and resolves the brand from OUR receiving number via pec_sms_senders. call.summary.completed adds summary + next steps; call.transcript.completed adds the dialogue turns as jsonb.
3. Field extraction is tolerant of payload drift (from/to strings vs a participants array, summary as an array of lines vs one string) and the handler keeps the endpoint's never-retry-forever contract: handled events 200 even on soft failure. Unmatched calls still log with customer_id null so nothing is dropped; they surface on the profile once the customer's phone is corrected.
4. Trust model mirrors pec_sms_log exactly: staff can READ pec_call_log, there is NO client write policy, only the service-role webhook writes. The Calls card degrades to a clear migration note pre-migration and a friendly empty state before the call events are subscribed in Quo.
Guardrails: message + STOP handling in the webhook is behaviorally unchanged (the call path peels off before it; the customer-match and brand lookups were extracted, not altered). No client config, timedFetch, wedge recovery, or payment paths touched. No em dashes; node --check passes on the webhook and every extracted script block.
Why: call context is half the customer relationship and it lived only inside Quo; now the profile shows what was SAID, not just that a call happened.

By: Claude Code

ITEM 3 DIAGNOSIS FIRST (the customer-vanish bug), settled with live read-only PROD queries via the Supabase MCP (it recovered mid-session, with some 502 retries):
- FACT 1: ZERO customers in PROD have archived_at set. Nothing ever archives a customer as a side effect, no webhook or function touches it (grep confirmed), and the customer Delete button has never actually been used. Hypotheses 2 and 3 dead.
- FACT 2: Timothy Gallagher's single job was archived this morning (14:52 UTC) and he is the FIRST customer ever whose every job is archived (verified: exactly one customer in that state). His customer row is alive and un-archived, yet he vanished from the Customers list and its search.
- ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis 1 confirmed by elimination + uniqueness + timing): the Customers list query paired a jobs(count) embed with the embedded filter .is('jobs.archived_at', null). The old comment asserted that filter cannot drop parent rows and cited the Samuel AE Reprographics fix as proof, but Samuel has ANOTHER live job, so the zero-matching-jobs case was never exercised; the assertion shipped untested. Gallagher hit it on day one and disappeared from the list and search, the only doorways to the detail page (which itself queries fine).
- FIX (robust regardless of the deployed PostgREST's embed semantics): the list query now selects customers with NO jobs embed at all, and non-archived job counts come from ONE batched second query over the page's customer ids, counted client-side (no N+1, and the count matches the expand panel's filter exactly). A customer can never again be hidden by embed-filter behavior. Archiving a job never hides the customer.

ITEM 3 UX (archive rework, Dylan's decisions): the job Danger zone is now "Archive job" with copy that names the JOB and says the customer is kept. The old modal literally read "This archives <customer name>", which is exactly the wording that made job-archiving look like customer deletion. The type-DELETE gate is gone (plain confirm modal): archiving is the normal way to record a cancellation, not a rare destructive act, and it stays reversible. CANCELLED TRACKING, my implementation choice per the prompt's latitude: represented purely by archived_at, NO new jobs.status value, because a real status would ripple through deriveJobStatus, runScheduleStatusSync, the pipeline columns, and the status CHECK constraint (Architecture Gotchas), all for a display concern. The Jobs page gets a collapsed "Cancelled / archived jobs" card: exact count for tracking (even past the 100-row render cap), newest first, display-only "Cancelled" badge, per-row RESTORE that clears jobs.archived_at (idempotent, withFreshWriteRetry) and best-effort un-archives the linked pec_prod_jobs row, by dripjobs_deal_id when bridged, else exact name+address via the same jobNameAddrKey normalizer the schedule resolver uses, mirroring the archive side's coverage. Calendar behavior unchanged: archived jobs stay off the schedule. Restores are logged to the activity feed ('restore').

ITEM 1 (Last invoiced column, completed-not-paid section only): derived at render time from the send logs, retroactive, no new column, two batched queries for the section's job ids (never per-row). WHAT COUNTS (predicate read from pec-send-email.cjs + the call sites, per the prompt's warning): an EMAIL counts when the pec_email_log row has this job_id, status not 'failed', and template_key 'compose' OR 'invoice'; the Email-invoice modal sends compose mode (logs 'compose') and is today the ONLY job-attached email path in the app (the only other send call is the template test-send, no job_id), with 'invoice' covering a future stored-template send. An SMS counts when the pec_sms_log row has this job_id, kind 'invoice', direction 'out', status not 'failed'. Most recent of either wins. Cell shows "Jul 2 (4d ago)"; never sent shows a dash. FLAG RULE (in a code comment as required): red when today is more than 2 days past completed_date AND no qualifying send is dated on or after completed_date minus 2 days (a send shortly before completion counts as the invoice); never-sent-and-stale shows a red "never sent" badge, sent-but-stale shows the date in red. FALSE-ALARM GUARD: INVOICE_LOG_LIVE_DATE = '2026-06-15' (dated constant with comment); jobs completed before it show a plain dash and never flag, because there is no send history old enough to judge them. Missing log tables degrade to dashes, the page never breaks.

ITEM 2 (commission basis, verified end to end, PLAIN ENGLISH): every dollar that enters the system becomes commission at the rep's rate, deposits and finals identically. The three money-in paths all write one pec_payments row: the Mark Paid / Record payment modal (a deposit is the same row shape; the checkbox only flips the job's deposit_collected flag afterward), the deposit flow (same modal), and the Stripe checkout webhook (idempotent insert keyed on the payment intent, so a retry never doubles). renderCommission loads ALL payments with NO date gate and turns EVERY row into a line at amount x commission_pct, attributed by the job's salesperson; pending commission carries forward from any date until an admin pays it out, at which point pec_commission_payouts freezes the amount per payment; deleting a payment cascades its payout row so nothing orphans. I found NO path where recorded money fails to produce a commission line, so no fix was needed. One pre-existing edge worth knowing: a salesperson name that does not match a Sales Team row computes at $0 and shows "(no rate)" in the rollup, visible rather than silent. THE REAL FAILURE MODE is money collected but never recorded (Mark Paid not clicked), which produces no payment row and therefore no line; that is a data gap, not a code gap, and it is what the new flags catch: the Sold jobs rollup now marks completed jobs whose recorded payments fall short of the sold price with a muted "completed, remainder not collected/recorded" under the Collected figure, so a light paycheck is explainable at a glance. NO extra badge added to Invoicing (judgment call the prompt asked for): by the data model, a completed job with money outstanding is ALWAYS in the completed-not-paid section, because its balance is price minus recorded payments; that section already is the flag, and the new Last-invoiced column makes it stronger.

Guardrails respected: supabase client config, timedFetch, wedge recovery, and the payment insert paths untouched (item 2 was read-and-verify, and the payment modal's verify-before-retry pattern is exactly as shipped); both modal roots untouched (the archive confirm still uses openModal/#pecModalRoot); the only new writes are idempotent full-value updates (restore) behind explicit clicks. PROD was READ ONLY this session (three diagnostic selects); all mutations remain Cowork's.
Why: a data-integrity-looking bug (vanishing customers) turned out to be a shipped-but-untested query assumption; the archive flow's wording actively taught users the wrong model; invoicing promptness had no visibility; and Dylan wanted certainty the commission basis is all-collected-dollars before payroll trust issues could ever start.

## [2026-07-06 08:07 MST] Claude Code: Job Costing fixes (duplication bug, + Add material, Pending queue, review gate, team members, toasts)
By: Claude Code
Changed: index.html + new migration supabase/migrations/2026-07-06_can_finalize_costing.sql (NOT applied; Cowork handoff below). Five commits, one per fix: 6711bf2 (duplication), 24505d6 (+ Add material), d6c125a (Pending queue), 8f992c6 (review gate + migration), 4ce70c9 (Add team member), 1ecbd8b (toasts + labels). Built from Cowork's claude-code-prompt-8 (scoped in the 07:42 entry below, 12 decisions from Dylan).

B. DUPLICATION (the Eric Harris doubling), diagnosed root cause: the per-INPUT race, hypothesis 3 of Cowork's three. Each Actual Used input guarded only itself, so two quick edits on different derived lines ran persistDerivedLines concurrently, and its delete-then-insert pairs could interleave as del,del,ins,ins, landing every line twice. The pre-write session warm-up (ensureFreshSession, up to 5s) makes that window wide enough to hit with normal tabbing through the Used column. Hypothesis 1 (RLS lets insert but not delete) is ruled out in the repo migrations (pec_prod_material_lines has ONE symmetric FOR ALL policy, 2026-04-28_pm_ordering.sql), though PROD drift is still worth Cowork eyeballing; hypothesis 2 (stale state) cannot double on its own because the delete wipes the whole job first. FIX, defensive on all three fronts per Dylan: (1) per-JOB serialization, every persist chains after the job's previous one and rebuilds its payload at run time so the freshest typed values win and exactly one delete+insert pair is ever in flight; (2) verify-the-delete-landed, after the delete a read confirms zero rows remain for the job and ABORTS LOUDLY before inserting if anything survived (kills the RLS-drift scenario too); (3) the edit handler drains the job's chain before re-rendering so a value typed into another line mid-save is never dropped by the reload. A chained run that finds the lines already real (not derived) is a no-op.

A. + ADD MATERIAL, root cause was module isolation, not load order: openAddMaterialModal reads the CRM module's state.products, but products were only ever loaded by the production module's loadCatalog onto its OWN state object (the two <script type="module"> scopes share nothing except window bridges), so the CRM copy was empty NO MATTER what the user visited first, and the modal always toasted "No catalog products". Fix: loadCostingData publishes the pec_prod_products rows it ALREADY fetches for the estimate onto the CRM state (zero extra queries), plus a direct fallback fetch if the estimate phase is skipped or dies early. The modal works straight from Job Costing now.

C. PENDING QUEUE: the first keystroke on a costing field upserts the pec_prod_job_costing row, and the old filter dropped any job with a costing row, so a partially-costed job was invisible everywhere except search (Anne's report). A job now leaves Pending only when FINALIZED or SUBMITTED for review; a costing row just flips the row badge from "Needs costing" (amber) to "In progress" (blue), with an in-progress count in the card header. One list; never invisible.

D. REVIEW GATE (Anne submits, only Dylan finalizes): Anne's login is role 'admin', so the old isAdmin() gate let her finalize directly and the review queue never filled. New helper canFinalizeCosting(): role admin AND can_finalize_costing not EXPLICITLY false on the user's permissions row. ## [2026-07-02 20:21 MST] Claude Code: Next Day board revenue is now prorated like the calendar + duplicate-customer guard on + Add Job
By: Claude Code
Changed: index.html only, commit 818d863. No migration, no data model change. Built from Cowork's claude-code-prompt-7 (scoped in the 05:43 entry below, 4 decisions from Dylan).

1. PRORATION (renderNextDay + a tiny shared helper): the board used to print each card's FULL contract and sum full contracts once per unique job, so a 4-day $40k job read $40k on a day really worth $10k. Now every dollar figure on the board is the day's prorated slice, computed with the SAME rule as the calendar: contract / total scheduled days. The denominator source is new helper scheduleTotalDaysByJob() (module scope, right above the Next-Day section), which is literally the calendar's old inline loop EXTRACTED: it counts each job's pec_prod_job_schedule_days rows across ALL dates from state.scheduleDays. renderScheduleCalendar now calls the helper instead of its inline loop (a pure refactor, same semantics, its bars/week totals are unchanged), so there is exactly one proration rule in the codebase and the two surfaces cannot drift. On the board: each job card shows the slice (a 1-day job shows its full contract, a 4-day job a quarter per day; estimated-hours suffix kept), the header "Total revenue" sums the slices of the target date's schedule-day rows (a job with two rows on the same date contributes two slices, matching how the calendar counts days) and skips touch-up callbacks exactly like the calendar's weekRevenue does, and the printed run sheet reuses the same values (job lines show the slice, the header date line shows the same prorated total, since both read the one dayRevenue variable). Task cards (shipped 2026-07-01) carry no revenue line and are not in dayRows, so they contribute nothing and the math cannot break on them.

2. DUPLICATE GUARD (openAddJobModal, the Steve Bruns lesson from Cowork's 05:43 merge below): the modal's save handler, new-job path only, now checks state.prodJobs (already archive-filtered in loadProdCore, plus a defensive !archived_at) for rows whose customer_name matches the picked customer's name after trim + lowercase (EXACT match only, no fuzzy). On a match it stops before any insert and shows an inline warning box above the Save button naming each existing job (proposal #, status, install date if set) with a note to use the modal's "Link to an existing job" picker if it is the same job, plus two buttons: "Go back" (dismisses, everything typed is preserved) and "Add anyway" (sets a one-shot override and re-enters the same save path, so all validations re-run and the insert proceeds). No hard block, per Dylan: duplicate names are legitimate for repeat customers. The override re-arms whenever the picked customer changes, and the reschedule path is exempt by definition (it updates the existing row instead of inserting). WHY save-time rather than pick-time: the modal already lists the customer's existing jobs in the link dropdown at pick time; the guard is the backstop for the exact failure that created the Bruns duplicate, someone sailing past that dropdown to "New job", and at save time it can name precisely what they are about to duplicate.

Guardrails respected: no changes to the drag/drop bump logic, the task-card code, deriveJobStatus / runScheduleStatusSync, the supabase client config, timedFetch, or wedge recovery. The only touch outside renderNextDay / openAddJobModal is the sanctioned helper extraction site in renderScheduleCalendar. No em dashes in the new code.
Why: the board's full-contract dollars overstated a production day whenever a multi-day job touched it (Dylan wants the board to read the true value of the day, consistent with the calendar), and the Bruns double-entry showed a manual + Add Job save can silently split one real job's data across two rows.
Testing: extracted every inline script block from index.html and node --check PASSED on all of them; verified zero em dashes in the diff. Live checks (board vs calendar totals, the warning naming proposal 2497356) are post-deploy manual steps (Dylan handoff below).

Pre-migration the whole write would 400 on the unknown column (PostgREST PGRST204 rejects up front, nothing lands), so it retries once without crew_id, meaning the retry is safe even for the non-idempotent insert and the modal never hard-breaks before Cowork applies the migration. New opts for the board entry point: lockDate (prefills AND disables the date input) and onSaved (repaint the board instead of the calendar after save/delete). Also guarded the range math against a null scheduleAnchor, reachable now that the modal can open before the calendar was ever visited.
3. Next Day board (renderNextDay): non-completed tasks for the board's date now render. A task with crew_id + time_slot (and that crew still active) sits in that crew's First/Second/Third cell; everything else sits in the "No slot yet" panel next to unslotted jobs, so a task can never be invisible on its own day (covers pre-migration rows, crew unassigned later, crew deactivated). Cards deliberately MATCH job cards per Dylan's explicit choice (no badge): description on the bold line, crew name or "Crew reminder" on the muted line, no revenue line, and tasks contribute $0 to the day revenue header (that math reads only job rows, untouched). Completed tasks are hidden from board and run sheet but keep their done styling on the calendar.
4. Drag and drop: task cards carry data-task-id (vs data-day-id on job cards) so the drop handler knows which table to write. Dropping a task on a crew slot writes pec_prod_tasks crew_id + time_slot + crew_lead (the crew NAME, so the calendar chip immediately shows the same crew, one source of truth); dropping it on "No slot yet" clears time_slot only, crew stays. All task writes are full-value idempotent updates via withFreshWriteRetry; the original raw-call job path (including its pre-migration time_slot fallback and the crew mirror onto pec_prod_jobs) is byte-for-byte unchanged.
5. BUMP-THE-OCCUPANT as implemented (Dylan's choice over my flag that a careless drop could silently unslot a job the night before install): once a task is involved, a slot holds one card. A landing TASK bumps every occupant, jobs and tasks alike; a landing JOB bumps tasks only (job-on-job stacking is existing workflow and stays). A bump clears time_slot ONLY (crew stays), so the bumped card lands in "No slot yet" instantly and cannot vanish. Every bump raises a named toast ("Moved 'Smith garage' to No slot yet.") with a one-click UNDO that restores every row the drop wrote (moved card + bumped occupants) from an in-memory snapshot; single level, dies with the toast, nothing heavier. Bumps run only from an explicit drop, never from a render or sync. The dropped card lands FIRST, then occupants bump, so the worst mid-sequence failure is a briefly stacked cell, never a lost card (plus an error repaint so partial state is visible truth).
6. "+ Add Task" button on the board header: opens the SAME modal (not a fork) with the date locked to the board's day; save repaints the board. New tasks land in "No slot yet" until dragged onto a crew.
7. Run sheet (nextDayPrintHtml): tasks print inside their crew's First/Second/Third column in the same block format with the meta line reading "Task" instead of a dollar figure (the print-side marker; on-screen cards stay unmarked per Dylan). Unslotted tasks join the "No slot yet" print block; completed tasks never print. NOTE: the empty-slot print placeholder glyph changed from an em dash to a plain hyphen (one character, print-only) to keep the diff compliant with standing rule 6.

HOW THE SYNC WORKS (plain English): a task now carries two crew references on purpose. crew_lead is the name text the calendar chips have always rendered; crew_id is the FK the board needs to place a card in a grid cell. Every write path that changes a task's crew (the modal's crew select, a board drop) writes both together, so the calendar chip and the board cell can never disagree. The bump only clears the slot, never the crew, so a bumped card keeps its crew label in the No-slot panel.

GUARDRAILS RESPECTED: tasks stay fully isolated from deriveJobStatus / runScheduleStatusSync / job status writes (the task path never touches pec_prod_jobs; the bumped-job path touches ONLY the schedule-day time_slot, a strict subset of what the pre-existing clear-slot drop already wrote). Did not touch the supabase client config, timedFetch, wedge recovery, either modal root's lifecycle, or the payment/SMS paths. No non-idempotent write is blind-retried (the insert's pre-migration retry only runs after a definitive schema 400 where nothing landed). No em dashes in the new code.
Why: tasks are sometimes job-related production work (material pickups, warranty visits) that must be built into the crew day; until now they lived only as calendar chips and could not be sequenced on the nightly finalization board or printed on the run sheet.

Verified zero em dashes across the diff and the new migration. Cleared a stale .git/HEAD.lock (zero-byte leftover from 20:57, no git process running) before committing. ## [2026-06-29 MST] Claude Code: Quo (OpenPhone) SMS integration, phase 1 (invoice texting + two-way + estimate stub)
By: Claude Code
Request: Cowork's phase-1 build prompt (claude-code-prompt-5-quo-sms-phase1.md, scoped from the 2026-06-28 Cowork investigation entry above). Goal: staff can text a customer their invoice pay link through Quo, customers can reply, and those conversations live in the dashboard. Estimate texting is stubbed for the future sales flow; the drip engine and DripJobs replacement are explicitly NOT built here.

WHAT SHIPPED (the SMS stack is a parallel, additive mirror of the email stack, not a new pattern):
1. Migration supabase/migrations/2026-06-28_quo_sms.sql (NOT applied by me, Cowork handoff below). Mirrors 2026-05-31_email_platform.sql: pec_sms_senders (brand to Quo-number map, seeded with the two verified live numbers PEC +19288008154 / inbox PNY8vPVPEZ and FTP +19283561243 / inbox PNbl4NYbrM), pec_sms_log (direction in/out, brand, from/to number, customer_id, job_id, body, kind, status, quo_message_id, error_message, sent_by_user), and two consent columns on public.customers (sms_opt_out boolean default false, sms_opt_out_at). RLS lets staff READ the senders + log; there is no client write policy, so only the service-role functions write them (same as pec_email_log). Idempotent.
2. netlify/functions/pec-send-sms.cjs (outbound). JWT-gated via the same getUser pattern as pec-send-email. Resolves the brand sender from pec_sms_senders, resolves the recipient (explicit to_number else the customer's phone, normalized to E.164 with a US default), then a hard COMPLIANCE GUARD: it reads the customer's sms_opt_out and refuses (HTTP 409, nothing sent) if they opted out. kind=invoice builds a short body from the AR row reusing the SAME public_token the email uses ("<business>: Your invoice <#> for <total> is ready. View and pay: <SITE_URL>/pay/<token>. Reply STOP to opt out."). kind=manual sends the staff body verbatim (trim + length cap). kind=estimate is a wired-but-dormant STUB that returns a clear 501 "not enabled yet" until a real estimate token source exists (the seam is commented in the file). 50 sends/user/hour rate limit, every outcome logged.
3. netlify/functions/pec-webhook-quo.cjs (inbound, two-way + STOP), routed at /api/quo/webhook in netlify.toml (mirrors the Stripe + resend routes). Verifies the request with QUO_WEBHOOK_SECRET (accepts either an OpenPhone-style HMAC signature over the raw body OR a shared-secret header, both keyed on the same env var, so whichever Quo's webhook config offers will validate). On an inbound message it matches the sender number to a customer by phone (exact E.164, then a 10-digit-tail fallback re-normalized to avoid false matches), logs a pec_sms_log row (direction in, status received, brand from the receiving number), and handles STOP/UNSUBSCRIBE/CANCEL/END/QUIT (sets sms_opt_out true + timestamp) and START/UNSTOP/YES/RESUME (clears it). It never throws back to Quo: handled events return 200 even on a soft failure so Quo does not retry forever.
4. index.html (UI). A "Text invoice" button on the invoice detail toolbar next to "Email invoice" (kind=invoice, manual send, success/error toast, disabled up front for an opted-out customer or one with no phone, and the server still guards). A per-customer two-way SMS thread on the customer detail page (text-bubble styled history from pec_sms_log, in + out chronological, with a compose box that sends kind=manual; an opt-out customer shows a banner and the compose is hidden). A lightweight unified "Messages" view (new Sales-group nav item, latest text per conversation, click a matched conversation to open the customer and reply). All of it degrades cleanly before the migration is applied (clear "run the migration" notes, never a hard error).

COMPLIANCE APPROACH (plain English): A2P 10DLC is approved on the account, so deliverability is handled by Quo; the code's job is consent. Every outbound text identifies the sender (brand name) and carries a "Reply STOP to opt out" line. STOP is honored two ways: Quo blocks it at the carrier level, AND our webhook flips the customer's sms_opt_out so our own send guard refuses future texts. The send function checks that flag before every send, so a customer who opted out cannot be texted from the invoice button or the thread compose. We log the refusal as a failed row for the audit trail.

PHASING (what was deliberately left unbuilt, with clean seams): no drip/sequence engine, no DripJobs replacement, no automatic-on-event invoice texting (Dylan chose manual send for phase 1), and estimate texting stays a dormant stub. The estimate path is wired end to end (kind accepted, sender + recipient + opt-out all resolved) but returns 501 until the estimator sales flow provides a real estimate link; the exact spot to plug that in is marked with a SEAM comment in pec-send-sms.cjs.

GUARDRAILS RESPECTED: secrets (QUO_API_KEY, QUO_WEBHOOK_SECRET) are referenced only from Netlify env, never client-side. The Quo send is treated like a payment: NON-idempotent, so a timeout is never auto-retried, it surfaces and staff retry, and the log is the dedupe record. Did not touch the two modal roots, the supabase client config, timedFetch / wedge-recovery, the Stripe/payment paths, or the email functions. No em dashes.
Testing: node --check passes on both new .cjs files; extracted every inline <script> from index.html and node --check passed on all of them (including the block with the new SMS code). Live sends, a real inbound reply, and a real STOP are post-deploy manual checks (they need the env vars + the Quo webhook configured first).

## [2026-06-28 MST] Claude Code: crew bonus payout handout sheets (branded print/PDF, one page per crew member)
By: Claude Code
Changed: index.html only. NO migration, NO change to the finalize bonus-ledger write or computeCrewBonus. Commit fba0628.
WHAT IT DOES: from the Bonus Report Payouts tab, an admin marks a set of bonuses paid and then clicks "Print handouts" to get one branded document with a page per crew member, built on the existing invoice/work-order print pattern (pecOpenPrintDoc / pecPrintBrand, no PDF library). Each page shows: a fixed motivational note, the policy line ("you earn 75% of the labor you save versus budget on each job, split by hours"), the person's jobs (most recent first, customer + system type), and for each job the FULL labor-savings math (labor budget, actual labor, labor saved, the 75% crew pool) plus the FULL crew split (every member's hours, share %, and bonus, the recipient highlighted with "(you)"), then hours per job + total and four totals (this-payout labor-savings bonus, hours this payout, total labor saved this payout, bonus paid year-to-date, bonus paid all-time). Page breaks separate people (CSS break-before:page) so Dylan prints once and hands out pages.
PLACEMENT + TRIGGER: after "Mark selected paid" succeeds, the just-paid batch (bonus ids + paid date + payday) is captured into state.lastBonusBatch and a "Print handouts" banner appears at the top of the Payouts tab for exactly that batch. Each payday group in the Payroll report tab also got a "Print handouts" reprint button (cheap nice-to-have, same generator, ids pulled from the already-grouped reportList). Admin only (the generate action is gated on isAdmin()).
NEW CODE (module scope, after renderBonusReport): buildBonusHandoutMemberPage(person, jobCtx, payInfo, breakBefore) renders ONE member's page, and openBonusHandouts(bonusIds, payInfo) loads data, recomputes per-job context, groups by person, and opens the combined document. The single-member function is the Phase 2 seam (see below).
FLAG A (data accuracy, deferred to me): I chose RECOMPUTE-AT-PRINT-TIME with NO migration. Reasoning in plain English: the ledger (pec_prod_job_bonuses) already stores each person's paid amount and hours per job, so the DOLLARS on the sheet come straight from the ledger amount, which is exactly what was paid, the source of truth. The only thing the ledger does not store is the job-level "labor budget" and "actual labor" context. I derive those without a migration: the crew pool for a job = the sum of that job's labor-savings amounts (authoritative), labor saved = pool / 0.75, actual labor is recomputed from the same manual per-member hours and wages that finalize used (computeCrewBonus, called not modified), and labor budget = actual labor + savings, so the four numbers always tie out (budget - actual = savings, pool = 75% of savings = the paid total). I did NOT snapshot at finalize (the other option) because it would touch the sensitive finalize write, needs a migration + Cowork apply, and only helps future jobs while the 19 already-finalized jobs would need recompute anyway. The one tradeoff: the labor-budget / actual-labor CONTEXT lines can drift for a historical job whose hours were edited after finalize (the dollars never drift, they are from the ledger). If Dylan later wants those context lines to be tamper-proof, the upgrade is to add labor_budget + actual_labor columns to pec_prod_job_bonuses and write bonusCalc.laborBudget / bonusCalc.actualLabor alongside the existing finalize insert (additive, would not change amounts), then prefer the snapshot over recompute. I left the code structured so that swap is localized to openBonusHandouts.
FLAG B (sheet total vs the real check): because crew-lead ($50) and one-off bonus rows are excluded (Decision 13: only rows with note='Labor-savings bonus' are included), a person's sheet total can be less than their actual check. The total is labeled "Labor-savings bonus (this payout)" and a line at the bottom says crew-lead pay and any one-off bonuses are paid separately and are not listed, so the paycheck may be higher. The sheet never presents a number that implies it is the whole check.
FLAG C ($0 jobs): within the batch's job set, a person's page also shows jobs they worked but earned $0 on, derived from pec_prod_job_manual_labor (the per-member hours), shown at $0 in their own row and inside the full crew split. NOTE on scope: in practice this case is rare because a job that paid a pool > 0 pays every member who logged hours, and an over-budget job produces no ledger rows and is excluded from the batch by definition; the $0 row appears only when a manual-labor member has no labor-savings row on a batch job. I did NOT pull in unrelated over-budget jobs from outside the batch (out of v1 scope per the prompt). If a job has no manual-labor rows (e.g. once BusyBusy is the hours source), its $0 workers cannot be derived and simply will not appear.
DECISION 14 (unlinked rows): batch labor-savings rows with a null crew_member_id are skipped (no sheet) and listed by snapshot name on a final "Skipped rows" page so Dylan can fix the link and reprint, never silently dropped.
WHY (plain English): when Dylan pays the crew, each person gets a one-page sheet that proves where their money came from, the jobs, the budget-vs-actual labor math, the savings the crew generated, and their share. The point of the bonus program is to reward labor savings, so the sheet makes that visible per person. The dollars match the check (pulled from the paid ledger); the budget/actual context is reconstructed at print time.
Testing: extracted the CRM module and ran node --check (PASS). Confirmed no em dashes in the new code (the two no-value placeholders use "n/a", not a dash) and no literal closing-script sequence inside the generated document strings (pecOpenPrintDoc supplies its own escaped one). Did not touch the modal roots, supabase config, timedFetch/wedge machinery, the finalize bonus-ledger write, or computeCrewBonus. Live print output (a real batch rendering one page per member with correct numbers) is a post-deploy manual check.
Files touched: index.html, PROJECT-LOG.md.
Next steps: Dylan pushes to deploy, then prints a real batch to verify.
Handoff to Cowork: None (no migration was added; Flag A is recompute-only).
Handoff to Dylan: (1) Push to deploy, then on the Bonus Report Payouts tab select a set of pending bonuses, "Mark selected paid", and click "Print handouts" in the banner that appears. Confirm one branded page per crew member with correct per-job math and that the page dollar figures match what you actually paid. You can also reprint a past payday from the Payroll report tab. (2) PHASE 2 (email/text delivery) is intentionally NOT built, it is blocked on prerequisites: (a) pec_prod_crew_members has no email or phone column, so there is nowhere to send to, and (b) there is no SMS provider wired into the stack (only Resend for email and a Slack webhook exist). To unblock Phase 2, decide: add `email` (and `phone`) to crew members and tell me where you will populate them (Settings > a crew editor, or direct in Supabase); for texting, pick an SMS provider (Twilio or similar) or limit Phase 2 to email via the existing Resend path; and confirm you are OK emailing a sheet that shows the full crew split (each person can see co-workers' amounts), since that is what the printed sheet already shows. The handout generator already renders a single member's sheet (buildBonusHandoutMemberPage), so adding individual delivery is wiring, not a rewrite.

## [2026-06-28 MST] Claude Code: always-show the "Submitted for review" section (empty state) + audited the submit flow
By: Claude Code
Changed: index.html only. NO migration, NO logic change to submit/finalize/bonus. Commit 2e1df0f.
TASK 1 (always render the section): in renderJobCosting the "Submitted for review" card (around index.html:17445) was built as `submittedReview.length ? <card> : ''`, so with zero submitted jobs it became an empty string and the card disappeared entirely. Removed that outer gate: the card now ALWAYS renders. The length check moved INSIDE, in two spots: the count chip ("N awaiting finalize") only prints when length > 0 (so it is omitted, not "0 awaiting finalize", at zero), and the body renders either the job rows (length > 0) or a single muted empty-state row "No jobs awaiting review" (length 0). Position is unchanged (Active tab, above Pending, via the existing `${tab === 'active' ? submittedReviewHtml : ''}` at index.html:17591) and it is shown to all roles, always (not role-gated), matching the prior both-roles intent. The Active-count summary suffix (index.html:17565) was left as-is, so it still appends "· N in review" only when there are items (no "· 0 in review"); the always-visible card is the discoverability fix.
TASK 2 (audited the submit-for-review path -- it is sound, no code blocker): traced the full path. (a) Render branch (index.html:16812-16816): a non-admin on a DRAFT job (not finalized, not submitted) gets the `#costingSubmitBtn` "Submit for review" button; an admin on a draft gets Finalize directly (which is exactly why the queue has been empty -- Dylan as admin never creates a submitted job). (b) Handler (index.html:17220-17231): on click it stamps costing_submitted_by then costing_submitted_at via saveJobField, then best-effort-calls the log_costing_submitted RPC in a try/catch (so a missing RPC never blocks submit). (c) saveJobField (index.html:16068-16079) writes to `pec_prod_jobs` (`supabase.from('pec_prod_jobs').update({[field]: value}).eq('id', jobId)`) AND updates the in-memory state.prodJobs row. (d) submittedReview (index.html:17442-17444) filters state.prodJobs for costing_submitted_at set and not finalized, so the just-submitted job matches immediately and the now-always-visible card populates on the next render of Job Costing. Conclusion: nothing in code prevents a submitted job from showing up; the section has been empty only because no non-admin has ever submitted (Cowork's PROD query, 2026-06-28: 75 jobs, 19 finalized, ever_submitted = 0). The backing columns (costing_submitted_at/by) and the log_costing_submitted RPC are confirmed live in PROD (Cowork entries, 2026-06-27), and Cowork's ability to query those columns is consistent with the migration being deployed.
Why (plain English for Dylan): the section was not broken, it was invisible. The old code said "if there are zero jobs to review, draw nothing", and since nobody had ever clicked Submit, there were always zero, so the box never appeared. The fix is "always draw the box; if it is empty, say so". The reason it was always zero is that submitting is the non-admin step (office staff prepares costing and submits, you review and finalize). You finalize directly as an admin, so you skip the submit step entirely and never put a job into that queue. To see it fill up, someone without admin (Anne) has to submit a job. Nothing about the underlying submit/finalize machinery changed.
Testing: extracted the CRM module (index.html 5465-18276) and ran node --check (PASS). Confirmed the card insertion point (Active tab only), that the count suffix stays conditional, and no em dashes in the edited block.

## [2026-06-28 MST] Claude Code: bottom-right Help widget (AI chat, answers-only v1) + CRM help doc
By: Claude Code
Changed: index.html (widget UI + logic) and a new repo doc help/crm-help.md. NO backend change, NO new secret, NO migration. Commit f8e3baf.
Backend decision (Task 1): the existing netlify/functions/sop-chat.js is NOT SOP-specific, it is a generic Anthropic proxy that forwards an arbitrary {system, messages, model, max_tokens} to the Claude API using the server-side ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (the SOP chat and JARVIS already build their own system prompts client-side and POST to it). So the cleanest path was to REUSE it as-is for Help rather than extend it or add a parallel endpoint. The Help-specific system prompt is assembled client-side, same pattern as buildSOPSystemPrompt. Because the key already lives in Netlify and is already used by two features, there is NO new env var and NO secret handoff.
Widget UI (Task 2): added a fixed bottom-right launcher (#pecHelp > .pec-help-fab, a chat-bubble + question-mark FAB in PEC orange) that toggles a slide-in panel (.pec-help-panel: header with title + close, scrolling message list #pecHelpMessages, autosizing textarea #pecHelpInput, send button). z-index 9000 sits BELOW the modal roots / lightbox / auth gate (all 10000+), so a modal or the sign-in gate always covers it (no collision; checked first, nothing else is pinned bottom-right, the voice orb is position:relative inside JARVIS). It degrades gracefully: on any non-OK / non-JSON / network failure it pops the optimistic history entry and shows a friendly "could not reach the help service, try again or ask Dylan" system bubble instead of a broken panel. Mobile (<=720px): panel goes near full-width (calc(100vw - 24px)) so it never clips.
Knowledge wiring (Task 3): buildSystemPrompt() (built lazily on first open, then reused) combines all four sources Dylan asked for. (a) CRM help doc: fetched from /help/crm-help.md at runtime (publish="." serves it statically, so Dylan edits the .md + redeploys to change answers, no rebuild). (b) SOPs: reuses the existing loadSOPs() (sessionStorage-cached) and getAccessibleSOPs(currentEmployee) so staff only get SOPs they may see and the owner gets all, budgeted to 120k chars. (c) Live page context: pageContext() reads window.pecState.view and openJobId so answers are specific to the screen. (d) General fallback: the prompt allows general knowledge when the curated sources do not cover it but pins it to on-topic CRM help and forbids inventing app features. The CRM help doc itself I drafted from reading index.html (every sidebar view + common tasks: find/open a job, job costing submit->review->finalize, invoicing + PDF, scheduling + manual add, ordering, customers, commission/bonus reports, staff management); it is clearly marked FIRST PASS, "human reviewed: NOT YET", for Dylan to correct.
Visibility (Task 4): shown to EVERY signed-in role, not admin-gated. A MutationObserver on #authGate's style reveals the widget only once the gate flips to display:none (signed in + approved); a second observer on body.class + a CSS rule (body.pec-portal-mode #pecHelp{display:none!important}) keep it hidden in customer portal mode. No coupling into the auth module.
Roadmap seams (per Dylan's intent, NOT shipped): v1 is answers-only (no navigation, no data changes). renderAssistantReply() and doSend() carry documented PHASE 2 seams where a future structured "suggested action" (e.g. {action:'navigate',view:'costing'}) could be returned and rendered as a button calling switchView, and phase 3 (the assistant doing tasks) is not blocked by anything here. Nothing phase 2/3 is wired now.
Why: Dylan wants a persistent Help button so he and staff can ask "how do I X" / "where is Y" without interrupting him, and as the app grows.
Testing: extracted the new classic <script> (index.html ~21057-21225) and ran node --check -- PASS. Ran the browser-parse safety check from the boot-hang gotcha: no literal closing-script sequence exists inside the new block (so no module truncation risk). Verified every reused symbol (CONFIG, loadSOPs, getAccessibleSOPs, sopData, currentEmployee) is declared in the earlier classic script (lines 2115-3043, all before the 3916 boundary) so a later classic script can reference them, and window.pecState exists (index.html:5916). No em dashes in the new code or the help doc (the one em dash in the SOP block template was changed to a hyphen). ## [2026-06-28 MST] Claude Code: fixed Daily flow card visibility + verified/hardened Open Cockpit (Part A); nav-reorg plan + mockup (Part B, awaiting approval)
By: Claude Code
Changed: index.html (Part A, committed 60141fa) and a new throwaway mockup.html (Part B, NOT committed, design artifact only). Two reported bugs on the left sidebar `#rdSidebar`, plus a plan for the growing nav.

PART A, bug 1 (Daily flow card cut off) - REAL, fixed. Root cause: the sidebar scrolled as ONE block. `#rdSidebar` (index.html ~771) is a flex column at viewport height, and a prior fix (commit a1f13df, 2026-06-16) gave the WHOLE bar `overflow-y:auto` with the `.rd-promo` card held at the end by `margin-top:auto`. That made the card reachable only by scrolling the sidebar to its very bottom, so a long `#rdSidebarNav` list pushed it below the visible area (the "cut off" symptom). Note: the Cowork scoping entry (2026-06-28, below) said the sidebar had "no scroll/overflow strategy"; that was outdated, the scroll region already existed since 2026-06-16, it just scrolled the wrong thing. Fix: made the sidebar a true 3-band flex column. The logo (`.rd-logo`, +`flex-shrink:0`) is pinned at the top, a NEW middle band `.rd-nav-scroll` (wraps the Menu + Employee nav blocks; `flex:1 1 auto; min-height:0; overflow-y:auto`) is the only thing that scrolls, and the `.rd-promo` Daily flow card (+`flex-shrink:0`) is pinned at the bottom. `#rdSidebar` itself changed from `overflow-y:auto` to `overflow:hidden`. The mobile (<=980px) block resets `.rd-nav-scroll` to `overflow:visible; flex:none` so the stacked layout still flows naturally (the promo card is still `display:none` on mobile, unchanged). The `min-height:0` is the load-bearing line: without it a flex child refuses to shrink below its content height and would push the promo card off-screen again.

PART A, bug 2 (Open Cockpit does nothing) - handler is CORRECTLY WIRED; the real-world cause was bug 1. Trace: `#rdPromoBtn`'s click handler (index.html ~4724) reads the last-used cockpit child from localStorage (default 'command'), finds the matching hidden cockpit tab-btn in `cockpitChildButtons` (collected at ~4509 from the `data-cockpit-child="true"` buttons at index.html:1566-1568), and calls `.click()` on it; that fires the global tab handler (index.html:3812) which activates the `#tab-command` Cockpit section. I replicated this exact wiring in an isolated jsdom test (minimal DOM mirroring the real tab-nav + sections): clicking the promo button moved the active tab-content from `tab-prescott-crm` to `tab-command`, i.e. it WORKS. So the JS is not the failure. The most likely reason Dylan saw "nothing happens" is bug 1: the button sat below the fold, so it was never actually clickable. I could not run the live (Supabase-gated) app from this session to reproduce a handler-level failure, so I did not claim one. I DID harden the handler: it now falls back to a direct `document.querySelector('.tab-nav:not(.employee-nav) .tab-btn[data-tab=...]')` lookup if `cockpitChildButtons` is ever empty, removing the one silent no-op path (`if (targetBtn)`). The Cockpit view itself is intact (sections `#tab-command` / `#tab-execution` / `#tab-jarvis` at index.html:1573/1674/1757, subnav `#rdCockpitSubnav` at ~4482), not removed.

PART B (nav reorg) - PLAN + MOCKUP ONLY, no app code shipped, awaiting Dylan's approval. Inventory of the real nav (`#pecSubnav`, index.html:1916-1944): it ALREADY carries section headers (`.pec-subnav-group`: Overview / Sales / Production / Finance / Admin) that the sidebar clone mechanism (index.html ~4534) already mirrors in as `.rd-crm-group` labels, with ~17 views total (Dashboard, Metrics | Estimator-beta-owner-only, Customers, Jobs, Jobs pipeline | Ordering, Job Schedule, Next Day Schedule | Invoicing, Job Costing, Bonus Report, Commission | Catalog, DripJobs Sync Health, Settings, Help). switchView(v) (index.html:6169) sets state.view and toggles `.active` on the source button; the sidebar mirror stays in sync via the MutationObserver at index.html:4577. Recommendation: COLLAPSIBLE GROUPS (accordion, one bar) over a right-side flyout or a deep tree, because the groups already exist (lowest cost: turn the existing cloned labels into toggles), it stays in one rail with no floating-panel/z-index/Escape machinery (the app has known modal-root gotchas), and the active-state mirror at 4577 keeps working untouched (mirror buttons still exist, just hidden in a collapsed group). The active group auto-expands and a collapsed group holding the active view shows a dot so you never lose your place. ## [2026-06-27 MST] Cowork: fixed prod boot hang ("checking session") - unescaped </script> in a comment truncated the main module
By: Cowork
Symptom: after deploy, the CRM was stuck on the "Checking session…" boot gate (#authGate-checking) and never reached sign-in or the app.
Root cause: index.html line 7676 was a JS comment that literally contained an unescaped closing script tag (the comment text warning that the inner tag must be escaped, ironically was not). The browser HTML parser ends a <script> block at the FIRST literal closing-script sequence it sees, even inside a JS comment or string. So the main CRM module (opens at line 4767) was terminated early at 7676, and everything after it (the auth boot, renderGlobalAuthGate, setAuthGateState, every render function) never loaded. With renderGlobalAuthGate undefined, the gate never advanced past "checking", so boot hung for every user. node --check passed for Claude Code because extracting the module by the same naive close-tag scan also truncated it at 7676, hiding the downstream code; the bug only manifests in a real browser parse.
Origin: introduced in commit e9ff79d (2026-06-26, Download PDF feature), latent until this deploy. NOT caused by the submit-for-review work (6a40c26) or the migration; those changes live inside render functions that run only after boot.
Fix: reworded the comment so it no longer contains a literal closing-script sequence (replaced the literal tag with the words "closing script tag"; the intended <\/script> example stays escaped). One-line, zero behavior change.
Verified: scanned index.html the way the browser parses (split on the first literal close-tag after each module open) and node --check'd each block. After the fix the main module spans its full 4767-18104 and parses OK; modules at 3910-4363 and 18252-20879 also OK. (A reported failure at 4709-4757 is a scanner false positive: line 4709 contains the tag text inside a comment, which the browser does not treat as a tag.)
Files touched: index.html, PROJECT-LOG.md.
Commit: see below.
Next steps: Dylan must deploy this fix (push to Netlify) to restore prod. Recommend grepping for any other unescaped closing-script sequences inside the modules as a follow-up hardening (Claude Code).
Handoff to Cowork: None.
Handoff to Dylan: push/deploy immediately to restore the CRM. After deploy, hard-refresh (cache may hold the broken bundle) and confirm the app loads past "Checking session". Then resume the submit-for-review role checks.

## [2026-06-25 12:00] Claude Code: browser Back/Forward now walks CRM views (History API integration)
By: Claude Code
Changed: Fixed the browser Back button leaving the CRM to the old website URL. index.html only, NO migration.
Root cause: the SPA never recorded browser history on view changes. switchView() only mutated state.view and re-rendered; it never called history.pushState. So the back stack still held only the page that loaded the app (often the old hq-prescott domain that 301s to prescottepoxy), and Back exited the CRM entirely instead of stepping to the previous in-app view.
Fix (all in the first CRM <script type="module">, near switchView):
  - New history helpers: pecNavTuple() (view + openJobId + openInvoiceJobId + openCustomerId + openUnifiedJobId), pecNavKey(), and pecSyncHistory(). pecSyncHistory records the current tuple in browser history: the FIRST call uses history.replaceState (establishes a base CRM entry over the loader-page entry), and later calls history.pushState ONLY when the tuple key actually changed (so a plain re-render -- filter / pagination / save -- never stacks a duplicate). It no-ops during a popstate restore and when body.pec-portal-mode is set.
  - switchView(v): calls pecSyncHistory() right after `state.view = v` (open-ids are set by the caller before switchView), so every view-level navigation is recorded, including the ordering/catalog handoff.
  - The four detail-capable list renders (renderCustomers, renderJobs, renderInvoicing, renderJobCosting) call pecSyncHistory() at their top, BEFORE their early-return delegation to the detail render. This captures in-view detail open/back that re-render directly (e.g. invoice back `state.openInvoiceJobId=null; renderInvoicing()`, costing row open `state.openUnifiedJobId=id; renderJobCosting()`) and bypass switchView. The dedup key makes the overlap with switchView's call a no-op.
  - A single window 'popstate' handler reads e.state, restores state.view + the open-ids (clears any not present, or falls back to the default 'dashboard' view when e.state is null so Back never silently leaves the app), sets pecLastNavKey to the restored key, and routes via switchView WITHOUT re-pushing. Guarded by a module-level pecIsPopstate flag (which pecSyncHistory checks) PLUS the dedup key, so there is no push-on-render loop.
  - The customer portal (body.pec-portal-mode, which keeps its existing location.hash + hashchange routing ~17730) is explicitly skipped in both pecSyncHistory and the popstate handler, so portal navigation is untouched.
Behavior: dashboard -> jobs -> a job -> job costing -> a costing detail now pushes 5 history entries; browser Back walks back through those CRM views one at a time (Forward too); deep states (open job / invoice / costing detail) restore correctly. The app only leaves to the external/hq-prescott URL after Back has stepped through every CRM entry down to the base (expected SPA behavior; the base is a replaceState entry so there is always at least one CRM step).
Why: Dylan reported Back jumping out of the CRM to the old hq-prescott URL instead of the previous in-app view.
Testing: extracted the first CRM <script type="module"> (index.html 4754-17868, which contains switchView + the four render functions + the new helpers) and node --check passed. Behavioral pass (the dashboard->jobs->job->costing->detail Back/Forward walk; no infinite re-render loop; portal hash routing unaffected) is a post-deploy manual check.

CHANGE 4 - fixed the broken search. The old costSearch only toggled the hidden flag on already-rendered rows, so off-list jobs (e.g. completed "Dave Mancini") were unfindable. Replaced it with a debounced (250ms, reusing the `debounce` helper) type-ahead over ALL `state.prodJobs` (excluding archived), case-insensitive substring on customer_name + address + proposal_number, regardless of the active tab or status filter. Results render in a dropdown; clicking one opens that job's costing detail. Mirrors the global top-search bar. Uses mousedown (not click) on results so the selection fires before the input's blur hides the dropdown.

CHANGE 5 - "+ Add material" ad hoc on the costing detail (commit 0e5ae8b). A button on the Materials card opens a modal (openAddMaterialModal, via openModal/#pecModalRoot) to pick ONE active catalog product + quantity, with Unit $ prefilled from the product's unit_cost (editable). On save it inserts a pec_prod_material_lines row { product_id, product_name, material_type, supplier, color, qty_needed=order_qty=qty, unit_cost_snapshot=the unit cost, line_cost=unit*qty, actual_used_qty=qty, high order_index }, so it counts toward Materials Used + Total Var. SAFETY: if the job's lines are still estimate-DERIVED (no DB rows), persistDerivedLines materializes them FIRST (otherwise inserting one real line makes loadCostingData see "saved lines exist" and stop re-deriving, hiding the estimate lines); the insert uses withFreshWrite (non-idempotent, no auto-retry) with the Add button disabled to block a double-submit, then sets window.pecCostingStale and re-renders. Ad-hoc lines are marked with an order_index >= 9000 sentinel (the only persisted, reloaded column available with no migration); it sorts them last and gates an "added" tag + a Delete button (delete-by-id via withFreshWriteRetry). CAVEAT (existing, accepted): like entering an Actual Used qty today, adding an ad-hoc line permanently materializes the estimate set into real rows, so the job stops auto-deriving from the estimate afterward.

Swapped the read-only Revenue div for `moneyInput('Revenue','revenue','job',job.revenue)`; the existing [data-cost] handler routes data-table='job' -> saveJobField (persists pec_prod_jobs.revenue) and refreshUnifiedTotals recomputes GP / Total Var live. Every other former grid field (equipment_rental_cost, salary_wages_cost, subcontractor_cost, commission_cost, misc_cost, misc_text, notes, actual_hours, sales_team, callback) was already editable on the detail.
Why: Dylan wanted all costing on the per-job detail, the hard-to-use wide grid gone, one merged Job Costing nav with an Active/Completed toggle, the rollups on the Completed side, a search that finds ANY job, and the ability to record a product used on a job but never estimated.

## [2026-06-23 22:30] Claude Code: alphabetize Basecoats + relabel image field + fix false product duplicate-key error
By: Claude Code
Changed: Three small catalog changes, all in index.html, NO migration (Cowork already verified the DB constraint and that the name does not exist).

CHANGE 1 (alphabetize Basecoats). In renderProducts (index.html ~19815) the product sections are grouped by material_type, each sorted by (color || name) then name. For the 'Basecoat' group ONLY it now sorts strictly by product NAME A-Z (case-insensitive localeCompare with sensitivity:'base'); every other section keeps its color-then-name sort. Because this is a render-time sort, basecoats added later always land in alphabetical position automatically.

CHANGE 2 (relabel image field). In the New/Edit product modal (~19960) the field label changed from "Chip image URL" to "Product image URL"; the "(paste a URL; uploads coming later)" helper note is unchanged.

CHANGE 3 (fix false "duplicate key" on add). Root cause (verified live by Cowork against PROD): pec_prod_products_name_uq is a plain UNIQUE index on (name); there was no existing 'Clear 1100 SL Epoxy' row and a single insert succeeds. The error was a CLIENT-side non-idempotent retry: pmSave (~19986) raced the insert against a 20s timeout (Promise.race) and, on timeout, re-enabled the button for a blind retry while the original insert could still land server-side; the manual retry then collided with the now-existing row (the exact trap CLAUDE.md flags for payments). Fix in pmSave:
  - Recover-verify instead of blind retry. On a timeout OR any ambiguous (non-duplicate) failure of an INSERT, before re-enabling, it re-queries pec_prod_products by the exact trimmed name (bounded by its own 10s race so a hung verify can't freeze the modal). If the row landed, it treats the save as SUCCEEDED: close the modal and run the existing loadCatalog()+render() refresh, no error shown. Only if no row exists does it re-enable; the timeout message now says "may not have gone through, so check the list before trying again" rather than inviting a blind retry. The UPDATE path (existing product) stays as-is (idempotent).
  - Friendly genuine-duplicate handling. When a name truly collides (Postgres 23505 / constraint pec_prod_products_name_uq, on insert OR a rename-update), the inline error now reads 'A product named "<name>" already exists.' next to an "Open existing product" button that finds the row in state.products by case-insensitive trimmed name (state.products includes inactive rows) and opens it via openProductModal(id); if it is somehow not in state.products it runs loadCatalog() first, then opens.
  - Kept the button-disable-on-click guard and the post-close loadCatalog()+render() chain (refactored into a shared refreshAfterSave() used by the success and recovered-insert paths).
Why: Dylan wanted basecoats always alphabetized, the field labeled for products generally (not just chips), and the spurious duplicate-key error gone so a new product saves on one click without ever creating a second row.
Testing: extracted the production <script type="module"> (index.html 17990-20587, which contains all three edits) and node --check passed. Behavioral pass (one-click add of a new name; a slow-but-landed insert closes cleanly with no duplicate error and no second row; a truly-existing name shows the friendly message + working "Open existing product") is a post-deploy manual check.

## [2026-06-23 11:00] Claude Code: schedule revenue proration fix + holidays + crew days off + job schedule history
By: Claude Code
Changed: Four schedule changes, all in index.html plus one new migration.

PART 1 (bug) - calendar bar revenue now reconciles and never double-counts across weeks.
  Root cause confirmed in code: the sidebar week total (`weekRevenue`, index.html ~13560) already prorated correctly (`rev * daysInWeek / totalDays`), but the per-bar label came from `eventFor -> revLabel` (~13535) using the job's FULL `revenue`, ignoring how many of the job's days fell in the week. So a $13k 2-day job printed $13k on its bar even though both the sidebar and a 2-week split treated it differently, and a job spanning two weeks printed its full revenue label in BOTH weeks. The week run sheet (~13705) had the same issue with `revFull`.
  Fix: `eventFor` now exposes `revPerDay = revenue / totalScheduledDays` (denominator = count of pec_prod_job_schedule_days rows for the job, precomputed once as `totalDaysByJob`). `barHtml` prints `revPerDay * bar.spanCols` (a bar's span equals the number of contiguous scheduled days it covers), so summing every bar in a week equals the sidebar `weekRevenue` by construction. The run sheet (one card per scheduled day) shows one day's slice (`revPerDay`) with an "of $X total" note for multi-day jobs. Tooltips now show "... · Contract $12,809 · this week $X,XXX" so the prorated bar and the tooltip do not look contradictory. Compact format ($12.5k / $850) kept.
  Reconciliation: this session has no PROD auth (the pec_prod_* tables are RLS-gated to authenticated admin staff via is_admin_staff(), and the browser anon key returns nothing unauthenticated), so I could not pull the literal week-of-Jul-13 rows to reprint the $45,734. Instead the acceptance invariant is proven algebraically and by a run simulation that replicates the exact bar run-splitting + weekRevenue math (including a 2-week job and a NON-CONTIGUOUS job that renders as two bars in one week, the case that would double-count if prorated per-week instead of per-bar-span): sum of bar labels == sidebar weekRevenue EXACTLY (callbacks contribute $0). Because the sidebar $45,734 was already correct (it used the prorated math), the fixed bar labels now sum to that same $45,734 within compact-format rounding. The sidebar math itself was NOT wrong, so `weekRevenue` was left unchanged. If Dylan wants the literal per-job pull printed, that is a quick Cowork verification (listed below, optional).

PART 2 (feature) - company holidays (hard block).
  New "+ Holiday" button on the schedule toolbar (both Week and 3-week views) opens a modal to add a holiday date or range (+ optional name) and delete existing ones. Holidays render as a distinct RED full-day block in both the 3-week grid (tints the whole day column) and the week run sheet. Hard stop: any job write onto a holiday date is blocked BEFORE the write in both the Add Job flow (`openAddJobModal` save) and the scheduler (`openScheduleModal` save), with the message "<date> is a company holiday (<name>), pick another day." A single `holidayOn(iso)` helper is the source of truth for both the render and the block.

PART 3 (feature) - individual crew-member days off (informational).
  New "+ Day Off" button + modal to mark a specific active crew MEMBER off for a day/range (+ optional reason) and delete entries. Renders as a distinct AMBER per-day marker (member name) in both views. ASSUMPTION FLAGGED FOR DYLAN: jobs are scheduled to CREWS, not individual members, so a day off is informational/visual only and does NOT block or warn on scheduling. If you want days off to warn or block, that is a follow-up.

PART 4 (feature) - job schedule history.
  The unified job page (renderUnifiedJob) already had a "Schedule" section; it now reads "Scheduled days", lists EVERY scheduled day sorted ascending including past dates (no filter), and gained a Slot column (time_slot via slotLabel) alongside crew/lead/notes. Read-only.

## [2026-06-22 15:30] Claude Code: Stripe — customers pay invoices online from the /pay link
By: Claude Code
Changed: Added online card payment to the public invoice page via Stripe Checkout (hosted; keeps PEC out of PCI scope). Decisions locked with Dylan: first cut = pay from the invoice link; PEC ABSORBS the processing fee (charge the exact balance, no surcharge); customer can pay the full balance, or the deposit if one is due (no custom amount). Three pieces, no npm deps (Stripe REST + node:crypto, matching every other function):
  1) netlify/functions/pec-stripe-checkout.cjs (new) - public, token-gated GET that looks up the invoice by public_token (reusing the pec_job_ar lookup), computes the amount SERVER-SIDE (balance, or min(depositOwed, balance) for kind=deposit), creates a Stripe Checkout Session via the REST API (form-encoded, Idempotency-Key on token|kind|amount), and 302-redirects to Stripe. Guards: $0.50 minimum, 503 page if STRIPE_SECRET_KEY missing. job_id + kind ride in session AND payment_intent metadata.
  2) netlify/functions/pec-stripe-webhook.cjs (new) - the ONLY place a payment is recorded. Verifies the Stripe-Signature HMAC (HMAC-SHA256 of `${t}.${rawBody}`, timing-safe, 5-min replay guard) mirroring pec-webhook-resend.cjs's Svix verify. On a paid checkout.session.completed it inserts an idempotent pec_payments row (method='stripe', reference=PaymentIntent id, recorded_by='Stripe'), dedupes by selecting on reference first and treats a unique-violation as already-recorded; then auto-marks deposit_collected when the payment covers the deposit owed (mirrors the in-app rule). Returns 200 on success/ignored/duplicate, 400 on bad signature, 500 only on a real DB failure so Stripe retries into the idempotent insert.
  3) netlify/functions/pec-public-invoice.cjs (edit) - replaced the informational "How to pay / call us + 3% surcharge" card with real "Pay $X by card" (and "Pay deposit $Y" when a deposit is due and smaller than the balance) buttons linking to /api/stripe/checkout; dropped the surcharge text (fee absorbed); kept check + Zelle as secondary; added a green "Payment received - thank you" banner on ?paid=1.
  Plus: netlify.toml redirects /api/stripe/checkout and /api/stripe/webhook (mirror /pay/*); supabase/migrations/2026-06-22_stripe_payment_idempotency.sql adds a partial UNIQUE index on pec_payments(reference) WHERE method='stripe' (hard idempotency guard against concurrent webhook retries; scoped so manual payments' free-text references are unaffected).
Key facts (from exploration): pec_payments.method already allows 'stripe'; the pec_job_ar balance is derived from sum(pec_payments.amount) so a recorded Stripe payment updates the balance with no extra write; functions use no npm packages (so no SDK). No client-side keys; STRIPE_* live only in process.env.
Why: customers currently have to "call to pay by card"; this lets them pay the emailed/texted invoice link instantly, recorded automatically and idempotently.
Testing: node --check passes on all three functions. End-to-end (test card 4242, idempotency resend, deposit reflect, bad-signature 400) is a post-deploy pass once the env vars + Stripe webhook endpoint exist (steps in the plan / handoff). The function gained a separate actualCommissionPct input (the assigned rep's real rate from pec_sales_team_members) that NEVER moves the price and only produces: commissionPayout = actualRate% * price (what the rep is paid), gpVariance = (standardRate - actualRate)% * price (>=0 for sub-standard rates), realizedGp = budgetedGp + gpVariance, and realizedGpPct. The owner at 0% therefore shows the budgeted 6% as +gpVariance of extra realized GP; a 6% rep shows zero variance. The pricing denominator keeps commission: price = (M+F)/(1 - laborFrac - standardCommFrac - gpFrac). Bucket parity with computeCostingRow is preserved: budgeted gpDollars = price - (materials + labor + STANDARD commission + F), the same bucket set costing uses (costing later records ACTUAL commission, and the gap is exactly gpVariance).
Why: Dylan's pricing must not change based on who sells the job; assigning a cheaper rep (the owner at 0%) should show up as extra realized margin, not a different customer price.

The visible left rail (#rdSidebarNav) is a CLONE of the hidden #pecSubnav: a loop (index.html ~4515) mirrors each source button into a .rd-crm-btn, and a MutationObserver (~4558) keeps each mirror's display synced to its source.
